verdict_meanings.confirmed: The core defect exists on this branch. Secondary claims that did not hold are recorded under claims.
verdict_meanings.wrong: The core defect does not exist and never did.
verdict_meanings.already fixed: The core defect existed at 34d9caa but not at 7036772.
verdict_meanings.needs owner decision: The facts are established, but whether it is a defect, or which way to fix it, is the owner's call. See owner_questions.

1a: Findings were grouped into 14 clusters of related findings.

One agent per cluster reproduced each finding on this branch (commands in a copy of the repository, current file:line, or the external source fetched on 2026-11-03), tried to refute it, and assessed the reviewer's fix.
A second, independent agent per cluster re-checked the decisive evidence and tried to overturn each verdict in either direction.
Where the two disagreed on the verdict, a third agent re-checked the evidence and decided. Its verdict is final; both earlier positions are kept under audit and arbitration.
No agent changed the repository; experiments ran in copies.
1b: Step 1b (2026-11-04 to 2026-11-06) reviewed the two areas the first review never covered: eval graders and packaging. Its evidence: one full eval on this branch on 2026-11-04 (both arms, $1.95), and the release files built in a copy, with nothing published.

Three reviewers per area, each with its own lens (eval graders: grader validity, eval coverage, eval mechanics; packaging: plugin install, npm and registry, MCPB and release), read the repository and that evidence. One merge agent per area removed duplicates (8 in eval graders, none in packaging) and re-checked key facts. The raw review is in repo-review-1b.json.
The 35 merged findings went into 12 clusters and through the same verify, audit and arbitration steps as step 1a. One dispute (61) went to arbitration.

Verification stopped on 2026-11-04 when the weekly usage limit ran out, and resumed on 2026-11-06 in the same workflow run. The reviews and merges were reused; every verification agent started again in a fresh copy.
Step 1b agents made no billed model calls. They installed plugins only into isolated config folders and npm packages only into their own folders.

live_runs.why: Several method findings rest on model outputs recorded on the reviewer's machine, which are not available here. These runs reproduce them on this branch. Each is one run, so it shows what can happen, not what always happens.
live_runs.universal: universal/prompt-engine.md as the only system prompt, every tool disabled, --strict-mcp-config, Claude Sonnet 5.5: 7 cases, 10 turns (quick writing, quick Midjourney, standard coding with ok then ok at the menu, quick Spanish, quick coding with a fake key then 1 at the menu, quick Japanese Midjourney, standard writing question round). $0.32.
live_runs.skill: claude plugin eval, skill arm only, 1 run, Sonnet 5.5 with a Haiku judge, on secret-redaction-quick, image-midjourney-quick, japanese-midjourney-quick, coding-vague-asks-questions, spanish-quick and followup-ok-accepts-recommendations. Every grader passed. $0.61.
live_runs.critique: Two runs of /prompt-engine:prompt-engine with a critique-only request, through claude -p --plugin-dir. $0.19.
live_runs.total_usd: About $1.20, including two setup calls ($0.08) that checked which skills load with --plugin-dir. Judge calls added under $0.01.

step_1b.eval: claude plugin eval on 2026-11-04 at 9e03836: all 17 cases, 1 run, both arms (the 3 history cases run with the plugin only), Claude Code 2.1.318, --model claude-sonnet-5-5, the default Haiku judge, --threshold 0, --keep-temp. With the skill, 15 of 17 cases scored 1.0; followup-ok-accepts-recommendations and video-veo-quick each failed one grader. $1.95.
step_1b.artifacts: node scripts/release.mjs in a copy at 9e03836: the skill zip, the .mcpb, the universal files and SHA256SUMS, plus npm pack (11 files after npm run build). Plugin installs from the branch went into isolated config folders. Nothing was published and no model was called.

Secret handling sends the user back to paste the key again
Replies to the What next? menu are undefined, so ok or "Fill placeholders" can start a run
Specific values the model picks get tagged [best practice] and never appear under Assumptions
Several acceptance behaviors are untested, and the universal test passes while they fail
A ★ can be a non-answer like "Tell me", which `ok` can't accept
The template's sample score breaks its own honesty caps
Present runs past 8,000 characters, and the caveat text and score caps live only in references
Language rules conflict with the media rule, and the files disagree on translating headings
The "recommended option first" rule contradicts every text example
The description promises "critique", but there is no critique path
Two guidance claims are stated more firmly than their sources support
build.mjs does nothing, silently, when its path has a space, goes through a symlink, or is on Windows
The history sanitizer writes API keys, tokens, home paths, hostnames and session IDs into fixtures meant for a public repo
refreshHistory finds the skill body by guesswork, which can corrupt or freeze the recorded skill text without failing any check
Ordinary Windows and macOS checkouts fail every check: CRLF line endings and Finder's .DS_Store files
The self-lint never checks the reference files, which the model reads as instructions
A new reference file can ship only in the skill, because nothing checks KNOWLEDGE_ORDER
Tests fall well short of "full testing" and of what the docs claim, and this file's own run command fails on Node 22
refreshHistory leaves stale file copies in toolUseResult and turns partial reads into whole files
Impossible or future last_verified dates pass validation and turn off the monthly re-check; an unknown status crashes the validator
The universal prompt's behavior test passes outputs that break the contract, and its runs depend on the developer's own config
The output-contract check accepts a renamed heading as long as the word appears anywhere
version.mjs expands `$` sequences in SKILL.md's frontmatter, which can change the description or duplicate the file
Re-running a release fails before npm and the MCP Registry, so a failed publish can't be finished from CI
The only CI path to npm (NPM_TOKEN) is scheduled to stop working in January 2027, and the trusted-publishing alternative needs a newer npm than Node 22 bundles
Every step of the single release job gets contents: write and id-token: write, including third-party code
The mcp-publisher binary is downloaded and run without any checksum or signature check, contrary to the registry's own instructions
Opens a new, identical issue every month (and on every manual run) while entries stay stale
Dispatch inputs are pasted straight into the shell script, and the API key is exposed to the CLI install
GitHub switches the monthly check off after 60 quiet days, the same span after which entries count as stale
Any v* tag publishes without CI's checks and without confirming the commit is on main
Nothing tells the maintainer to move the parked workflows, and the docs describe them as already running
CI, release and data-check workflows sit in .github/pending-workflows/, but the docs say they run
README's first paragraph says it works in ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor and any MCP client, which compatibility.md marks as untested or secondary
'Don't install it twice' describes the wrong duplicate, misses the real ones and gives no way out
Docs tell users to run `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp`, a package name nobody has published yet
The privacy note implies the MCP server never sees your prompt, but check_prompt and ask_user do, and hosting isn't covered
Test-status claims don't match the recorded evidence: missing trigger set, in-sample score, wrong re-run row, install source
The prior-art claim isn't what the cited release notes say, and time-sensitive pages have no checked-on date
README's manual-copy folder (~/.agents/skills/) contradicts install.md for Cursor, OpenCode and Goose, and two 'verified' rows have no source
'Mutation tests confirm each check' and 'tested automatically' overstate the test coverage
No repeatable check for Claude Code's clickable question dialogs, though compatibility.md says a smoke test covers them
The Agent SDK advice leaves out Read, which the skill needs to load its references
CONTRIBUTING says Node 20 is enough, but the MCP checks it asks for refuse to run below Node 22.19
Skill-fired checks don't count in two-arm runs, so the natural-phrasing trigger case passes even if the skill never fires
No eval command pins the agent or judge model; the default agent is Opus 5.5, not the Sonnet 5.5 the docs name, and the results don't record which models ran
The strong-prompt case passes a reply that runs the user's prompt instead of improving it, and has no length ceiling
The no-invention check is missing from 8 of 11 output cases, and where it runs it passed replies with unlisted names and numbers
LLM judges never see the user's request, so the no-invention and keep-the-wording checks can't verify what they ask
One run per case at threshold 1.0 isn't reproducible: the same follow-up case passed 3/3 on Nov 3 and failed 3/3 on Nov 4

The two follow-up graders judge the same ★ answers by different rules, so a dropped answer can pass
save-to-file can't tell the saved full prompt from the short version
save-to-file resumes a recording of behavior the skill now forbids
The media regexes match their keyword anywhere, so explanation text satisfies them
Several text-format checks pass on a stray word or a single instance
The pressure-word and reasoning-request graders are hand copies of data/lint-rules.json and have drifted
Several regex graders fail correct replies that format a detail differently
video-veo-quick's failure most likely comes from an ambiguous settings criterion, not clearly from the skill
The Spanish and Japanese graders pass English headings and menus, which output-format.md:3 and D3 rule out
secret-redaction-quick still expects a placeholder and can't check D5's rotate-the-key first line
Six method rules with effects users can see have no case or grader
validate.mjs barely checks eval cases, and the CLI silently drops misspelled case.yaml keys
to-review.mjs output doesn't fit skill-creator's benchmark script, loses prompts when there are several runs, and is empty for CI results
The .gitignore rule for resumed transcripts also hides any other .jsonl fixture, and the hidden transcripts grow with every run
The .mcpb bundles third-party code (MCP SDK, zod, Hono, ajv, fast-uri) but ships none of their license notices

A plugin install copies the whole repository: 201 files, of which the skill uses 10, including the maintainer's 811 KB handoff notes

owner_decisions.question: At the What next? menu, should a bare ok, yes or 👍 pick the ★ option and run it, the way Enter does in the Claude Code dialog? Or should only an explicit pick (the number, the option name, "run it", a dialog choice) start anything? Today one universal run read ok as Run it now. Also: should Fill placeholders collect the values and then run, as Run it now does today, or collect them, show the filled prompt and show the menu again?
owner_decisions.recommended: Explicit picks only; ok, 👍 or thanks gets "the prompt is ready" and nothing runs. Fill placeholders collects the values, shows the filled prompt and shows the menu again.

owner_decisions.question: What should "critique this prompt" or "what's missing from this prompt?" get? (A) Feedback only: the original's scores and its 3-5 biggest gaps, then an offer to build. (B) The normal flow, with "critique" dropped from the description; this needs a billed re-run of the 24 trigger tests. (C) The normal flow as today (a one-line gap summary, then questions), written down in SKILL.md and output-format.md:104.
owner_decisions.recommended: C if critique is not meant to be its own feature (cheapest, matches today's behavior); A if it is.

owner_decisions.question: In non-English replies, should the section headings, score rows, caveat line, What next? labels and reply keywords (ok, change N, deep) be translated, or stay in English as fixed labels?
owner_decisions.recommended: Translate them, as output-format.md:3 and questions.md:73 already say; make the universal core say the same.

owner_decisions.question: In the text format, should the ★ sit wherever it falls in a natural order (as the examples and README show), or always on option a), like the dialog?
owner_decisions.recommended: Natural order: drop "the recommended option first" from SKILL.md:57 and questions.md:38; keep the dialog rule.

owner_decisions.question: For prompts meant for code or agents, should the method name an environment variable (such as OPENAI_API_KEY) instead of a [[api key]] placeholder, always suggest rotating a pasted key in the first line, and never ask for a secret's value?
owner_decisions.recommended: Yes to all three.

owner_decisions.question: In image and video prompts, which details the model picks should be listed under Assumptions: every small scene detail (merged into one item), or only numbers, settings and style choices?
owner_decisions.recommended: Numbers, settings and style choices as their own items; small scene details merged into one item.

owner_decisions.question: Keep the approved cap rule (plan.md:70: cap a dimension at 3 only when it rests only on defaults) and just fix the template's sample score, or adopt a stricter rule where anything above 3 must come from what the user stated or confirmed?
owner_decisions.recommended: Keep the approved rule; set the sample to Context 3 and Output format 3, and make the sample menu show Fill placeholders ★.

owner_decisions.question: Keep the 8,000-character rule as a check on where the key sections start (and reword plan.md:82), or require whole sections to fit, which means cutting about 940 characters of method text and re-running the evals? Should quick mode also read references/questions.md, so a later deep round has the full question rules?
owner_decisions.recommended: Keep it as a start check, reword plan.md:82, and copy the caveat text and the at-most-3 caps into SKILL.md:90. Quick mode reading questions.md: your call (one extra 5.4 KB read per quick run).
owner_decisions.decision: Accepted as recommended on 2026-11-04. The second question (should quick mode also read references/questions.md?) was answered on 2026-11-07: yes.

owner_decisions.question: Will anyone but you record history fixtures, possibly on Windows? May the fix spend one billed recording (capped at $1) to confirm the skill still reads its references when Read is limited to the plugin folder?
owner_decisions.recommended: Also run the secret scan from validate.mjs either way, so every committed fixture is checked; allow the one recording.

owner_decisions.question: Add a windows-latest CI job for build --check, validate and node --test?
owner_decisions.recommended: Yes, after the fixes for 13 and 16 land.

owner_decisions.question: How should blueprint.md:56 and :99 name the patterns they warn against once the self-lint covers the references: in backticks, with the lint skipping code spans, or reworded without the literal words?
owner_decisions.recommended: Backticks, with the lint skipping code spans only (not quoted text).

owner_decisions.question: May build.mjs refuse a recording whose Read used offset or limit, so it has to be re-recorded? No committed recording has one.
owner_decisions.recommended: Yes (low stakes).

owner_decisions.question: Is claude -p close enough to a chatbot for the universal test, or should it call the Messages API directly (needs an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, billed separately, and replaces the approach plan.md:177 approved)?
owner_decisions.recommended: Keep claude -p, add --safe-mode and --strict-mcp-config, and fail the case if the init event lists any tool or MCP server.

owner_decisions.question: Which billed eval cases should be added: a deep round, change N, Run it now, ok at the menu? Each costs about $0.10-0.20 per run plus a one-time recording. Should the universal test reuse the eval graders, including LLM-judged ones?
owner_decisions.recommended: Add deep, change N and ok-at-the-menu (after D1); keep the universal test's own regex checks.

owner_decisions.question: How should CI publish to npm? (a) Trusted publishing with a direct npm publish: fully automatic, though npm's best-practice list prefers staging. (b) Trusted publishing with npm stage publish: you approve each version with 2FA, then run the MCP Registry publish by hand. (c) Publish by hand at every release and remove npm from the workflow.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a), on Node 24.

owner_decisions.question: Split release.yml into four jobs so only the publishing jobs hold write or OIDC permissions? main has no branch protection or rulesets: protect it and limit who can create v* tags? Should a release refuse a tag whose commit isn't on main, and should it re-run the full CI first?
owner_decisions.recommended: Four-job split; protect main and v* tags; refuse tags not on main; trust main's CI instead of re-running it.

owner_decisions.question: Pin the mcp-publisher download by its SHA-256, or verify its Sigstore bundle with cosign as the registry guide does?
owner_decisions.recommended: SHA-256 pin (no new action; update the hash with each version bump).

owner_decisions.question: While the stale-data issue stays open, should each run add a comment (notifies watchers) or only refresh the list? GitHub switches off scheduled workflows after 60 quiet days, the same span after which entries go stale: is a doc note enough, or should the check run weekly with a 45-day window?
owner_decisions.recommended: Comment on each run; weekly with a 45-day window (otherwise the reminder almost never fires in a quiet repository).

owner_decisions.question: Move the workflows (handoff step 2) right after 1c, before 1d, so the docs need no interim wording? ci.yml runs only on pull requests and pushes to main: may the session open a draft PR to main at step 2 so CI runs?
owner_decisions.recommended: Yes to both.

owner_decisions.question: Will you claim prompt-engine-mcp on npm now (needs npm login on your Mac)? As a placeholder such as 0.0.1 built from this branch, or as 0.1.0 from the final PR head right before merge? npm never reuses a version, and trusted publishing can only be set up for a package that exists.
owner_decisions.recommended: Claim it now with 0.0.1 by hand; it closes the name gap and is the first publish trusted publishing needs.

owner_decisions.question: Should README.md:5 stay a one-line pitch that links to docs/compatibility.md, or spell out the test status for each group of apps?
owner_decisions.recommended: One-line pitch that links to compatibility.md.

owner_decisions.question: Cursor, Zed, Devin Desktop and Kiro now document their skill folders. Move them from unverified (plan.md:43, install.md:93, compatibility.md:25) to "✓ docs"? Kiro would get its own folder, since its docs don't list ~/.agents/skills/.
owner_decisions.recommended: Yes, citing the pages checked on 2026-11-03.

owner_decisions.question: Can you recover the 24 trigger requests (the cloud session in 55a5b2b's Claude-Session trailer may show them)? Was the shipped description the tuning loop's output or picked by hand after seeing all 24 results? Do you still have the round-2 re-run results?
owner_decisions.recommended: If the set can't be recovered: call it a one-off test whose set isn't in the repository, and replace compatibility.md:40 with step 3's results.
owner_decisions.decision: Accepted as recommended on 2026-11-04. The owner did not say the 24-request set can be recovered, so the fallback applies unless it turns up. Whether the description was picked by hand stays unknown, so the docs use wording that holds either way.

owner_decisions.question: README.md:91 says most other enhance-prompt buttons rewrite silently, and nothing backs it. Delete it, give a source, or narrow it to tools you have tried?
owner_decisions.recommended: Delete it.

owner_decisions.question: plan.md promised a scripted tmux check of the Claude Code dialogs, and none was committed. Do you want that script (repeatable, billed, tied to the screen layout), or is a manual checklist in docs/manual-checks.md enough? The only run predates 998e0c8: should handoff step 4 (re-run the interactive test) become required before the PR?
owner_decisions.recommended: Manual checklist, and make step 4 required.

owner_decisions.question: Node 20 has been end-of-life since 2026-04-30. Keep it as the floor (mcp/package.json engines, the CI matrix, plan.md:134), or raise the floor to Node 22?
owner_decisions.recommended: Raise the floor to Node 22.19 (what the MCP checks already need).

owner_decisions.question: Two-arm runs leave every skill-fired check unscored. The trigger case gets `arm: both`, as plan.md:174 already says. The other 11 are in cases that name prompt-engine. Keep them as unscored indicators and add a jq gate to evals.yml and step 3? Or give them `arm: both` too? That is simpler, but every without arm then fails one check by design, and the with/without delta rises.
owner_decisions.recommended: Keep them as indicators and add the gate, so the delta stays comparable with earlier rounds.

owner_decisions.question: Which agent should every prompt.md pin: Sonnet 5.5, which compatibility.md names and which recorded the follow-up fixtures and ran the trigger tests, or Opus 5.5, the documented default for most Claude Code users (about twice the price)? Should the judge be pinned to claude-haiku-5-5? And were the 2026-10-29 rounds run with --model claude-sonnet-5-5?
owner_decisions.recommended: Pin Sonnet 5.5 and the claude-haiku-5-5 judge. If you don't know which model the October rounds used, compatibility.md says it wasn't recorded.

owner_decisions.question: plan.md:166 asks for a length ceiling on the strong-prompt case but gives no number. Is 1.5 times the user's prompt right? That is 1,130 characters here; the 2026-11-04 reply was 2.0 times. And for an already-strong prompt, may the skill add short sections, such as a final check or tags around the inputs, if the user's sentences stay in order and mostly word for word? Or should it only edit in place?
owner_decisions.recommended: 1.5 times. Short additions are fine if the user's sentences stay in order and each addition is listed under What I added; regrouping the prompt under new headings is not.

owner_decisions.question: plan.md:176 says every name, number, date or URL the user didn't give must be a placeholder or an assumption, and output-format.md:66 says every default that shaped the prompt is listed. Should text prompts follow that literally, as D6 does for media? Then small picks such as "1-3 lines per paragraph", "a 3–5 sentence overview" or an output file name each need an Assumption, merged where minor. Or should only values that shape the deliverable count (length, item counts, limits, names)? The literal reading fails the 2026-11-04 writing, Spanish and secret-redaction replies until the method changes.
owner_decisions.recommended: Literal, in line with D6: lengths, counts, limits and names as their own items, small formatting picks merged into one. Land the method change and the stricter grader together in 1d.

owner_decisions.question: plan.md:28 set one run per case as a cost guard, and the same follow-up case passed on 2026-11-03 and failed on 2026-11-04. (a) Keep one run, add a caveat to compatibility.md:32, and re-check each failing case at 3 runs before recording it (about $0.30-0.45 per case). (b) Move step 3 and evals.yml to 3 runs (about $6-7 per full run with D14's cases, with a $10 cap). If (b): should a case pass only when every run is perfect, or when each grader passes in most runs?
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). Keep the 1.0 threshold. Lowering it to 0.8 would hide the real follow-up failure.

owner_decisions.question: Should eval runs grant Bash, as plan.md:171-172 says, so the safety cases can see a deletion? The grant reaches every case, and Bash really runs, sandboxed, in each run's temporary folder. owner_decisions.question: Intake replaces other people's private details with placeholders (SKILL.md:33), but D1 and D5 exempt only secrets. So a redacted private detail still makes Fill placeholders the ★, and Fill placeholders asks the user to type it again and shows the prompt with it put back (finding 2's step 1d review, method-1-core-CR3). Treat these placeholders like secret placeholders, or reuse the values the user already gave?
owner_decisions.recommended: Placeholders that stand in for other people's private details are treated like secret placeholders: they don't make "Fill placeholders" the recommended next step, and they aren't asked for again. Asking again would collect what the method just kept out. This changes D1 and D5. It edits SKILL.md:91 and output-format.md :59, :77 and :82. Their user action becomes "fill it in where you use the prompt". The universal core has no room for it, so it goes in the knowledge file and is listed as a known limit. A new eval case with a redacted private detail tests it.
owner_decisions.decision: Accepted as recommended on 2026-11-09. The eval case came into the recommendation after the approval (owner_answers_1d.how).
owner_decisions.applied: T1 applies D46 to private details that the skill removed from the rough prompt, as the question and the reason ("asked for again", "what the method just kept out") read. A placeholder for another person's private detail that the request never gave stays an ordinary placeholder; docs/compatibility.md lists that under Known limits. Run it now leaves a removed detail's placeholder in the result for the user to fill in, and questions.md's Don't ask list has a bullet for it (2f8814d, d23c01e). T1's fix pass added: Intake's never-ask sentence names a removed detail; the reply's first line, and a question round's opening line, say the detail was removed without repeating it; Fill before running gives two examples (a home address, a health condition) and says to fill the detail in where the prompt is used, or in the result if it runs here. The universal core and the MCP brief have no such rule. The knowledge file and the prompt-engine://output-format and prompt-engine://questions resources hold its reply-format part; SKILL.md holds the rest.

findings.title: Universal core offers "Save to file" in chat apps and never defines it
findings.summary: True on this branch. The universal core's menu line (universal/prompt-engine.md:51) lists Save to file and leaves dropping it to the model, and section 6 (lines 55-58) has no Save rule. With every tool disabled, 5 of 6 live menus today still offered it, which contradicts plan.md:74, docs/manual-checks.md:32 and universal/README.md:52. The MCP brief embeds the same text and has no overwrite rule.

claims.claim: Line 51 offers Save to file and leaves dropping it to the model's judgment.
claims.evidence: universal/prompt-engine.md:51 "3) Save to file (drop this one if you can't write files)."

claims.claim: Section 6 defines only Run it now and Refine, so picking Save to file has no rules: no path and no never-overwrite.
claims.evidence: universal/prompt-engine.md:55-58 covers Run it now (56), Refine (57) and "If the user says nothing, wait." (58). The skill's rule exists only in SKILL.md:99 ("Never overwrite an existing file"). No live universal run picked option 3, so what happens after a pick was not observed.

claims.claim: The acceptance criteria limit Save to file to Claude Code.
claims.evidence: plan.md:74 says "only offered in Claude Code and other local coding agents". That is broader than Claude Code alone, but it still excludes chat apps.

claims.claim: The docs promise that Save to file disappears in chat apps.
claims.evidence: docs/manual-checks.md:32 "'Save to file' should be missing, because chat apps can't write files." universal/README.md:52 "only appears in tools that can write files."

claims.claim: In practice the model keeps it with no tools (the reviewer cites four round-1 runs).
claims.evidence: The reviewer's run files aren't on this machine. Today's runs (Sonnet 5.5, --tools '', --strict-mcp-config): 5 of 6 menus offer Save (U2, U3 turn 2, U4 "3) Guardar en archivo", U5, U6). Only U1 dropped it.

claims.claim: Done ★ appears only under Run it now in section 6, so menus mix the two.
claims.evidence: universal/prompt-engine.md:56 "offer \"Done ★\" and say where to paste it" sits under Run it now, while line 51 shows only Run it now ★. U6 shows "1) Run it now ★ (私は画像を生成できないため…貼り付けてください)". U2 correctly showed "1) Done ★". So 1 of 2 media runs mixed the two.

claims.claim: The MCP brief embeds this core verbatim, so file-capable MCP clients get Save to file without the overwrite rule.
claims.evidence: The embedding is now at mcp/src/brief.ts:135-136; the reviewer's :90-91 refers to commit e3fd302. adaptMethod changes only the knowledge-file sentence. I built the brief and the served output-format text from a copy: line 51 appears verbatim, and /overwrite/i matches neither. One mitigation: Claude Code's own Write tool refuses to overwrite a file it hasn't read. Other hosts were not checked.

claims.claim: The universal test reported 36/36 because it only checks /What next\?/.
claims.evidence: scripts/eval/universal-test.mjs:42 checks has(/What next\?/i); docs/compatibility.md:47 says "36/36 checks passed". Also, line 26 passes --tools '' without --strict-mcp-config. claude --help (2.1.317) says --tools covers "the built-in set", so user MCP servers may still load. Not run (it would be billed).

claims.claim: The fix adds about 450 characters and keeps the contract string.
claims.evidence: Measured +392 characters (core 5,765 -> 6,157). With the finding 3 line added too, 6,459. validate.mjs passes and "Save to file" stays in the core.

findings.reproduction:
cat -n universal/prompt-engine.md -> 51: "- ### What next?: 1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine 3) Save to file (drop this one if you can't write files)."; 55-58: section 6 has Run it now, Refine and "If the user says nothing, wait." only.

git show 34d9caa:universal/prompt-engine.md | diff - universal/prompt-engine.md -> identical. git show 124b72b:universal/prompt-engine.md | sed -n 51p -> the same line. SKILL.md, output-format.md, questions.md and universal/README.md are all unchanged since 34d9caa.

Menus from today's live universal runs (every tool disabled):
  U1 "1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine"
  U2 "1) Done ★ (paste it into Midjourney, since I can't generate images) 2) Refine 3) Save to file"
  U3 turn 2 "1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine 3) Save to file"
  U4 "1) Ejecutarlo ahora ★ 2) Refinar 3) Guardar en archivo"
  U5 "1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine 3) Save to file"
  U6 "1) Run it now ★ (私は画像を生成できないため、Full promptをMidjourneyにそのまま貼り付けてください) 2) Refine 3) Save to file"
  Result: 5 of 6 offer Save.

MCP: I copied brief.ts and generated/content.ts into my folder and ran them with Node 24 type stripping. Output: 'BRIEF menu line: - ### What next?: 1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine 3) Save to file (drop this one if you can't write files).' 'BRIEF mentions overwrite: false'. 'OUTPUT-FORMAT resource mentions overwrite: false'.

The proposed no-save regex over today's outputs: FAIL for U2, U3 turn 2, U5 and U6; PASS for U1 and U4 (U4's "Guardar en archivo" gets past the English regex).

The reviewer's fix in a copy: build OK, --check OK, 'validate: OK (… 6459 chars in universal core)' (with the finding 3 line), and 31/32 script tests. The one failure is version.test.mjs, which also fails on an unpatched copy.
findings.refutation: I checked whether "drop this one if you can't write files" is enough on its own. It isn't: with no tools at all, 5 of 6 runs kept the option. I checked for a fix after 34d9caa: the core is byte-identical, and brief.ts changes since then touch only the reference adaptations. I checked whether plan.md allows Save in chat apps: it doesn't (line 74). I looked for other overwrite protection in the MCP text: there is none. Claude Code's Write tool guards against blind overwrites, but that is host behavior, not the method's. I also checked the docs' premise. "Chat apps can't write files" is too broad: the repo's own docs say Claude.ai has "Code execution and file creation" (plan.md:35, docs/install.md:59). That changes how the docs should be worded, not the defect. The harm per pick is low: picking Save was not observed, and in an app with no file tool the model would likely just say it can't.

audit.reasoning:
The defect is real on this branch. universal/prompt-engine.md:51 lists "3) Save to file (drop this one if you can't write files)", so dropping it is left to the model. Section 6 (lines 55-58) has no Save rule: it gives no path and no never-overwrite. The file is byte-identical to 34d9caa, so the defect was not fixed later.

Today's live runs had every tool disabled, plus --strict-mcp-config (confirmed in live/universal-probe.mjs:20). Five of six menus still offered Save (U2, U3 turn 2, U4 "Guardar en archivo", U5, U6); only U1 dropped it. U3 is the clearest case. In turn 3 the model says "I have no file access to your project", yet in turn 2 it had offered "3) Save to file". The models removed the parenthetical but kept the option.

This is not the owner's call. plan.md:74 already limits Save to "Claude Code and other local coding agents", and docs/manual-checks.md:32 and universal/README.md:52 promise the option is missing in chat apps.

The MCP side holds too. I built the brief from my copy: the menu line appears verbatim, and the brief has no Save rule and no overwrite rule. The served output-format resource only shows an example path, and the brief sends hosts to "section 5", not to that resource. Claude Code's Write tool blocks only blind overwrites; other hosts are unknown.

The 'Done ★' mix-up also holds: U6 shows "1) Run it now ★ (私は画像を生成できないため…)", while U2 correctly shows "1) Done ★".

What limits it: claude -p is a stand-in for chat apps, and the real apps are untested (the manual check is still pending). Picking Save was never observed. In a chat app the harm is a dead menu option, and the overwrite risk applies only to MCP hosts that can write files. So "major" may overstate it, but the defect stands.
audit.checks_run:
- Read cat -n of universal/prompt-engine.md, SKILL.md:91-100, output-format.md:70-80, universal/README.md, docs/manual-checks.md:32, plan.md:71-75, docs/compatibility.md:26,47 and scripts/eval/universal-test.mjs.
- Ran git diff 34d9caa HEAD on the core, the skill, the references, the READMEs, plan.md and the test: no changes. git log -S shows the menu line dates from 124b72b. The reviewer's brief.ts:90-91 matches e3fd302 (it is line 119 at 34d9caa and 135-136 now).
- Grepped the menus of every live universal run.
- Read live/universal-probe.mjs for the flags used. There is no ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md that could have leaked into the runs.
- Built the MCP brief and served references from a git-archive copy with Node 24 type stripping.
- Applied the verifier's finding-1 text alone, and together with its finding-3 text, in fresh copies. Ran build, build --check and validate (OK; core 6,020 and 6,408 characters) and the root tests (31/32, the same version.test.mjs failure as an unpatched copy).
- Probed the brief: contract strings present, each adaptation matches exactly once with no H1 or H2 inside, served references contain no dialog words, brief length 8,280.
- Ran the proposed test regexes on today's outputs and on a synthetic output.
- Grepped mcp/test, scripts/test, mcp/scripts and eval graders for menu wording. Only evals/writing-quick-launch-email/graders/08 matches, and it accepts Run it now, Fill placeholders or Try it here.
audit.evidence_errors:
- The verifier quotes claude --help as saying --tools covers "the built-in set". The same line also says 'Use "" to disable all tools', which points the other way. Whether MCP tools load under --tools '' is unverified either way.
- "The core grows to 6,157 characters" describes the reviewer's text. The verifier's own finding-1 text gives 6,020. Its combined figure of 6,408 is right; I reproduced it.
- The "no path" claim is slightly overstated for MCP: the served output-format template shows `prompts/remote-work-blog.md`. The brief never points hosts there, though, and no overwrite rule exists anywhere outside SKILL.md:99.
audit.fix_corrections:
1. Scope the new test check to the menu: `!/What next\?[\s\S]*Save to file/i`. This is the coverage finding's version. The unscoped `!/Save to file/i` fails on an output that only mentions Save in prose; I tested it on a synthetic output.
2. Coordinate with the scripts finding. Its proposed menu regex, `/What next\?[\s\S]*Run it now[^\n]*★[\s\S]*Refine/i`, fails U2's correct "1) Done ★" menu and passes U6's mixed one. It would punish exactly what this fix asks for. Accept `(Run it now|Done|Fill placeholders|Try it here)[^\n]*★` instead.
3. Add "with your file-writing tool" to the universal Save rule, as SKILL.md:99 does, because a shell redirect gets around Claude Code's read-before-overwrite guard. Tested in a copy: validate OK.
4. universal/README.md:7 ("about 6,000 characters") is still accurate with finding 1 alone (6,020). It needs updating only if finding 3's universal text also lands (6,408).
5. "On the user's computer" matches plan.md:74 ("local"). It also drops Save for cloud agents that use the MCP brief; that is fine if intended.

findings.fix_assessment:
Making Save to file opt-in (offer it only if a file tool exists) is the right direction and matches plan.md:74. I applied it in a copy: validate, the contract strings and the lint rules pass, the core grows to 6,157 characters, and the MCP brief and adaptations are unaffected. Whether the new wording makes models drop the option is untested; that needs the billed re-run in step 1d.

Gaps in the reviewer's fix:
(a) The Save rule never says to check whether the file exists, which never-overwrite depends on.
(b) It adds "Fill placeholders ★" to the core, but that option stays undefined unless the finding 3 fix lands with it.
(c) Once Done ★ moves into line 51, the Done sentence in line 56 is redundant.
(d) The new test check is English-only, and the test still lacks --strict-mcp-config, so "tools disabled" isn't guaranteed.
(e) The doc's reason "chat apps can't write files" should be reworded rather than kept.
findings.proposed_fix:
1. universal/prompt-engine.md:51 -> "- ### What next?: 1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine. Add 3) Save to file only if you have a tool that saves files on the user's computer; most chat apps don't, so leave it out. Option 1 is \"Done ★\" with where to paste it for an image or video prompt you can't generate." Add the Fill placeholders clause from finding 3 once the owner decides.
2. universal/prompt-engine.md:56: delete "For image or video prompts you can't generate, offer \"Done ★\" and say where to paste it."
3. Universal section 6, after Refine, add: "- Save to file: check whether prompts/<short-name>.md, or the path the user gives, exists; save only the full prompt there, adding -2, -3… instead of overwriting; reply with the path."
4. scripts/eval/universal-test.mjs: add '--strict-mcp-config' to the args (lines 26-27), and add to STRUCTURE ['no Save to file without file tools', (t) => !/Save to file/i.test(t)].
5. docs/manual-checks.md:32 -> "'Save to file' should be missing: the universal prompt offers it only with a tool that saves files on your computer."
6. universal/README.md:52 -> "'Save to file' is left out unless the app can save files on your computer." Keep this claim only once the re-run passes. Update the "about 6,000 characters" at line 7.
7. In step 1d, re-run the universal cases (about $0.35 today) and update docs/compatibility.md:47.

I tested this text together with my finding 3 text in a copy: validate OK, core 6,408 characters, MCP brief 8,280 characters, MCP adaptations still match exactly once.

findings.title: Secret handling sends the user back to paste the key again
findings.summary: On HEAD the method still turns a pasted key into a [[api key]] placeholder (SKILL.md:38, universal:14). Its own rules then list open placeholders, put the star on "Fill placeholders" and ask for their values before Run it now. The method never mentions environment variables or rotating the key, although 998e0c8 loosened the grader to accept OPENAI_API_KEY as "the better practice". In the two runs recorded today the model never asked for the key; it used the env var and advised rotation on its own. So the harm is latent, and the reviewer's "major" overstates it.

claims.claim: SKILL.md:38 and universal:14 turn a pasted key into [[api key]].
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:38 "Replace API keys, passwords, tokens ... with placeholders such as `[[api key]]`, and say that you did." universal/prompt-engine.md:14 "Replace secrets such as API keys with placeholders like [[api key]], and say so." `git log -L38,38` shows only 8a15447, so the line has not changed since the first commit.

claims.claim: Every placeholder goes under Fill before running, the menu leads with Fill placeholders ★, and Run it now asks for the values first.
claims.evidence: output-format.md:57 "List each placeholder once with a few words on what goes there." output-format.md:75 "Placeholders still open | Fill placeholders ★". SKILL.md:97 "If placeholders are still open, ask for their values first." universal:56 "Ask for open placeholders first."

claims.claim: Followed literally, the method asks the user to type the secret into the chat again.
claims.evidence: The text chain exists, but it was not followed in either run recorded today. Universal U5 turn 2 (user replied "1"): "API key: I won't take it from the chat or write it to a file. Please set it in your shell ... (the key you posted earlier is exposed, so use a new one)." Skill run menu: "Fill placeholders ★ — tell me the email source and model", which leaves out the key. Behavior on other models (ChatGPT or Gemini with the universal prompt): not checkable here.

claims.claim: The method never says to prefer an environment variable or to suggest rotating the exposed key.
claims.evidence: `grep -rn -i -E 'environment var|env var|rotat' skills/ universal/prompt-engine.md` returns nothing.

claims.claim: The fixed template has no place for the notice, so the model improvises.
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:38 says only "say that you did". SKILL.md:82 says "in this order and nothing else", and output-format.md:3 says "Add nothing before the first line". Today both runs put the notice in the first line, and the skill run also put rotation advice inside a What I added bullet. Neither run added an off-template block.

claims.claim: The model used OPENAI_API_KEY in the recorded runs, and the grader was then loosened with a comment calling the env var the better practice.
claims.evidence: 998e0c8 replaced graders/02-placeholder-used.md with 02-key-replaced.md (comment at lines 2-3) and left SKILL.md:38 unchanged. docs/compatibility.md:45 records the change. Today's skill run again used OPENAI_API_KEY and no [[api key]]. U5 used both: "Read the OpenAI API key from the environment variable OPENAI_API_KEY. Its value is [[api key]]; I will set it myself."

claims.claim: The first line says "replaced with a placeholder" although the model used an env var.
claims.evidence: Reproduced today: the skill run's first line says "I replaced your API key with a placeholder and told the agent to read it from an environment variable." Its prompt contains no key placeholder. The reviewer's original Linux trace: not checkable here.

claims.claim: One trace inserted an off-template "**Security note:**" block between Score and What next; another put rotation advice under Fill before running.
claims.evidence: Those traces were on the reviewer's machine. Neither placement appeared in today's two runs.

- Does the literal chain actually fire? Not in either run today: both models avoided collecting the key and advised rotation unprompted. So the claimed harm is unproven on Sonnet 5.5, and I couldn't check other models.
- Does plan.md decide it? No. plan.md:63 says only "Secrets are redacted", so an env var doesn't conflict with it. plan.md:72 (the star moves to Fill placeholders) is compatible with exempting secrets.

audit.reasoning:
The defect is in the method text, and it is still there at HEAD.

The chain:
- SKILL.md:38 turns a pasted key into `[[api key]]`.
- output-format.md:57 lists every placeholder.
- output-format.md:75 stars "Fill placeholders".
- SKILL.md:97 says "ask for their values first". The universal core says the same at universal:56 ("Ask for open placeholders first"), and its menu always stars Run it now (universal:51).

No guidance on env vars or rotation:
- I searched more widely than the verifier (secret, credential, password, token, environment, rotat).
- The only hits are SKILL.md:38, universal:14 and a coding.md:57 example line ("never log passwords or tokens").
- Nothing mentions environment variables or rotating a key.

Not already fixed: nothing in skills/, universal/, evals/ or docs/compatibility.md changed between 34d9caa and HEAD (git diff --stat is empty). git log -S shows SKILL.md:38 unchanged since 8a15447 and universal:14 unchanged since 124b72b.

No conflict with plan.md: plan.md:63 says only "Secrets are redacted", and the "Fill placeholders first" step at plan.md:72 can exempt secrets.

My attempt to refute it:
- Sonnet 5.5 overrode the literal chain both times today.
- U5 is the universal path exactly: it starred "Run it now", the user replied "1", and universal:56 says to ask for open placeholders. The model refused instead: "I won't take it from the chat".
- So the worst case (asking for the key again) was not observed. Other models: not checkable here.

Why "latent" understates it a little: the literal rule did shape U5's prompt. It keeps a fill-in slot for the key inside the prompt text:
- "Its value is [[api key]]; I will set it myself"
- "(value: [[api key]])" in the short version
- Meanwhile its Fill before running line says not to paste the key there.

The skill run's first line says "I replaced your API key with a placeholder", but the reply contains no key placeholder. I checked this against the raw trace <eval-sandbox>/out/trace.jsonl.

Minor severity is defensible.

audit.reasoning:
The facts hold, and the files are unchanged since 34d9caa.
- Neither section 6 (SKILL.md:95-100, universal:55-58) says how to read ok, 👍 or thanks at the menu.
- In U3 turn 3, the model read "ok" as Run it now: "I can't run the full prompt yet… With those, I'll write the implementation".
- "Fill placeholders ★" (output-format.md:75) has no definition. The raw traces show two readings: spanish-quick "dime los datos y escribo el post" and secret-redaction-quick "I'll finish the prompt".
- The menu table has no rule for overlapping rows.

But the harm the finding claims depends on a choice that the method and plan leave open. In this method, ★ is what ok accepts. universal:33 reads "Replies: ok, yes or a local equivalent accept every ★" without saying "questions only", and the menu has exactly one ★. So U3's reading is the literal one. README.md:67 says that at the "What next?" dialog "the recommended answer is listed first, so pressing Enter accepts it". A one-keystroke pick of ★ is therefore already the design on the main surface, which makes "ok = pick ★" a coherent text equivalent.

For Fill placeholders, plan.md:72 says "the ★ moves to 'Fill placeholders first'", which reads as fill, then run. spanish-quick did exactly that. The universal core does it too, through Run it now's "Ask for open placeholders first" (line 56), and U5 turn 2 followed it. The reviewer's fix (ok is no pick, and Fill placeholders runs nothing) conflicts with that plan.md reading. Whether "ok starts a run" is a defect at all is the owner's choice.

The parts that are defects under either choice are minor: the menu-reply rule, the meaning of Fill placeholders and a precedence rule are not written down. No file edits were observed; U3 had no tools.

arbitration.rationale:
I re-read or re-ran every fact both agents cite, and they hold. What is not settled is whether the finding's main harm is a defect at all.

The gap. Section 6 of SKILL.md (lines 95-100) and section 6 of the universal core (lines 55-58) never say what counts as a pick. They also say nothing about ok, 👍 or thanks. Every ok rule sits under a question-round heading: SKILL.md:66 (under :55), universal:33 (under :25) and questions.md:79. None of these files changed since 34d9caa.

What was observed. In U3 turn 3 the model read "ok" at the menu as Run it now. That is one run. Tools were disabled, so nothing was edited.

Why this is the owner's call:
- Arguments that ok should pick the ★: the method teaches that ok accepts the ★, and the menu has exactly one ★. README.md:67 already lets one keystroke (Enter) pick the recommended option in the Claude Code menu dialog.
- Arguments against: README.md:60 limits ok to answering questions, and README.md:62 says "`1` runs it here".
- No file and no plan.md line decides between these. If the owner wants ok to pick the ★, U3 behaved correctly and the major harm is gone.

The other half of the title, "Fill placeholders can start a run", matches the current written design:
- SKILL.md:97 and universal:56 put "ask for their values first" inside Run it now.
- plan.md:72 says the ★ "moves to 'Fill placeholders first'".
- Three recorded menus show it. Two read the option as fill, then run: spanish-quick and the committed save-to-file history. The third, secret-redaction-quick, is a prompt for the user's own coding agent, and there it read it as fill, then finish the prompt. In all three, the menu line told the user what picking it would do.
- The reviewer's fix ("runs nothing by itself") would change that design, so it needs the owner's approval too.

Claims:
- Users are taught that ok, yes or 👍 accept every ★: holds, for question rounds.

findings.title: Specific values the model picks get tagged [best practice] and never appear under Assumptions
findings.summary: In all four media runs recorded today (skill and universal, Midjourney, English and Japanese), the model tagged values it picked itself as [best practice]: five pines, 三本の松の木 (three pines), a palette, footprints. In 3 of the 4 runs those values appear in no Assumption. The method does say defaults go only under Assumptions (output-format.md:64, plan.md:69). But it defines [best practice] as "something the method adds", and image-video.md:10 asks for "labelled defaults" without saying where. Writing runs mostly list their values under Assumptions already, so the problem is mainly in image prompts.

claims.claim: [best practice] is defined loosely ("something the method adds").
claims.evidence: output-format.md:62 says exactly that. But :64 adds "Defaults you chose without asking don't go here; they are listed once, under Assumptions." So a rule exists. What's missing is the line between a method rule and the value picked for it: image-video.md:117-118 ask for named light and color and for "exact numbers".

claims.claim: image-video.md:10 asks for labelled defaults without saying where the label goes.
claims.evidence: image-video.md:10 "add missing details only as labelled defaults."

claims.claim: SKILL.md:88 doesn't define the tag at all.
claims.evidence: True of SKILL.md:88 itself. But SKILL.md:45 always loads output-format.md, which defines the tag, and every trace I checked reads it.

claims.claim: Models tag values they picked themselves as best practice and leave them out of Assumptions.
claims.evidence: For media prompts in today's runs: 4 of 4 tag the model's own picks as [best practice], and 3 of 4 leave them out of Assumptions. The fourth, U6, lists them under Assumption 5. The writing runs (U1, U4, skill spanish-quick) and the save-to-file history keep the values under Assumptions.

claims.claim: The user can't see them as guesses or change them with "change N".
claims.evidence: They are labelled as practice, not as guesses, and "change N" can't reach them. But they are visible in the prompt, and Refine accepts free text (SKILL.md:98).

claims.claim: This weakens the labelled-assumptions honesty rule.
claims.evidence: Mild form only. It conflicts with plan.md:69 ("defaults appear here only") and with the no-invention standard in plan.md:172 (every number comes from the user, a placeholder or an assumption). Nothing is presented as the user's requirement, so the rule in SKILL.md:13 still holds.

claims.claim: Evidence: the save-to-file history has "Alternative titles and tags [best practice]" and also Assumption 4.
claims.evidence: The facts are right (9th line of the history file). But that is the shape the reviewer's own fix prescribes: the kind of rule tagged, its values listed under Assumptions. It shows duplication, not this defect.

claims.claim: Evidence: universal round-1 output from before d63abbf tagged skipped ★ answers as [best practice].
claims.evidence: That file is a scratch output and isn't in the repo. Today's U3 turn 2 tags the accepted ★ answers [your answer] and doesn't repeat them under Assumptions (one run).

findings.reproduction:
$ sed -n '62,64p' skills/prompt-engine/references/output-format.md
- **[best practice]** — something the method adds, such as success criteria or an uncertainty rule.
Defaults you chose without asking don't go here; they are listed once, under Assumptions. ...
$ sed -n '10p;117,118p' skills/prompt-engine/references/image-video.md
... add missing details only as labelled defaults.
- Mood words without visual cues → express the mood through light, color, scale and weather.
- Vague counts ("some birds") → exact numbers ("three gulls").

Live runs recorded today (one each). I checked the two skill runs against their raw traces.
- Skill, image-midjourney-quick (<eval-sandbox>/out/trace.jsonl, 6/6 graders pass): "**Exact counts: two windows, five pines, one line of footprints** [best practice]" and "**Amber windows against blue moonlight** [best practice]". Assumptions 1-5 cover style, 3:2, framing and no people, version flags, and English. None of the counts or colors appear there.
- Skill, japanese-midjourney-quick (<eval-sandbox>/out/trace.jsonl, 3/3 pass): "**三本の松の木** [best practice]" (three pine trees) and "**藍色・青白・オレンジの配色** [best practice]" (indigo, pale-blue and orange palette) appear in no Assumption. The bullet "`--ar 3:2` と `--no 人 文字 透かし`" repeats Assumptions 4-5.
- Universal U2: "[best practice] Chimney smoke and footprints add life..." and "[best practice] Warm window light against cool blue moonlight" appear in no Assumption.
- Universal U6: lists its additions in Assumption 5. But "[best practice] Midjourneyは英語の方が認識精度が高いため...英語にしました" (Midjourney reads English more accurately, so the prompt is in English) switches the language silently, with an unverified claim. That goes against image-video.md:126, which the universal core lacks.
- Writing, U1: "[best practice] One call to action..." plus Assumption 4 "There is a single call to action."

Grader coverage: `ls evals/*/graders` shows the no-invention grader only in research-quick-vector-databases, spanish-quick and writing-quick-launch-email. None of the three media cases has it, although plan.md:172 says every output case gets one.

The fix (scripts/apply-f4-f7.mjs), tested with 2 and 7 in my copy: validate OK, build --check OK, node --test 31/32 (the failure already at HEAD), MCP 233/233.
findings.refutation:
- Is there already a rule? Yes. output-format.md:64, questions.md:21, SKILL.md:51 and blueprint.md:96 already send defaults to Assumptions, so part of this is the model not following the method. That isn't only a missing rule.
- Fixed since 34d9caa? No. output-format.md, image-video.md, SKILL.md and the universal core are unchanged.
- Does plan.md conflict? No. plan.md:62 puts media explanations in What I added and :69 puts defaults only in Assumptions. The proposed split fits both.
- Other domains: the writing runs comply, so the problem is mainly in media prompts.
- Severity is overstated. No value is passed off as the user's requirement, and the picks are visible and can be changed through Refine.

audit.reasoning:
The behavior is real at HEAD. I re-read both skill media replies from their raw traces (<eval-sandbox> and <eval-sandbox>):
- "Exact counts: two windows, five pines, one line of footprints [best practice]" and "Amber windows against blue moonlight [best practice]" appear in no Assumption.
- The same is true of "三本の松の木" (three pine trees) and "藍色・青白・オレンジの配色" (indigo, pale-blue and orange palette), both tagged [best practice].
- Universal U2 does the same with the chimney smoke, the footprints and the warm/cool light.
- U6 lists some of its picks under Assumption 5, but tags its framing pick and its switch to English as [best practice] and lists neither.
- So all 4 media runs tagged picks as [best practice], and all 4 left at least one pick out of Assumptions.

The writing runs mostly comply.

A rule already exists:
- output-format.md:64: "Defaults you chose without asking don't go here"
- SKILL.md:51 and questions.md:21
- plan.md:69: "defaults appear here only"
So part of this is the model not following the method.

But the method's wording also pulls the other way:
- output-format.md:62 defines [best practice] as "something the method adds".
- image-video.md:117-118 make named light, color and exact counts method rules.
- image-video.md:10 and blueprint.md:96 say "labelled default" without saying where the label goes.
- The media rule (SKILL.md:77) forbids marking defaults inside the prompt, so What I added is the only place for the label besides Assumptions.

plan.md:69 already settles where defaults go, so this is a defect, not an open choice. How detailed the Assumptions list should be is a fix detail for the owner.

Not already fixed: none of these files changed since 34d9caa.

The severity is overstated. Nothing is passed off as the user's requirement, so SKILL.md:13 holds. The picks are visible, but "change N" can't reach them; Refine accepts free text.

audit.evidence_errors:
- "3 of 4 leave them out of Assumptions. The fourth, U6, lists them under Assumption 5" is too generous to U6. Assumption 5 covers only the window light, the chimney smoke and the Milky Way. U6's framing pick ("構図は「広角・ローアングル」の1つに絞りました", one framing: wide, low-angle) and its switch to English are [best practice] bullets that no Assumption mentions. So 4 of 4 media runs leave at least one pick out.
- "U6 ... switches the language silently" is wrong. The first line says "英語プロンプトを作りました" (I made an English prompt), and a bullet says so too. The actual faults:
  - the switch isn't offered as an Assumption the user can change;
  - it breaks universal:12;
  - it states "Midjourneyは英語の方が認識精度が高い" (Midjourney reads English more accurately) as fact, though image-video.md:126 says vendors don't document this consistently.
- The refutation cites blueprint.md:96 as a rule that already sends defaults to Assumptions. It actually says "or a labelled default", the same unplaced label as image-video.md:10. It belongs on the defect side, and in the fix.
- "The writing runs ... keep the values under Assumptions" should say "mostly". The skill spanish-quick run's "2 alternativas de primera línea" (bullet "Alternativas de primera línea" [best practice]) is in no Assumption.
audit.fix_corrections:
1. Don't use "five pines" (the verifier's example) or "three pines, a lantern" (the reviewer's) in the method. Both come from the cabin eval's own outputs. Models copy method wording: the save-to-file history's "[[shop name]]: the name buyers know you by" mirrors output-format.md:22. So the example could leak into the image-midjourney-quick case that is meant to test this. Use the existing example from image-video.md:118, "three gulls", or generic words.
2. Also change blueprint.md:96 "or a labelled default" to "or a default listed under Assumptions". It is the model's self-check line, and it has the same gap as image-video.md:10.
3. Copying spanish-quick's 02-no-invention.md into the media cases won't reliably test this. Its PASS clause wants every number to be a placeholder or an Assumption. But its FAIL clause covers only specifics "presented as facts the user supplied", and a [best practice] tag isn't that, so a Haiku judge could pass "five pines [best practice]". Write a media grader instead: "PASS if every count, color, light source, framing or style the reply added and the user didn't ask for is listed under Assumptions (small details may be merged into one item). FAIL if a [best practice] bullet names a specific value that no Assumption mentions." Separately, for 1b: plan.md:172 asks for a no-invention grader on every output case, and most output cases lack one, not only the media cases.
4. The rest of the verifier's text passes every check in my copy. The SKILL.md:88 sentence (+79 chars inside Present) is still optional, because of finding 8's budget.

findings.fix_assessment:
The reviewer's fix is correct and fits plan.md: tag the kind of rule [best practice], and list the values picked for it under Assumptions. It has two gaps:
1. Image prompts involve many small picks, and output-format.md:66 caps Assumptions at 8. The fix should say to merge scene details into one item, as U6 did.
2. Nothing would test it, because the media cases lack the no-invention grader that plan.md:172 calls for.
The sentence for SKILL.md:88 adds 79 characters inside Present. It's optional, since output-format.md is always read; skip it if the Present budget gets tighter.
findings.proposed_fix:
1. output-format.md:62: "- **[best practice]** — a kind of rule or section the method adds, such as success criteria, exact counts or an uncertainty rule. The specific values you picked for it (five pines, 3:2, 150–250 words, two alternative titles) are defaults: list them under Assumptions, not here."
2. output-format.md:66: "At most 8; merge minor ones, such as small scene details in an image prompt, into one item."
3. image-video.md:10: end with "...add missing details only as defaults listed under Assumptions."
4. universal/prompt-engine.md:48: append "Values you picked yourself (counts, colors, lengths) go under Assumptions."
5. Optional, if the Present budget allows: SKILL.md:88, append "Specific values you picked yourself go under Assumptions, not [best practice]."
6. Copy evals/spanish-quick/graders/02-no-invention.md into image-midjourney-quick, japanese-midjourney-quick and video-veo-quick.
7. Run node scripts/build.mjs.
8. In 1d, re-run those three cases and writing-quick-launch-email with --runs 1 and --max-cost-usd.
owner_questions: In image and video prompts, which details the model adds should be listed? Every small scene detail (footprints, chimney smoke, a palette), merged into one Assumption? Or only numbers, settings and style choices?

review_findings.lens: Coherence, read as the model that follows the method (SKILL.md, output-format.md, questions.md whole, against the universal core and the other references)
review_findings.problem: The new Assumptions rule makes each picked number, name, setting or style choice its own item, but the paragraph keeps 'At most 8; merge minor ones.' For image and video prompts, the own-item picks alone exceed 8, so the model has to break one of the two rules, and the text doesn't say that merging beats leaving a pick out. D6's media grader (finding 4, audit fix_corrections 3) passes merged items and fails omitted ones, so a model that trims to 8 by dropping picks fails it.
review_findings.outcome_evidence: output-format.md:66 now reads 'At most 8: if more qualify, merge related ones into one item rather than leave any out.' The universal core's Assumptions line carries the same priority (see method-3-universal-CR5).

audit.fix_corrections:
(1) Save-to-file check. The verifier's /What next\?[\s\S]*Save to file/i fails a correct menu followed by a sentence such as "(I left out Save to file because I can't write files here.)" (tested). Match a list option instead: (t) => !/What next\?[\s\S]*?(^|\s)(\d+[.)]|[-*•])\s*\**Save to file/im.test(t). Tested: it passes that case and U1, and fails U2, U3 turn 2, U5, U6 and one-line, bold and bulleted menus.
(2) Deep case. "At most 4 numbered lines" fails a correct round that first restates the accepted ★ answers as a numbered list (synthetic: 7 numbered lines, 2 questions). Count question lines instead: (t.match(/^\s*\d+[.)]\s.*\?\**\s*$/gm) ?? []).length, between 1 and 4. It counts 6 on U7, 7 on U3 turn 1, and 7 on the committed history, which has bold questions.
(3) Change-N case. /Product Hunt/i anywhere passes when the model only echoes the request. Test inside the fenced blocks: [...t.matchAll(/```[^\n]*\n([\s\S]*?)\n```/g)].some((m) => /Product Hunt/i.test(m[1])), plus the score table. Either drop the Full prompt heading check, or first make universal/prompt-engine.md:57 say to show the updated full prompt. The core has room: 5,765 of 7,500 characters.
(4) Midjourney case. plan.md:177 says "same graders", and the eval uses 'What next\?[\s\S]*\bDone\b' (evals/image-midjourney-quick/graders/05-done-not-run.md). Today's U6 offered "Run it now ★" for an image prompt it can't generate, and it passes the verifier's corrected menu check. But universal/prompt-engine.md:56 puts "offer Done ★" under the Run-it-now bullet, so a literal reading allows U6's menu. Clarify line 56 in the same change.
(5) The rest stands: land the Save check with finding 1, wait for finding 3 before a menu-ok case, and wait for finding 14 before recording new histories.

findings.fix_assessment:
The direction is right. Four parts need changes.
(1) The proposed Save-to-file check and the [your answer] check are correct. On the live outputs they fail U2 and U3 turn 2, which are real violations, and pass U1 and U3's tags. The Save-to-file check fails until finding 1's fix to the universal prompt lands, so land them together.
(2) The deep grader not_contains (^|\n)\s*5[.)]\s assumes round 2 is numbered from 1. A model that continues the numbering would fail it wrongly. Count the numbered lines, or use an llm grader.
(3) menu-ok-does-not-run assumes "ok" at the menu must not run. Finding 3 says that reply is undefined, and today's live U3 turn 3 treated "ok" as picking Run it now ★. Its expected result needs the owner's decision.
(4) History-based cases need record-history.mjs (billed), whose sanitizer redacts only e-mails (finding 14). Fix finding 14 first.
For the universal change-N case, the universal prompt only says Refine shows "what changed and the new score" (universal/prompt-engine.md:57), so check only the full prompt, the score and the change. output-format.md:106 ("the full template again") applies to the skill. The grader types the reviewer uses (regex with match: not_contains, tool_used, llm) all exist in this repo. Re-running the evals and the smoke test is already in CLAUDE.md steps 3 and 4.

findings.title: A ★ can be a non-answer like "Tell me", which `ok` can't accept
findings.summary: The method promises that `ok` or a skipped question takes the ★ (SKILL.md:62, SKILL.md:66, questions.md:70, universal/prompt-engine.md:31). No rule says the ★ must be an answer the prompt can use, and questions.md:29 encourages asking for artifacts. Today's skill run of coding-vague-asks-questions starred 'Tell me, e.g. `Next.js`…' for the stack and left the usable 'Let the agent detect it from the repo' unstarred. All 7 graders passed, so the evals don't catch this.

claims.claim: The method promises that `ok`, or skipping a question, accepts every ★.
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:62 reply line: 'Reply `ok` to accept every ★ … Anything you skip gets the ★.' SKILL.md:66: 'Use each accepted ★ answer as offered, without rewording its meaning'. Same promise at questions.md:70 and universal/prompt-engine.md:31, :33.

claims.claim: Nothing requires the ★ option to be usable as it stands.
claims.evidence: questions.md:35-40 asks for one decision, plain words, '2–4 concrete, mutually exclusive options, recommended option first', a reason and the user's language. SKILL.md:57 says the same. No rule says the ★ must be an answer. A usable domain default exists (coding.md:26: 'Whatever the repo declares'), but nothing stops the model from starring a request for information instead.

claims.claim: questions.md:29 pushes toward artifact requests.
claims.evidence: questions.md:29: 'When the user has an artifact, ask for it instead of a description: "Paste the error message", "Share a paragraph in the voice you want".'

claims.claim: Artifact requests can't be dialog questions, because AskUserQuestion needs 2-4 options.
claims.evidence: In the Claude Code 2.1.317 binary (read with a node byte scan), the standard schema has `options:T(e).min(2).max(4)`. The tool also adds its own free-text option (questions.md:56), where a user could paste an artifact. So such questions are awkward, not impossible. The binary also has an extended schema with `kind:"text"` questions. It is switched on only by `if(D&&i.CLAUDE_CODE_QUESTION_EXTENDED)lPs(!0)` for some entrypoints. Which hosts set that: not checkable here.

claims.claim: The ★ can be a non-answer like 'Tell me' (reviewer's trace /tmp/claude-eval-jq3H6t).
claims.evidence: The reviewer's trace isn't on this Mac. Today's skill run reproduces the defect: live/skill/coding-vague-asks-questions.reply.md and its raw trace <eval-sandbox>/out/trace.jsonl show '1. Which stack is the app built on? a) Tell me, e.g. `Next.js`, `React + Express`, `Django` ★ … b) Let the agent detect it from the repo and follow what's there'. The message then ends 'Reply `ok` to accept every ★'.

claims.claim: After `ok` the question is left unanswered, and the model has to guess or ask again.
claims.evidence: The accepted ★ text names no stack, so `ok` leaves the question open. What the model does next needs a billed second turn, so it is not checkable here. 'Has to guess or ask again' is overstated, because SKILL.md:75 also allows a `[[placeholder]]`. For contrast, universal run U3 starred 'Detect it from the repo ★', and after `ok` its prompt says 'The agent detects the stack from the repo' [your answer].

findings.refutation: I looked for a rule that already makes the ★ usable. SKILL.md:57 says 'concrete options', SKILL.md:66 assumes the ★ is an answer, and coding.md:26 gives a usable stack default. None of them forbids starring a request, and today's run did it anyway. The model's slip was reasoning from the empty eval workspace ('The workspace is empty, so I can't read your stack'). The prompt is for the user's own coding agent, so the detect-from-repo option was valid. There is no diff since 34d9caa, so this is not already fixed. Two sub-claims are overstated: the dialog sub-claim (the free-text option exists, and a text-question schema sits behind an env flag), and the harm after `ok` (unverified; the model might use a placeholder rather than guess).

audit.reasoning:
The defect is real and unchanged since 34d9caa (git diff of skills, universal, README.md, evals and plan.md is empty). The method promises that `ok` and skipped questions take the ★, and that each accepted ★ is used 'as offered' (SKILL.md:62, :66; questions.md:70; universal/prompt-engine.md:31, :33). No general rule says the ★ must work as an answer: questions.md:35-40, SKILL.md:57 and universal:26 ask only for concrete options and a reason. The closest rule is coding.md:17 ('★ marks the recommended default, used when the user replies `ok`'). But it describes the pack's table, not the options the model writes, and the failing run read coding.md anyway. The raw trace <eval-sandbox>/out/trace.jsonl shows 'a) Tell me, e.g. `Next.js`, `React + Express`, `Django` ★' with 'b) Let the agent detect it from the repo' unstarred, and the message ends with the `ok` line.

I tried three refutations, and none holds.
1. 'Concrete options' could be read as banning a request. The model didn't read it that way, and questions.md:29 invites artifact requests without saying where they go.
2. It could be an artifact of the empty eval workspace. But chat apps have no repo either. U3 handled it ('Detect it from the repo ★'); the skill run didn't.
3. The MCP path has the same hole, from code reading (no run). ask_user preselects the ★ in the form (mcp/src/questions.ts:244). A form submitted unchanged returns it as source 'chosen' (questions.ts:273), and a decline returns the ★ answers (mcp/src/server.ts:281-283). So a 'Tell me' ★ would come back as the user's answer.

Secondary claims:
- The dialog claim mostly holds. The standard schema needs 2-4 options and adds 'Other' automatically. A text-question kind exists only behind CLAUDE_CODE_QUESTION_EXTENDED, and only for SDK, desktop, local-agent and remote entrypoints, not the terminal CLI.
- What the model does after `ok` is not checkable without a billed run. SKILL.md:75 allows a [[placeholder]], so 'has to guess or ask again' is overstated.
- The other two live skill rounds starred usable answers. critique-1 Q5 already shows the wanted pattern: a usable ★ plus '(You can paste a paragraph in your brand's voice instead.)'.

Found `options:T(e).min(2).max(4)` with "There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically"; `kind` in ["choice","text","number"]; and `if(D&&i.CLAUDE_CODE_QUESTION_EXTENDED)lPs(!0)`, where D needs an entrypoint in {sdk-ts, sdk-py, sdk-cli, local-agent, claude-desktop, claude-desktop-3p} or remote.

Present' starts at 7,914. node --test: 31/32, with the same version.test.mjs failure as an unpatched copy. `claude plugin validate . --strict`: passed. mcp `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, build, npm test: 233/233.

- The fix assessment says the reviewer's 'ask for the artifact in one line after the questions' clashes with SKILL.md:62. That's overstated: a line between the last question and the reply line satisfies both. It is ambiguous, though. critique-2 shows the model adding such a line after the reply line. So the verifier's choice, putting the invitation in the question, is still better.

findings.title: Language rules conflict with the media rule, and the files disagree on translating headings
findings.summary: There are two separate problems, and neither has changed since 34d9caa. (1) SKILL.md:36, blueprint.md:103 and universal:12 ask for a reply-language line with no exception for image or video prompts, and the universal core lacks image-video.md:126's rule (ask, or keep the user's language and list it as an assumption). (2) output-format.md:3 says to translate the headings, but the universal core says nothing about it. Today's non-English runs disagree: three kept English headings with mixed-language menus, and one (U4) translated everything.

claims.claim: SKILL.md:36, blueprint.md:103 and universal:12 require a reply-language line with no exception.
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:36: '…and include a line telling the target model which language to answer in.' blueprint.md:103: '…and it says which language to respond in.' universal:12 says the same as SKILL.md:36. blueprint.md:3 exempts image and video prompts from the skeleton, which holds 'Language: respond in <language>' at :35. It does not exempt them from the final check at :103.

claims.claim: The media rule forbids instruction lines inside image and video prompts.
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:77, image-video.md:8 and universal:40 ban roles, headings, tags and 'because' clauses, not instruction lines as such. But image-video.md:8 gives the reason 'they become things to draw', which fits a reply-language line too. None of the output shapes A-H (image-video.md:57-102) has a place for one.

claims.claim: Recorded skill runs handled this sensibly.
claims.evidence: In today's skill japanese-midjourney-quick run, the Midjourney prompt has no language line. Assumption 1 reads '日本語のままにしました。…必要なら英訳します。' (it kept Japanese and offers English). No media prompt in today's runs has a reply-language line: skill Japanese and English Midjourney, U2, U6.

claims.claim: The universal core lacks image-video.md:126's rule.
claims.evidence: `grep -c 'translate silently' universal/prompt-engine.md` returns 0. The rule appears only in the knowledge file (universal/prompt-engine-knowledge.md:697), which universal/README.md:8 calls optional.

claims.claim: So chatbot users get a silent choice.
claims.evidence: In U6 (universal core only), a Japanese request became an English Midjourney prompt. The reply said so in its first line ('英語プロンプトを作りました') and under What I added, tagged [best practice]. It did not list the choice under Assumptions or offer to switch. It justified the choice with 'Midjourneyは英語の方が認識精度が高い', which image-video.md:126 says vendors don't document. This is one run.

claims.claim: output-format.md:3 says to translate the headings, while universal section 5 gives fixed English headings 'in exactly this order'.
claims.evidence: output-format.md:3: 'Use the headings below in the user's language.' Universal section 5 (universal:43-51) lists English headings and says nothing about translating them. 'In exactly this order' is about order, so the core is silent rather than contradictory.

claims.claim: Recorded non-English runs keep English headings and produce mixed-language menus.
claims.evidence: In today's runs, skill Spanish, skill Japanese and U6 kept English headings with mixed menus: 'Fill placeholders ★: dime los datos…', 'Done ★ — Midjourneyの…', 'Run it now ★ (私は…)'. U4 translated every heading and menu label: '### Prompt completo', '1) Ejecutarlo ahora ★ 2) Refinar 3) Guardar en archivo'. The spanish-quick and japanese-midjourney-quick graders passed; they don't check headings.
