audit.reasoning:
Both halves exist on this branch and are unchanged since 34d9caa.

The language line:
- SKILL.md:36 and universal:12 ask for 'a line telling the target model which language to answer in', and blueprint.md:103 checks for it. None has a media exception. blueprint.md:3 exempts media only from the skeleton.
- plan.md:52 says the same ('adding a "Respond in <language>" line'), while plan.md:62 wants media prompts in 'the target tool's own format'. The fix reconciles two plan lines; it doesn't override a decision.
- In the skill the conflict is on paper only. image-video.md:126 governs media language, and no media prompt in today's runs has a language line (skill English and Japanese Midjourney, U2, U6).
- The universal core is the real gap. 'translate silently' appears 0 times in universal/prompt-engine.md; it is only in the optional knowledge file (line 697). In U6 a Japanese request became an English prompt. The reply said so, but it justified the switch with an unverified claim tagged [best practice] ('Midjourneyは英語の方が認識精度が高い'). It didn't list the choice under Assumptions. So 'silent' is overstated, but 'not offered as a changeable choice' holds.

Headings:
- The files don't really disagree. output-format.md:3 says 'Use the headings below in the user's language'. The universal core is silent, and its 'reply in the user's language' (universal:12) points the same way.
- The real problem is behavior. Both skill runs read output-format.md and still kept English headings and English menu labels with translated text (raw traces e-Z6c1eS and e-x3sLM8). U6 did the same, while U4 translated everything, down to 'cambia 2: …'.
- The spanish-quick judge passed the English-heading reply 3/3. contract.json checks English heading strings only in the source files. Nothing in the scripts or the MCP server reads reply headings. So the harm is cosmetic, and which rule to keep is the owner's call.

But the Format B example (questions.md:63-68), the universal core's only example (universal:29) and the README (README.md:12-14) star b), and the universal core states no order. Outputs vary to match. In text the ★ works wherever it sits, and SKILL.md:61 and questions.md:53 restate the dialog's first-position rule, so this is an internal inconsistency, not a bug users would notice.

audit.reasoning:
The contradiction is real. It dates from the first skill commit (8a15447 added both the rule and the b) example), and nothing has changed since 34d9caa.
- SKILL.md:57 ('the recommended option first') and questions.md:38 ('recommended option first;') are general rules.
- Three examples star b): the Format B example (questions.md:63-68: 1b 2b 3b), the universal core's only example (universal:29: 1b) and the README (README.md:12-14: 1b 2b). The universal core states no order (universal:26).
- The method's own final check asks that 'examples agree with the instructions' (blueprint.md:98), so this fails its own standard.
- plan.md:18 fixes first position only for the Claude Code dialog, and SKILL.md:61 and questions.md:53 already restate it there.
- 'Every text example' is overstated: the 'Good' example (questions.md:42) and the What next? menus star the first item.
- Users won't notice. `ok` accepts every ★ wherever it sits, and ask_user takes the recommended option as an index (mcp/src/questions.ts:209).

One nuance the verifier missed: today the skill follows the rule, not the examples. Its three live question rounds put the ★ first 18 of 18 times (coding-vague 6, critique-1 7, critique-2 5). The variation comes from the universal core (U7: 1b 2c 3b 4a 5b 6a; U3: all a) and from the older committed history (1b, then a).

findings.title: The description promises "critique", but there is no critique path
findings.summary: The facts hold. The description says 'improve, critique or write' (SKILL.md:3), but nothing in the skill body, the universal core, the MCP server or plan.md says what a critique request gets. In two live runs, 'What's missing from this prompt?' got one or two sentences listing the gaps, then a round of 7 or 5 questions. So, unlike the finding says, the user does get a short direct answer. Whether a feedback-only request needs its own path, or 'critique' should leave the description, is a product-scope choice.

claims.claim: The description triggers on 'critique'.
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:3 'Use to improve, critique or write a prompt ...'. git log -L3,3 shows it arrived in 55a5b2b, 'Tune the skill description ...'.

claims.claim: The body covers only improving and writing prompts.
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:19 covers 'improve, enhance, rewrite, expand or optimize a prompt', a prompt for another AI tool, or invocation by name. Outside generated files, git grep -i critique finds only SKILL.md:3. universal/prompt-engine.md:9 ('improve, rewrite or write'), mcp/src/server.ts:63 and :213, and plan.md:51 (the trigger list) don't mention it either.

claims.claim: The trigger tests count 'What's missing from this prompt?' as a request that should start the skill.
claims.evidence: docs/compatibility.md:53: the first description 'missed "What's missing from this prompt?"'; the current description scored 24/24. The query set itself isn't committed.

claims.claim: A user who asks for feedback gets a question round.
claims.evidence: Both live runs (/prompt-engine:prompt-engine, Sonnet 5.5): critique-1.md asks 7 questions and critique-2.md asks 5, each ending with 'Reply `ok` to accept every ★'. No eval case covers a feedback-only request.

claims.claim: They get no direct answer until they reply.
claims.evidence: Both runs open with a short list of gaps. critique-1.md: 'It doesn't say what the post is for, who reads it, what angle on AI to take, how long it should be, how it should sound, or what facts about your company it can use.' critique-2.md: 'The main gaps are the angle, the reader, the goal, the length and the voice.' Neither gives scores or says why each gap matters. This is one run each, so it shows what can happen, not what always happens.

claims.claim: output-format.md:104 says a question round contains only the questions.
claims.evidence: output-format.md:104 'When you are asking questions, the reply is only the questions'. The runs treated the intro line of Format B (questions.md:61) as room for a one-line diagnosis.

claims.claim: The reviewer's sentence can be added as written.
claims.evidence: In my copy, the 280-character sentence moves '### 5. Present' to start at 8,086, and validate fails: 'section "### 5. Present" starts at char 8086'.

review_findings.problem: The new critique line reaches MCP hosts through the brief, but over MCP the question round goes through ask_user, and nothing says where the gap line goes. findings.title: build.mjs does nothing, silently, when its path has a space, goes through a symlink, or is on Windows
findings.summary: scripts/build.mjs:205 runs main() only when import.meta.url equals `file://${process.argv[1]}`. On this Mac, `build.mjs --check` exits 0 with no output on a stale tree, and `build.mjs` writes nothing, in three cases: a folder whose name has a space or a non-ASCII letter, a path through a symlink, and a path under /tmp. This causes the one failing root test here (version.test.mjs). CI is not affected, because it runs on ubuntu-latest, where checkout paths have no spaces or symlinks.

claims.claim: The guard compares import.meta.url with `file://${process.argv[1]}`.
claims.evidence: scripts/build.mjs:205: "if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) main();". build.mjs is unchanged since 34d9caa (`git log 34d9caa..HEAD -- scripts/build.mjs` is empty).

claims.claim: import.meta.url is percent-encoded and is the real path; argv[1] is neither, so they differ for spaces, non-ASCII names and symlinks.
claims.evidence: A probe printed both sides. Space: 'with%20space' vs 'with space'. Accent: 'caf%C3%A9' vs 'café'. Symlink: '.../symtarget/...' vs '.../symlink/...'. /tmp: 'file:///private/tmp/...' vs 'file:///tmp/...'. All four print equal: false; the plain real-path copy prints true. Node resolves argv[1] to an absolute path but does not follow symlinks.

claims.claim: On Windows the guard can never match.
claims.evidence: No Windows machine here. A simulation supports the claim: Node's pathToFileURL('C:\\Users\\dev\\prompt-engine\\scripts\\build.mjs', {windows:true}) gives 'file:///C:/Users/dev/prompt-engine/scripts/build.mjs', while the guard builds 'file://C:\\Users\\dev\\prompt-engine\\scripts\\build.mjs'.

claims.claim: When they differ, build.mjs writes nothing, and --check exits 0 with no output even on a stale tree.
claims.evidence: Reproduced in four copies: a folder with a space, a symlink, a non-ASCII folder, and a /tmp path. In each, after media-targets.md was made stale, `--check` exited 0 and printed nothing, and `build` exited 0 but left the stale line in place.

claims.claim: validate.mjs reports the file stale and says to run build.mjs, but running it does nothing.
claims.evidence: scripts/validate.mjs:217. In the copy with a space it printed 'error: skills/prompt-engine/references/media-targets.md: stale; run node scripts/build.mjs' and exited 1. Running build.mjs afterwards left the file unchanged.

claims.claim: version.mjs:73 runs build.mjs this way, so a version bump can leave mcp/src/generated/content.ts with the old VERSION.
claims.evidence: Holds whenever the real path has a space or a non-ASCII letter. In '$W/bump space/repo', `version.mjs 9.8.7` exited 0, but content.ts:4 still read 'export const VERSION = "0.1.0";'. Through a symlink it fails only when PE_ROOT names the symlinked path, as the test sets it. Without PE_ROOT, `root` comes from import.meta.url (build.mjs:16), which is already a real path, so the bump worked (VERSION "9.8.7").

claims.claim: On macOS os.tmpdir() is under /var, a symlink to /private/var, so the version test fails.
claims.evidence: os.tmpdir() = /var/folders/6w/.../T, and /var -> private/var. Today the failing test is the second one, not the first: commit 5beff3a added a test before it. The failure reads 'sets the version everywhere and the repository still validates ... error: mcp/src/generated/content.ts: stale'. The test passes with TMPDIR set to a real folder and fails with TMPDIR set through /tmp.

claims.claim: (Extra) `npm run generate` in mcp/ uses the same entry point.
claims.evidence: mcp/package.json:40 has '"generate": "node ../scripts/build.mjs"', so the same guard applies. I did not run it separately from a path with a space. Run from mcp/ with a relative ../ path in a real-path folder, both the old and the fixed guard work.

findings.reproduction:
$W = <scratch>/work/verify-scripts-build. Each copy was made with `git archive HEAD | tar -x`. I appended a line to skills/prompt-engine/references/media-targets.md, then ran from /:
- $W/plain/repo (control): `--check` exit=1, printing 'stale: skills/prompt-engine/references/media-targets.md'. `build` printed 'wrote ...'. validate OK.
- "$W/with space/repo", $W/symlink/repo (a link to $W/symtarget), $W/café/repo, and /tmp/claude-502/.../plain/repo: `--check` exit=0 with no output. `build` exit=0, and the stale line was still there (count 1). validate: 'error: skills/prompt-engine/references/media-targets.md: stale; run node scripts/build.mjs', '1 error(s)'.
- Version bump in "$W/bump space/repo": `node scripts/version.mjs 9.8.7` printed '... → 9.8.7' for 6 files, then 'Then run the checks and tag v9.8.7', exit=0. content.ts:4 still read 'export const VERSION = "0.1.0";'. validate: 'error: mcp/src/generated/content.ts: stale'.
- Real repository, read-only: `node --test scripts/test/version.test.mjs` failed 'sets the version everywhere and the repository still validates' with 'AssertionError ... error: mcp/src/generated/content.ts: stale; run node scripts/build.mjs ... 1 !== 0' (pass 3, fail 1). With TMPDIR=$W/realtmp: pass 4, fail 0. With TMPDIR=/tmp/.../realtmp: fail 1. `git status` stayed empty.
- Baseline on the repository: build --check 'generated files are up to date'; validate OK; root tests 'tests 32, pass 31, fail 1'.
findings.refutation: I looked for a fix after 34d9caa and found none: build.mjs and version.mjs are unchanged. I checked whether CI would hit it. It doesn't: ci.yml:14 runs on ubuntu-latest, where checkout paths have no spaces or symlinks and /tmp is a real folder. I checked whether a stale file could get past the full check sequence. It can't: validate.mjs:216-217 compares buildAll() with the files on disk, independent of the guard, and mcp/test/brief.test.ts:240-244 requires 'generated files are up to date' in the output, so that test fails rather than passing silently. The owner's checkout (<repo>) is a real path without spaces, so the normal workflow works. I also ruled out another cause for the macOS test failure: the same test passes with a real TMPDIR. What remains is real: `--check` gives a false pass on its own; build.mjs, version.mjs and `npm run generate` silently do nothing; validate's advice doesn't help; and a required check fails on macOS.

audit.reasoning: scripts/build.mjs:205 compares import.meta.url with 'file://' + process.argv[1]. import.meta.url is the real path and is percent-encoded; argv[1] is neither. I made copies whose paths have a space, an accent, a symlink, and a plain copy reached through /tmp. In each, `--check` exited 0 with no output on a stale tree, and `build` exited 0 without writing anything. The plain real-path copy worked. This is why test 2 of scripts/test/version.test.mjs fails on this Mac: it passes with TMPDIR set to a real folder and fails when TMPDIR goes through /tmp. version.mjs:73 leaves content.ts at VERSION "0.1.0" when the real path has a space, or when PE_ROOT names a symlinked path. validate.mjs:216-217 still reports the stale file, so the full check chain can't pass on a stale tree. But `--check` alone gives a false pass, and the fix validate suggests does nothing in these paths. build.mjs, version.mjs and validate.mjs are unchanged since 34d9caa, so this is not already fixed.
audit.checks_run: Copies made with git archive HEAD | tar -x under audit-scripts-build/: plain13, 'with space', 'café', symlink -> symtarget, and plain13 reached through /tmp. In each I appended a line to media-targets.md, then ran build --check, build and validate from /. Results: plain gave check=1, 'wrote', validate OK. The other four gave check=0 with no output, build=0, the stale line still there, and validate printing 'error: …media-targets.md: stale; run node scripts/build.mjs' with exit 1. A relative `node scripts/build.mjs --check` inside the space copy also exited 0. A probe printed both sides of the guard: 'with%20space' vs 'with space', 'caf%C3%A9' vs 'café', symtarget vs symlink, file:///private/tmp vs /tmp. version.mjs 9.8.7: in 'bump space' without PE_ROOT, content.ts:4 stayed "0.1.0" and validate failed. Through a symlink without PE_ROOT it became "9.8.7". Through a symlink with PE_ROOT set to the symlink path it stayed "0.1.0". Real repo, read-only: version.test.mjs gave 'not ok 2' and pass 3/fail 1; with TMPDIR=<real folder>, 4/4; with TMPDIR through /tmp, fail 1. Windows simulation: pathToFileURL(win path, {windows:true}) gives 'file:///C:/…', but the guard builds 'file://C:\…'. Fix A (reviewer) and fix B (verifier) in all four copies: both gave check=1, then wrote, then check=0. Under --preserve-symlinks-main on the symlink and /tmp copies, A exited 0 on a stale tree and B exited 1. With fix B: imports don't run main(); a relative run and `node ../scripts/build.mjs` from mcp/ work in the space copy; root tests 32/32 with the default macOS TMPDIR. With the verifier's build-path.test.mjs added: 33/33 under both the default and a real TMPDIR. The same test fails on current code with '0 !== 1' under both. Node docs: import.meta.main was 'Added in: v24.2.0, v22.18.0', so it's not in Node 20. `git log 34d9caa..HEAD -- scripts/build.mjs scripts/version.mjs scripts/validate.mjs` is empty.
audit.evidence_errors: Nothing wrong. Two notes. (1) 'CI is not affected … ubuntu-latest, where checkout paths have no spaces or symlinks' is an inference, not checked here, and the workflows are still parked in .github/pending-workflows/. (2) A consequence it doesn't mention: mcp/test/brief.test.ts:240-244 expects 'generated files are up to date' on stdout. In a checkout whose path has a space or a symlink, that test fails even when every file is fresh, because `--check` prints nothing there. I inferred this from the reproduction and did not run the MCP suite.
audit.fix_corrections: Fix B is right as proposed, and I re-verified it (see checks). One change to the new test: symlinkSync(dir, link, 'dir') needs admin rights or Developer Mode on Windows. Use process.platform === 'win32' ? 'junction' : 'dir'. CI runs only on ubuntu today, so this matters only for Windows contributors.

findings.fix_assessment: Two variants were tested. A is the reviewer's fix, `pathToFileURL(realpathSync(argv[1])).href === import.meta.url`. B compares the real paths of both sides. Both worked in every copy: a folder with a space, a symlink, an accented folder name, and the /tmp path. In each, the stale file gave `--check` exit 1, `build` removed the stale line, and the next `--check` exited 0. A relative run from the repo root worked. Importing build.mjs from validate.mjs did not run main(), and neither did an import with no argv[1]. All 32 root tests pass with the default macOS TMPDIR. The one difference is under `node --preserve-symlinks-main`: A still silently does nothing (exit 0 on a stale tree), because import.meta.url is then the symlink path; B exits 1. `import.meta.main` exists on Node 24 but not on Node 20, which these scripts support, so it can't be used alone. The reviewer's proposed test, a copy in a folder named with a space plus a symlink to it, fails on the current code ('0 !== 1'). It passes with either fix, with both a symlinked and a real TMPDIR, so it also protects Linux CI. With fix A plus the test: 33/33.

findings.title: The history sanitizer writes API keys, tokens, home paths, hostnames and session IDs into fixtures meant for a public repo
findings.summary: True on this branch. sanitize() keeps the conversation word for word. It rewrites only the exact plugin and temp-folder paths, and its only check is a refusal of ASCII-domain e-mails. So keys, tokens, other home paths, hostnames and the session ID in a recording pass straight through. Windows paths are never rewritten, npm specs such as next-auth@5.0.0 are refused without saying where, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is ignored, and no test can import the module. The three committed fixtures are clean, so the risk is in future recordings.

claims.claim: sanitize() keeps message, toolUseResult and thinking word for word, rewrites only the exact repo and cwd strings, and its only scan is an ASCII e-mail regex.
claims.evidence: record-history.mjs:70 KEEP_KEYS includes 'message' and 'toolUseResult'; :75 copies the values as they are; :82 text.split(repo).join('/plugin').split(cwd).join('/workspace'); :83 /[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+/. The file is unchanged since 34d9caa (git diff empty; last change 998e0c8).

claims.claim: Other private data in the first message, assistant text, thinking and anything the Read tool opens is written to the fixture.
claims.evidence: Run A (fake claude, planted transcript) exited 0 and out.jsonl kept everything planted. From the first message: an sk-ant key, a ghp_ token and an AKIA key. From a thinking block: /Users/alice, a foreign hostname, this Mac's hostname, the original session UUID and a claude.ai session_ URL. From a Read of a home file: its path, an sk-proj key and jürgen@müller.de. Also msg_ IDs. Only the attachment event's e-mail and an api-request-blob event were dropped. Context: thinking text is empty in the committed fixtures and in today's 2.1.317 transcript (signature only). The permissions doc says a bare tool name matches all uses of the tool, so the recorder's --allowedTools Read (line 37) pre-approves reads outside the working folder.

claims.claim: (a) The path rewrite runs on serialized JSON, so Windows paths are never rewritten.
claims.evidence: With sanitize() copied verbatim from HEAD, repo C:\Users\alice\src\prompt-engine and a Temp cwd both come out unchanged; POSIX paths come out as /plugin/... and /workspace. JSON doubles the backslashes, so split(repo) can never match. I could not run it on Windows. The fixture would also stay stale, because build.mjs:137 refreshes Reads only under ^/plugin/. Scope: no doc claims Windows support for maintainers, and the parked CI runs only on ubuntu.

claims.claim: (b) The e-mail regex refuses package specs without saying where, yet misses non-ASCII addresses.
claims.evidence: Refused: next-auth@5.0.0, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.2.3, @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.312 and git@github.com:… . The message ('sanitized transcript still contains an e-mail-like string; refusing to write it') names no line or text. In run B the refusal came after the (fake) model call. Missed: jürgen@müller.de and ivan@пример.рф, which have non-ASCII domains. Still caught: jürgen@example.com, through its ASCII tail. So only non-ASCII domains slip through.

claims.claim: (c) The transcript is looked for only in ~/.claude/projects, ignoring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and only after the billed call.
claims.evidence: Line 49 is const projects = join(homedir(), '.claude', 'projects'), and it runs after the spawn at :33. The sessions doc says CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR will 'Move storage off ~/.claude'. The env-vars doc says 'All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path', and that the variable can also be set in user or managed settings. Run C1 made one call, then failed with 'transcript for session … not found under <W>/home/.claude/projects'. Run C2, with no ~/.claude, failed with 'ENOENT … scandir …/.claude/projects'. The real claude wasn't run (billed); the fake writes where the docs say.

claims.claim: (d) Importing the module runs the recorder, so sanitize() has no tests.
claims.evidence: Importing prints the usage text and exits 2, because lines 20-24 run at import. A node:test file that imports it reports 'fail 1 … test failed'. No file in scripts/test mentions record-history or sanitize.

claims.claim: The three committed fixtures are clean, and the type filter drops the attachment events that hold the account e-mail.
claims.evidence: I scanned all three evals/*/history.jsonl. They contain no '@' at all, no /Users or /home path, no key or token pattern, no session_ URL, no /private, /var/folders or /tmp path, and no UUID other than event IDs and the fixed session ID. They do keep msg_ IDs (8, 8 and 6) and toolu_ IDs. Line 62 keeps only user and assistant events. In today's real 2.1.317 transcript, account and environment context sits in attachment events (session_context, environment).

claims.claim: Reviewer's evidence: the proposed patterns find nothing in the fixtures and catch every planted item.
claims.evidence: They find nothing in the three fixtures, and they catch the planted keys, token, /Users path, session URL and non-ASCII e-mail. The scan alone misses hostnames and the session UUID. Fix (2) handles this machine's hostname and the session ID, but in my prototype of the reviewer's fix a foreign hostname (alice-mbp.corp.internal) still got through.

claims.claim: Severity is major.
claims.evidence: The gaps are real and the output is public. But the input is mostly the maintainer's own, today's fixtures are clean, thinking text is currently empty, and CONTRIBUTING.md:109 asks for a manual read. The same sentence overstates what the script does. I rate it minor.

items.what_changed: Commit 035a462 came from an earlier run of this batch. I reviewed it against the records and the brief, re-ran its tests and kept it unchanged. New module scripts/eval/sanitize.mjs exports FIXED_SESSION, PRIVATE_PATTERNS (keys and tokens, home paths, claude.ai session IDs, the linear e-mail regex), publicText, machinePatterns, scanText and sanitize. sanitize() rewrites every string of the kept fields: the repo becomes /plugin, then the cwd (including its /var form) becomes /workspace, then home becomes ~. Each match is at a path boundary, accepts either separator, ignores case for a drive path, and keeps the rest of the path with '/' separators. The session ID becomes FIXED_SESSION, message.id is kept and thinking blocks are left as recorded. A final scan throws 'line N: kind' and never includes the match. record-history.mjs gets a real-path entry guard. Before the billed spawn it scans the first message and checks that $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects or ~/.claude/projects exists. After the call it searches both folders. review_findings.problem: The comment says every pattern runs in linear time, but the JWT pattern is quadratic. Each \beyJ start inside a long [\w-] run scans to the run's end and backtracks looking for a '.'. validate.mjs:337 runs this scan on every committed history.jsonl, so one long line in a PR can stall CI for minutes, and sanitize() runs the same scan. findings.title: refreshHistory finds the skill body by guesswork, which can corrupt or freeze the recorded skill text without failing any check
findings.summary: refreshHistory finds the old skill body by searching. It starts at the first '\n# ' (build.mjs:146) and ends at the last 'ARGUMENTS:' (build.mjs:147). The three committed recordings are refreshed exactly today, because each has an ARGUMENTS line. Three inputs corrupt or freeze a fixture with no check failing: a recording made without arguments, a SKILL.md body with no H1, and arguments that contain 'ARGUMENTS:'. Text placed before the H1 grows by one copy on every build, but that case is loud.

claims.claim: Claude Code appends the ARGUMENTS line only when there are arguments (installed 2.1.317).
claims.evidence: The binary has 'e=e.replaceAll("$ARGUMENTS",()=>(Z=!0,w(n))),!Z&&r&&n)e=e+`\n\nARGUMENTS: ${w(n)}`' inside 'function _Ve(e,n,r=!0,s=[],h,y)'. Plugin skills call it as '_Ve(Lo,Zn,!0,Ve,...)', where Lo starts with 'Base directory for this skill: '. So the line is added when the arguments are non-empty and no placeholder was substituted.

claims.claim: The reviewer's quote from the 2.1.312 bundle.
claims.evidence: Only 2.1.317 is installed. `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.312 dist.unpackedSize` = 190085, so the npm package is a wrapper and the code ships in a platform binary. The committed recordings, made with 2.1.312 according to the review, have the same shape as 2.1.317's.

claims.claim: SKILL.md:34 itself contains `ARGUMENTS:`.
claims.evidence: skills/prompt-engine/SKILL.md:34: '...arrives on a line that starts with `ARGUMENTS:`.' Every committed and live skill text contains 'ARGUMENTS:' twice.

claims.claim: (a) With a recording made without arguments, the new body is spliced in front of the stale tail of the old one. Later builds don't change it, and the checks pass.
claims.evidence: End to end in a copy, using save-to-file turned into a no-arguments recording with an older body: after one build the skill text is 18,267 characters (expected 10,027). It still contains '(OLD RULE)' and has '### 5. Present' twice. Then `--check` printed 'generated files are up to date' and validate printed OK. When the old body differs only near the top, everything from SKILL.md:34 onward appears twice.

claims.claim: (b) Text before SKILL.md's H1 is copied again on every build, and the checks never pass.
claims.evidence: With '<!-- note -->' before the H1, three builds gave save-to-file 68,240, then 68,257, then 68,274 bytes, holding 1, 2, then 3 notes. `--check` exited 1 after each build, and validate reported all three histories stale. This case is loud, not silent.

claims.claim: (c) If the body has no H1, the refresh is skipped from then on, silently.
claims.evidence: The first build after removing the H1 rewrote the three histories. A later edit ('REVISED-AGAIN') never reached them (0 occurrences), yet `--check` printed 'generated files are up to date' and validate printed OK. start = indexOf('\n# ') + 1 = 0, and the guard at build.mjs:151 requires start > 0.

claims.claim: In all three cases the follow-up evals test something other than the current SKILL.md.
claims.evidence: True for (a) and (c). In (b) the checks fail, so it can't pass the gate unnoticed.

claims.claim: The committed fixtures are affected now.
claims.evidence:
For all three committed recordings, and five live 2.1.317 traces from today, the skill text equals header + '

' + current body + '
' + '

ARGUMENTS: ' + args exactly. All seven invocations carried arguments.

claims.claim: (Extra) Arguments that contain 'ARGUMENTS:' are cut short, and another skill's text gets overwritten.
claims.evidence: Arguments 'improve this: ARGUMENTS: list the steps' become '...stop and wait. ARGUMENTS: list the steps': the first part of the request is lost, the rest is glued to the body's last line, and later builds don't change it. Separately, a text 'Base directory for this skill: /home/u/.claude/skills/other...' is replaced with prompt-engine's body, because build.mjs:144 matches only the generic prefix.

findings.title: Ordinary Windows and macOS checkouts fail every check: CRLF line endings and Finder's .DS_Store files
findings.summary: Git for Windows' default install sets core.autocrlf=true, which gives a CRLF checkout. On one, validate fails with 8 misleading errors, build --check reports 6 stale files, 6 of 32 script tests fail and version.mjs refuses to run. The fix the error text suggests, running build.mjs, makes it worse: content.ts and the three history.jsonl files get `\r\n` in their text, and every further build run adds another copy of the SKILL.md frontmatter to each history.jsonl. On macOS, a Finder .DS_Store in the skill folder or references/ fails validate, release.mjs and the 'repository passes as-is' test. Nothing that ships to users is affected.

claims.claim: There is no .gitattributes.
claims.evidence: `git ls-files | grep -i gitattributes` and `git log --all -- .gitattributes '**/.gitattributes'` both return nothing. There is none on disk either.

claims.claim: The scripts only handle LF: the frontmatter regexes at validate.mjs:33, build.mjs:168 and version.mjs:65, and the generated-file comparisons.
claims.evidence:
validate.mjs:33 `/^---
([\s\S]*?)
---
?/`, build.mjs:168 `/^---
[\s\S]*?
---
/` and version.mjs:65 use the same LF-only pattern. validate.mjs:217 and build.mjs:194 compare the raw file text.

claims.claim: On a CRLF checkout, validate gives 8 errors: missing YAML frontmatter, '### 5. Present' at char 8247, and 6 stale files.
claims.evidence: Reproduced exactly in a clone made with core.autocrlf=true.

claims.claim: build --check prints 6 stale lines.
claims.evidence: Reproduced: media-targets.md, the knowledge file, the 3 history.jsonl files and content.ts.

claims.claim: `node scripts/version.mjs 0.1.1` fails with 'no metadata.version line in the frontmatter'.
claims.evidence: On a real CRLF checkout it fails earlier, at the lockfile: 'mcp/package-lock.json: unexpected formatting; run `npm version 0.1.1 --no-git-tag-version` in mcp/ instead'. That hint is misleading. The SKILL.md message only appears once the lockfile is LF. Neither case writes anything (git status stays clean).

claims.claim: Ordinary Windows checkouts get CRLF.
claims.evidence: In git-for-windows/build-extra installer/install.iss (fetched today with gh api), lines 2373-2379 preselect 'CRLFAlways'. Lines 3262-3267 then write core.autocrlf=true.

claims.claim: Ordinary Windows and macOS checkouts fail every check.
claims.evidence: Overstated. `claude plugin validate . --strict` passes on the CRLF clone. A macOS checkout only fails once Finder writes a .DS_Store, and then build --check still passes. Only validate, release.mjs and one test fail.

claims.claim: With a .DS_Store present: walk() (validate.mjs:89) and the reference listing (validate.mjs:143) include it and validate fails. It is gitignored (.gitignore:7) and left out of the zip (release.mjs:36), but release.mjs runs validate first (release.mjs:30), so the release fails too.
claims.evidence: Reproduced: 3 errors. release.mjs --zip stops at 'Command failed: node scripts/validate.mjs' and creates no dist/. In scripts/test/validate.test.mjs, 'the repository passes as-is' also fails, because copyRepo copies .DS_Store.

claims.claim: New, not in the review: running build.mjs on a CRLF checkout corrupts the generated files.
claims.evidence: After `node scripts/build.mjs`, git diff shows real content changes in content.ts (every string gains `\r\n`) and in the 3 history.jsonl files. Each further run adds one frontmatter copy to each history.jsonl: 69,348 → 69,747 → 70,146 bytes, and 1 → 2 → 3 copies (HEAD has 0). Cause: build.mjs:168 fails to strip the frontmatter, then build.mjs:146 splices the body in again after the first '\n# '.

findings.reproduction:
W=<work folder>; git clone -c core.autocrlf=true file://<repo> crlf   (at 7036772)
git ls-files --eol → 198 w/crlf, 2 w/-text (the two PNGs)
node scripts/validate.mjs →
  error: skills/prompt-engine/SKILL.md: missing YAML frontmatter
  error: skills/prompt-engine/SKILL.md: section "### 5. Present" starts at char 8247; ...
  error: <6 files>: stale; run node scripts/build.mjs
  8 error(s)
node scripts/build.mjs --check → 6 'stale:' lines, exit 1
node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs → 32 tests, 6 fail (including 'the repository passes as-is' and 'rejects a Claude Code-only frontmatter key')
node scripts/version.mjs 0.1.1 → 'mcp/package-lock.json: unexpected formatting; ...'; with the lockfile converted to LF → 'skills/prompt-engine/SKILL.md: no metadata.version line in the frontmatter'
claude plugin validate . --strict → '✔ Validation passed'
node scripts/build.mjs; git diff --stat → 4 files with content changes. content.ts now reads `"# Prompt Engine\r\n\r\nYou are ..."`. validate still fails: frontmatter + 3 stale history.jsonl.
Repeated builds: evals/save-to-file/history.jsonl 69,348 → 69,747 → 70,146 bytes; 'name: prompt-engine' 1 → 2 → 3 (0 at HEAD).
.DS_Store copy (skills/prompt-engine/.DS_Store and references/.DS_Store):
  validate → two 'only Markdown files belong in the skill folder' errors and '.../references/.DS_Store: not linked from SKILL.md'; exit 1
  release.mjs --zip → exit 1, no dist/
  node --test validate.test.mjs → 'not ok 1 - the repository passes as-is'; 12 pass
  build --check → up to date
The real repo has no .DS_Store today (find).
findings.refutation: None of the cited files has changed since 34d9caa (`git log 34d9caa..HEAD` on the scripts, .gitignore and data). I checked whether CRLF checkouts are realistic: Git for Windows defaults to autocrlf=true. I checked whether the CRLF failure is only cosmetic: it isn't, because following the hint writes wrong content. I checked who is affected. CI runs only on ubuntu-latest (pending-workflows/ci.yml:14, :35) and isn't active yet, so CI isn't affected. Claude Code's own validator accepts CRLF. .DS_Store never ships, because it is gitignored and left out of the zip. No doc promises Windows support for contributors. The finding overstates 'every check' and 'ordinary macOS checkouts', but the core defect holds. It rates major because a Windows contributor can't get one check to pass, and the suggested fix damages eval fixtures.

audit.reasoning:
The core defect reproduces on this branch. I cloned a repo built from `git archive HEAD` with core.autocrlf=true, which gave 198 files with CRLF and the 2 PNGs as binary. On that clone, validate gives the same 8 errors: missing frontmatter, '### 5. Present' at char 8247, and 6 stale files. build --check lists the same 6 files. `version.mjs 0.1.1` stops at the lockfile message. With the lockfile converted to LF it stops at 'no metadata.version line'. Neither run writes anything.

Running build.mjs three times grows evals/save-to-file/history.jsonl from 68,235 to 69,348, 69,747 and 70,146 bytes. That is 1, 2, then 3 frontmatter copies, against 0 at HEAD. content.ts also gains `\r\n` inside its strings.

A .DS_Store in skills/prompt-engine/ and references/ gives 3 validate errors. It also stops `release.mjs --zip` before dist/ exists and fails 'the repository passes as-is'. A .DS_Store at the root or in evals/ is harmless.

The macOS case hits the owner's own documented step: docs/publishing.md:48 runs `node scripts/release.mjs` locally.

Git for Windows does default to CRLF. Its installer preselects CRLFAlways (install.iss:2374-2379) and writes core.autocrlf=true (:3262-3267).

There is no .gitattributes in the tree, in the history or in the global config. No cited file has changed since 34d9caa.

'Every check' is overstated: `claude plugin validate . --strict` passes on the CRLF clone and on the .DS_Store copy.
audit.checks_run:
Work folder: <scratch>/work/audit-scripts-validate.
- Read the scripts and .gitignore.
- Made src/ from `git archive HEAD`, committed it there, and cloned it with `-c core.autocrlf=true` into crlf/. Checked `git ls-files --eol`.
- In crlf/, ran validate, build --check, all script tests (TAP reporter), version.mjs 0.1.1 (also with an LF lockfile) and claude plugin validate.
- Ran build.mjs 3 times in a copy and measured the size and frontmatter count of history.jsonl.
- Ran the same tests on an LF copy (repo/) to compare.
- Simulated the Windows main-guard comparison with `pathToFileURL(path, {windows:true})`.
- .DS_Store copy (ds/): ran validate, build --check, release --zip, validate.test.mjs and plugin validate.
- Fetched installer/install.iss with a read-only gh api call and grepped for CRLFAlways.
- Looked for .gitattributes everywhere, and for .DS_Store in the real repo (none).
- Applied the proposed fix (tools/patch16.mjs) to LF, CRLF and junk-file copies.
- Cloned a repo that has the .gitattributes (crlf-ga/) and ran `git add --renormalize`.
- Probed the BOM regex forms.
- Ran all corrected fixes together on an LF copy and an all-CRLF copy (all/, all-crlf/).
audit.evidence_errors:
1. '6 of 32 script tests fail': on this Mac, test 30 ('sets the version everywhere…') also fails on a plain LF copy. That is finding 13: content.ts goes stale through the symlinked tmpdir. CRLF adds 5 failures (tests 16, 18, 19, 20 and 28), not 6.
2. The summary presents macOS results as what a Git for Windows checkout gets. On native Windows, build.mjs's main() never runs (finding 13). There import.meta.url is file:///C:/… while the guard builds file://C:\…. I simulated this from the path formats; I could not run it on Windows. So on Windows, `build.mjs --check` prints nothing and exits 0 instead of listing 6 stale files, and `node scripts/build.mjs` writes nothing. The corruption from following the hint therefore needs a CRLF tree where main() does run: macOS, Linux, or WSL over a Windows checkout. validate.mjs and version.mjs don't use that guard, so their failures do apply on Windows.
audit.fix_corrections:
1. Write the BOM regex as `/^﻿/`. The reviewer's text in findings/16.json has a literal U+FEFF there. Don't use the `\u{FEFF}` form from the CLAUDE.md gotcha: without the `u` flag, `/^\u{FEFF}/` matches the text 'u{FEFF}' and strips nothing (tested). Check the bytes after editing.
2. Land this before finding 13's main-guard fix, or with it. Once build.mjs runs on Windows, a CRLF checkout without this fix duplicates the frontmatter in history.jsonl and puts `\r\n` into content.ts.
3. The OS_JUNK filter and the release.mjs:36 `-x` additions must land together. With only today's `-x '*.DS_Store'`, Thumbs.db and desktop.ini in the skill folder go into the zip (4 junk entries in my test).
4. Tested and fine:
- The .gitattributes: an autocrlf=true clone gets 199 LF files and 2 binary; `git add --renormalize .` changes nothing.
- normalize at build.mjs:17 and :194, validate.mjs:22, and version.mjs:33, :53 and :64. With it, version.mjs 0.1.1 on the CRLF copy changes only the version lines.
- All corrected fixes together, on an LF copy and on an all-CRLF copy: build --check, validate, 31/32 tests (test 30 is finding 13), plugin validate, and release --zip (12 entries).

findings.fix_assessment:
The .gitattributes (`* text=auto eol=lf`, `*.png binary`) is correct and enough for Git checkouts. Tested: an autocrlf=true clone of a repo that has it is LF everywhere (199 w/lf, 2 w/-text). Validate, build --check, the tests and claude plugin validate all pass there. The index is already all LF with no CR or BOM, so no renormalize commit is needed, and .gitattributes isn't a forbidden root file.

The read normalization is incomplete as written. It fixes validate, but build --check still reports 6 stale files, because build.mjs:194 compares raw readFileSync output. With :194 normalized too, a CRLF clone without .gitattributes passes validate, build --check and 28/28 validate and lint tests. version.mjs 0.1.1 then changes only the version lines. It is worth keeping as a second layer, for files an editor saves with CRLF.

The OS_JUNK filter and the zip exclusions are correct. I tested them with .DS_Store, Thumbs.db and desktop.ini: validate passes, and the zip has the same 12 entries with no junk.

The reviewer's fix leaves out .gitignore lines for Thumbs.db and desktop.ini, and tests. All five fixes applied together pass every check.
findings.proposed_fix:
1. Add /.gitattributes with two lines: `* text=auto eol=lf` and `*.png binary`.
2. scripts/build.mjs: add `export const normalize = (s) => s.replace(/^﻿/, '').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n');`. Use it in read (line 17) and in main()'s comparison (line 194). Import it in scripts/validate.mjs (line 22) and scripts/version.mjs (lines 33, 53, 64) and wrap those readFileSync calls. Leave release.mjs:59 alone: it hashes binary files.
3. scripts/validate.mjs: add `const OS_JUNK = new Set(['.DS_Store', 'Thumbs.db', 'desktop.ini']);`. Add `.filter((f) => !OS_JUNK.has(f))` in walk() (line 89) and to refFiles (line 143).
4. scripts/release.mjs:36: `'-x', '*.DS_Store', '*Thumbs.db', '*desktop.ini'`.
5. .gitignore: add `Thumbs.db` and `desktop.ini` after line 7.
6. scripts/test/validate.test.mjs: add 'passes with CRLF line endings', which converts SKILL.md and references/media-targets.md to CRLF and expects exit 0. Add 'ignores .DS_Store in the skill folder', which writes references/.DS_Store and expects exit 0.
owner_questions: Optional: should CI also run the root checks (build --check, validate, node --test) on windows-latest? Without that, nothing stops Windows support from breaking again. release.mjs needs zip and unzip, so it would stay Linux-only.

Optional: add a windows-latest CI job for the root checks? Until finding 13 is fixed, it would give a false pass on build --check. release.mjs --zip needs zip and unzip, so the job would cover only build --check, validate and node --test.

items.title: Check text out as LF (.gitattributes), and read every source as LF without a BOM

items.what_changed: New .gitattributes with exactly '* text=auto eol=lf' and '*.png binary'; `git add --renormalize .` changed nothing. build.mjs exports normalize(), which strips a BOM by charCodeAt(0) === 0xfeff (no regex, no raw BOM in the source; grep for EF BB BF prints 0) and turns CRLF into LF. read() and main()'s comparison use it. validate.mjs's read() uses it (import { buildAll, root, normalize, OS_JUNK }). version.mjs's three reads (bumpJson, the lockfile, SKILL.md) use it. release.mjs:59 is left alone.
items.tests: build.test.mjs: 'a CRLF checkout builds as up to date, and a rebuild writes LF text without copying the frontmatter' and 'a byte-order mark at the start of a source file changes nothing'. validate.test.mjs: 'passes with CRLF line endings', via a new passes() helper. version.test.mjs: 'sets the version in a CRLF checkout, changing only the version lines'. Checked by mutation: with normalize as the identity, all four fail. With a normalize that keeps the BOM, the BOM test fails. With validate's read raw, the validate CRLF test fails (and both build tests, which call validate). With main()'s comparison raw, the CRLF build test fails. With each of version.mjs's three reads raw on its own, the version CRLF test fails (unexpected keys, 'unexpected formatting', 'no metadata.version line'). Manual: a `git clone -c core.autocrlf=true` of the branch has 203 w/lf and 2 w/-text, and build --check and validate pass. The same clone of 66ee919 has 200 w/crlf, 6 stale files and 8 validate errors.
items.deviations: Tests a bit stronger than the prototype: the CRLF build test first asserts the histories really were converted, and also rejects a raw CR in the rewritten histories. The version CRLF test asserts each file keeps its line count. I also updated version.mjs's header comment, which said edited files keep their formatting: they are now written with LF and no BOM. That change is folded into the 13a+16a commit.

It uses the same checkout and setup-node 22 as the skill job and runs only build --check, validate and node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs (not release.mjs --zip, not claude plugin validate). It inherits ci.yml's contents: read. This is the same change as 33a, made once.
items.tests: Structural spec (my tools/check-ci-structure.mjs): windows job present with runs-on, shell bash, the skill job's checkout and Node, exactly the three run blocks and their step names; these checks fail on the base ci.yml and on a mutation that adds release.mjs --zip to the job. check-workflows lists `job windows: runs-on "windows-latest"` with bash -n clean; actionlint 1.7.12 and Ruby YAML pass. The three blocks, extracted from ci.yml, ran under bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail on a copy of this branch: exit 0, 32/32 script tests. Windows itself not run (first run at step 2).
items.deviations: Took 33a's shape, as the batch summary says: job id `windows`, name "Scripts on Windows", with shell: bash (16d's draft had `skill-windows` and no bash). Optional parts: the `git ls-files --eol` step was not added, because D10 approved only these three checks. The optional rename of the "Script tests" step was done in both jobs: "Script tests (build, validator, version, release and eval scripts, lint-rule timing)". It names the tests the core and evals lanes add, so on this branch alone it names files that aren't here yet.

review_findings.problem: No test checks the skill zip's -x exclusions. This batch makes validate skip .DS_Store, Thumbs.db and desktop.ini, so validate no longer stops a release when they are present. The -x list is now the only thing that keeps them out of dist/prompt-engine.zip, the coupling 16's audit (fix_corrections 3) warned about. The brief asked only for a manual check, which was done, so the item meets its record. Still, a regression here would ship junk silently.
review_findings.outcome_evidence: release.test.mjs 'release.mjs --zip leaves out the files Finder and Explorer write': writes the three OS_JUNK names into skills/prompt-engine/ and references/, runs release.mjs --zip with the normal PATH (skipped without zip/unzip), and checks that unzip -Z1 lists none of them. It fails with the -x list back to '*.DS_Store'.

review_findings.problem: release.mjs still parses .claude-plugin/plugin.json raw. With a BOM in that file, build --check and validate now pass (this batch), but release.mjs crashes with a SyntaxError stack trace before it reaches validate. build.mjs:17-18's new comment says a BOM an editor added 'changes nothing'. The read is pre-existing, no item covers it, and the implementer already listed it under open_issues. Impact is low because version.mjs strips the BOM when it bumps.
review_findings.outcome_evidence: release.mjs now imports normalize and parses plugin.json through it; the binary hash in section 4 is untouched. New test 'release.mjs --zip reads a plugin.json that starts with a byte-order mark' passes, and fails with the raw read restored (SyntaxError, exit 1).

findings.title: The self-lint never checks the reference files, which the model reads as instructions
findings.summary: The selfCheck lint runs only on SKILL.md and universal/prompt-engine.md (validate.mjs:121). The 9 reference files are never linted, although the skill reads them in its first turn and build.mjs copies them into the knowledge file and the MCP content. CONTRIBUTING.md:48-50 and .claude/CLAUDE.md:16 both say the validator enforces this for method text. Today's references are clean, apart from two lines in blueprint.md that name the patterns in order to warn against them.

claims.claim: selfCheck rules run only on SKILL.md and the universal core.
claims.evidence: validate.mjs:121: `const INSTRUCTION_FILES = [SKILL, 'universal/prompt-engine.md'];`

claims.claim: The 9 reference files are never checked.
claims.evidence: I appended 'You MUST ask at least three questions. Think step by step before answering.' to references/questions.md and ran build: validate says OK. No other check covers the references. The MCP self-lint (mcp/test/brief.test.ts:230-236) checks the server's own text and buildBrief({mode:'standard'}), and that brief holds the adapted universal method but no reference text (mcp/src/brief.ts:124-139).

claims.claim: The skill reads them in its first turn.
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:42: 'Read the reference files you need now, in this first turn'.

claims.claim: build.mjs copies them into the universal knowledge file and the MCP server.
claims.evidence: After the edit, grep finds the sentence once in universal/prompt-engine-knowledge.md and once in mcp/src/generated/content.ts (build.mjs:163-167 and :176-183).

claims.claim: CONTRIBUTING.md:48-50 says the guidelines apply to the references and that the validator flags pressure words.
claims.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:48: 'These apply to `SKILL.md`, the references and the universal prompt'. CONTRIBUTING.md:50: 'The validator flags capitalized pressure words such as MUST or NEVER'. .claude/CLAUDE.md:16 adds: 'Method text ... The validator enforces both'.

claims.claim: With backtick and double-quote stripping, only blueprint.md:56 is flagged on today's files.
claims.evidence: My probe of all selfCheck rules over SKILL.md, the core and the 9 references. Raw: blueprint.md:56 '(MUST, NEVER, CRITICAL)' and blueprint.md:99 '"think step by step"'. Stripped: blueprint.md:56 only.

claims.claim: The reviewer's loop over refFiles works when placed at line 121.
claims.evidence: refFiles is declared later, at validate.mjs:143. Placed at :121, the loop throws 'ReferenceError: Cannot access 'refFiles' before initialization' (tested). skillFiles, defined at :93, works.

findings.reproduction:
In a copy of HEAD: printf '\nYou MUST ask at least three questions. Think step by step before answering.\n' >> skills/prompt-engine/references/questions.md
node scripts/build.mjs → wrote the knowledge file, 2 history.jsonl and content.ts
node scripts/validate.mjs → 'validate: OK (10 skill files, 9967 chars in SKILL.md body, 5765 chars in universal core)'
grep -c 'You MUST ask at least three questions' → universal/prompt-engine-knowledge.md: 1; mcp/src/generated/content.ts: 1
selfCheck probe, raw: blueprint.md:56 'MUST', 'NEVER', 'CRITICAL'; blueprint.md:99 'think step by step'. Stripped: blueprint.md:56 only.
Reviewer's loop placed at :121 → ReferenceError: Cannot access 'refFiles' before initialization.
Two working variants, both using skillFiles:
  R (strip code spans and double quotes, reviewer): clean copy fails on blueprint.md:56; after backticking :56 it passes; the questions.md mutation gives 'MUST' and 'Think step by step' errors; 13/13 validate tests pass.
  B (strip code spans only): clean copy fails on :56 and :99; after backticking both it passes; same mutation results; 13/13 tests pass.
  Adding `End every prompt with the line "You MUST answer in JSON."` to SKILL.md: HEAD flags it; B flags it; R passes it ('validate: OK').
findings.refutation: I looked for a deliberate exclusion. plan.md:150-153 lists 'pressure words' and 'visible-reasoning wording, which the skill describes abstractly' without naming files. The commit that added the lint (124b72b) gives no reason for checking only two files. I looked for another check that lints the references and found none: the MCP test covers only the server's text and the universal method. The file is unchanged since 34d9caa. The text shipping today is clean, so this is a gap in a guard, not a live defect. I rate it minor, not major. The docs that claim the guard exists are wrong.

audit.reasoning:
validate.mjs:121 lints only SKILL.md and universal/prompt-engine.md. I appended 'You MUST ask at least three questions. Think step by step before answering. IMPORTANT: use a scratchpad.' to references/questions.md and ran build. validate says 'validate: OK'. The sentence then appears once each in the knowledge file, content.ts and two history.jsonl files.

No other check lints the references. The MCP self-lint (mcp/test/brief.test.ts:229-236) covers INSTRUCTIONS, the tool descriptions and buildBrief. buildBrief (brief.ts:124-139) contains no reference text.

The docs say this guard exists: CONTRIBUTING.md:48 and :50, and .claude/CLAUDE.md:16 ('The validator enforces both'). CLAUDE.md:9 counts references/ as part of the method.

plan.md:152-153 doesn't limit the lint to two files. The commit that added the list, 124b72b, gives no reason for the limit.

The skill reads its references in the first turn (SKILL.md:43), and blueprint.md every time (SKILL.md:45).

I probed every selfCheck rule for all matches. Today only blueprint.md:56 (MUST, NEVER, CRITICAL) and :99 ('think step by step') match, and both name the patterns to warn against them. So this is a gap in a guard, not wrong text shipping: minor. Unchanged since 34d9caa.
audit.checks_run:
- Read validate.mjs:115-148, CONTRIBUTING.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, plan.md:150-158, SKILL.md:40-50, brief.ts and brief.test.ts.
- Mutation in a copy, then build and validate, then grep of the generated files.
- Grepped mcp/test for selfCheck and LINT_RULES.
- My own probe (tools/probe17.mjs), with all matches, run raw, with code spans stripped, and with code spans and double quotes stripped.
- Variant copies:
  - the reviewer's loop at :121;
  - B, which strips code spans only;
  - R, which also strips double quotes.
- B with blueprint.md backticked: build, validate, validate and lint-rules tests, and the mutation.
- A double-quoted 'You MUST answer in JSON.' added to SKILL.md, run on HEAD, B and R.
- Grepped mcp/test and the eval graders for the blueprint wording.
- Checked the server-written adaptation text (brief.ts:67-93) against the selfCheck rules: no matches.
audit.evidence_errors:
1. The first-turn sentence is at SKILL.md:43, not :42, which is blank. SKILL.md:45 is the line that reads blueprint.md 'always'.
2. Missed: the server-written text in mcp/src/brief.ts:67-93 (FORMAT_A, MENU_SENTENCE and ASK_USER_NOTE) is served inside buildReference but isn't linted by either suite either. It is clean today.

Everything else reproduces, including the ReferenceError and the R-versus-B difference.
audit.fix_corrections:
1. Confirmed: placed at :121, the reviewer's loop throws "ReferenceError: Cannot access 'refFiles' before initialization". Use skillFiles instead.
2. Variant B, tested:
- The clean copy flags blueprint.md:56 and :99.
- With both backticked and the files rebuilt, validate is OK and the validate and lint-rules tests pass 28/28.
- The questions.md mutation reports 'MUST' and 'Think step by step'.
- Variant R misses a double-quoted MUST added to SKILL.md that HEAD catches.
3. If the MCP self-lint is later extended to buildReference and buildChecklist output, which would also cover the adaptation text, it needs the same code-span stripping, because it matches raw text and would flag a backticked `MUST`. The other way is for blueprint.md to name the patterns without the literal words.
4. Editing blueprint.md regenerates the knowledge file, content.ts and the 3 history.jsonl files. No MCP test or eval grader depends on those two lines (grep).

findings.fix_assessment: Right direction, but the fix as written has two problems. First, refFiles doesn't exist yet at line 121, so it crashes; skillFiles, which already holds SKILL.md and every reference, works. Second, stripping double-quoted text weakens today's check: a quoted pressure word in SKILL.md or the universal core, such as a line meant to be copied into produced prompts, would no longer be caught (tested). Stripping only code spans keeps the current strictness, at the cost of also backticking blueprint.md:99. Both variants pass the clean copy once blueprint.md is edited, catch the reference mutation, and pass 13/13 tests. Neither touches SKILL.md or the universal core, so no budget or contract string changes. build.mjs regenerates the knowledge file, content.ts and the three history.jsonl.
findings.proposed_fix:
scripts/validate.mjs:121-128: set `const INSTRUCTION_FILES = [...skillFiles.filter((f) => f.endsWith('.md')), 'universal/prompt-engine.md'];`. Add `const unquoted = (t) => t.replace(/`[^`\n]*`/g, ' ');` with the comment '// Text in `code spans` names a pattern, often to warn against it; it is not an instruction.' Then match against `unquoted(read(f))`.
skills/prompt-engine/references/blueprint.md:56 → '(`MUST`, `NEVER`, `CRITICAL`)'.
skills/prompt-engine/references/blueprint.md:99 → 'magic phrases (`think step by step`, `take a deep breath`)'.
Then run node scripts/build.mjs.
scripts/test/validate.test.mjs: add 'rejects capitalized pressure words in a reference file': append 'You MUST ...' to references/questions.md and expect /questions\.md: "MUST" \(pressure-words\)/.
CONTRIBUTING.md:50: say the validator checks SKILL.md, the references and the universal prompt, and that quoted examples of these patterns go in backticks.
owner_questions: Should the lint skip only `code spans`, or double-quoted text too? I recommend code spans only: it keeps today's check on SKILL.md and the universal core, and needs backticks at blueprint.md:56 and :99. Skipping double quotes as well, as the reviewer proposed, changes only :56, but quoted pressure words would then go uncaught in every file. The blueprint.md edit only changes quote marks. Is the step-3 full eval enough, or do you want those cases re-run in step 1d?

How should blueprint.md:56 and :99 name the patterns?
(a) In backticks, with a lint that skips code spans. This keeps today's strictness on SKILL.md and the universal core.
(b) Reworded without the literal words, as SKILL.md:74 and universal/prompt-engine.md:38 already do. This matches plan.md:152 ('which the skill describes abstractly') and needs no lint exemption, but the model loses concrete examples of what to remove.
Skipping double-quoted text, as the reviewer proposed, is not recommended.
Also: is the step-3 full eval enough after this edit, or should the affected cases be re-run in 1d?

left_for_later.part: The whole fix: lint all skill Markdown files with code spans skipped (D11), and backtick blueprint.md:56 and :99, in one commit
left_for_later.why:
Extending validate.mjs's selfCheck lint to the references fails validate on blueprint.md:56 ('MUST, NEVER, CRITICAL') and :99 ('think step by step') until those method lines change, and method text belongs to 1d. By the same rule as a grader that would fail today's correct method, the check lands with that method edit.
Spec:
(1) scripts/validate.mjs:121: `const INSTRUCTION_FILES = [...skillFiles.filter((f) => f.endsWith('.md')), 'universal/prompt-engine.md'];`. skillFiles is defined at :93; refFiles is declared later, at :143, and throws a ReferenceError at :121. Add the comment '// Text in `code spans` names a pattern, often to warn against it; it is not an instruction.' and `const unquoted = (t) => t.replace(/`[^`\n]*`/g, ' ');`, then match each selfCheck rule against unquoted(read(f)). Skip code spans only, not double-quoted text (D11): skipping quotes misses a quoted "MUST" in SKILL.md, which was tested.
(2) blueprint.md:56 becomes '(`MUST`, `NEVER`, `CRITICAL`)'; :99 becomes 'magic phrases (`think step by step`, `take a deep breath`)'.
(3) Run node scripts/build.mjs, which rewrites the knowledge file, content.ts and the histories.
(4) validate.test.mjs rows, in 19's table if it has landed:
- 'You MUST ...' appended to references/questions.md fails with /questions\.md: "MUST" \(pressure-words\)/;
- a backticked `MUST` in a reference passes;
- a double-quoted "MUST" in SKILL.md still fails.
(5) CONTRIBUTING.md:50: the validator checks SKILL.md, the references and the universal prompt, and quoted examples of these patterns go in backticks.
(6) Optional (audit fix_corrections 3, evidence_errors 2): extend mcp/test/brief.test.ts's self-lint at :230-236 to buildReference(name) for each REFERENCE_RESOURCES entry and buildChecklist(domain) for each DOMAINS entry, stripping code spans the same way. That also covers the server-written FORMAT_A, MENU_SENTENCE and ASK_USER_NOTE (mcp/src/brief.ts:68-93).
(7) blueprint.md is read in every run (SKILL.md:45). D11 left open whether step 3's full eval is enough, so 1d's cost-capped re-run (coordination[8]) covers it.
Prototypes: <scratch>/work/audit-scripts-validate/tools/patch17.mjs (variant B) and the f17-B-* copies in <scratch>/work/verify-scripts-validate/.

review_findings.problem: The batch made validate.mjs skip code spans in the universal core (D11). The MCP self-lint 'applies the self-check lint rules to the text the server adds' still matches buildBrief() raw, and buildBrief embeds universal/prompt-engine.md, so the two suites now disagree. A backticked pattern in the universal core passes validate and fails the MCP suite. The batch's notes_for_next_batches tell method-3-universal: 'The universal core is now linted with code spans skipped (D11) ... Name a pattern only inside backticks.' A batch 3 that follows that note in the universal core will break the MCP tests.
review_findings.outcome_evidence: brief.test.ts's self-lint of the text the server adds now strips code spans with a shared unquoted(), as validate.mjs does. Mutation checks: a backticked MUST in the core passes, and a bare MUST still fails.

review_findings.problem: Record part (6) extends the MCP self-lint so that it 'also covers the server-written FORMAT_A, MENU_SENTENCE and ASK_USER_NOTE' (audit evidence_errors 2). The new test's comment, commit 3722d8d's message and the report all say the served references carry the note before an unadapted reference. They don't today: adaptReference prepends ASK_USER_NOTE only when an adaptation misses or dialog wording is left over, and neither happens. So the note is never linted. FORMAT_A and MENU_SENTENCE are covered.
review_findings.outcome_evidence: The served-references self-lint now includes adaptReference('questions', ''), which returns only ASK_USER_NOTE, and asserts that it does. Mutation check: 'You MUST' in the note fails the test.

findings.title: A new reference file can ship only in the skill, because nothing checks KNOWLEDGE_ORDER
findings.summary: build.mjs builds the universal knowledge file and the MCP content only from the hard-coded KNOWLEDGE_ORDER list (build.mjs:54-57). validate.mjs checks that each reference is linked from SKILL.md (:141-148), but not that it's on that list. A new reference added without CONTRIBUTING step 3 ships in the skill but not in the universal or MCP formats, and every script check passes. Even with step 3 done, the MCP server won't serve a new domain unless its hard-coded domain lists are updated, and nothing checks that either.

claims.claim: The knowledge file and the MCP content are built only from KNOWLEDGE_ORDER.
claims.evidence: build.mjs:163-167 collects refs only for KNOWLEDGE_ORDER. renderKnowledge (:85, :88) and REFERENCES in content.ts (:99, :179) use only those refs.

claims.claim: validate checks that references are linked, not that they're in KNOWLEDGE_ORDER.
claims.evidence: validate.mjs:141-148. KNOWLEDGE_ORDER isn't even imported (validate.mjs:16).

claims.claim: If step 3 is skipped, the pack reaches Claude Code and claude.ai but not the universal prompt or the MCP server, and every check passes.
claims.evidence: Reproduced: validate OK (11 skill files), build --check up to date, script tests pass, and 0 hits in the knowledge file and content.ts. build left content.ts byte-identical, so the MCP suite gets the same input as before; I didn't run it.

claims.claim: New: even with step 3, the MCP server doesn't serve a new domain.
claims.evidence: mcp/src/brief.ts:10 hard-codes `DOMAINS = ['coding', 'writing', 'research', 'image-video', 'general']`. The same names are written out at brief.ts:112, server.ts:67 and server.ts:469. No MCP test compares REFERENCES with DOMAINS ∪ REFERENCE_RESOURCES; today all three are the same 9 names (checked). CONTRIBUTING.md:65 says 'If the MCP server lists domains by name', and it does.

claims.claim: The reviewer's reverse check reports a reference that's listed but missing.
claims.evidence: With research.md deleted, validate crashes with ENOENT inside buildAll (validate.mjs:216 → build.mjs:165) before printing anything. The message appears only with finding 21's buildAll guard (tested).

I checked whether some reference is meant to be skill-only: all 9 are in KNOWLEDGE_ORDER, and no doc describes skill-only references. The file is unchanged since 34d9caa. All references are listed today, so this is a guard gap that only bites when a contributor skips a documented step. I rate it minor, not major.

items.title: Isolate universal-test.mjs runs, check every turn's init event, and tighten the reply-line, no-draft and menu checks
commits: f84ddb9ae2
items.what_changed: scripts/eval/universal-test.mjs: each turn runs claude -p with --tools '', --safe-mode, --strict-mcp-config, --disallowedTools 'mcp__*', --output-format stream-json and --verbose. A new exported readTurn(stdout) parses the output line by line and skips lines that aren't JSON. It throws when there is no init event with tools and mcp_servers arrays, when there is no result event, or when the result has is_error (the message includes the subtype). It returns {...result, model, leaks}. The main loop is a pair of labelled for...of loops and checks every turn. A turn with leaks prints 'FAIL  <case> turn N: tools or MCP servers loaded: <list>; stopping' and breaks out of the whole run; a clean turn prints 'PASS ... no tools or MCP servers loaded (<model>)'. The unused replies array is gone. Checks: MENU is exactly the brief's regex, and a comment names its option prefix. 'ok reply line' is the strict contract string. 'no full prompt yet' rejects a fence, a heading, bold or plain 'Full prompt:' label, a score table or a menu. The header is rewritten (see 42b). The script now exports readTurn, MENU, STRUCTURE, QUESTIONS, ACCEPTED, DEEP_ROUND, CHANGED and CASES. The run sits in main() behind an entry guard that compares real paths (the same form as finding 13's fix), so importing the file starts no run. .claude/handoff/plan.md:187 now lists --disallowedTools "mcp__*" --output-format stream-json --verbose.
items.tests:
New scripts/test/universal-test.test.mjs, 16 tests, no model calls:
- the checks on synthetic replies (the 17 texts from u22-checks.mjs plus 5a's);
- readTurn unit tests;
- the script run against a fake claude, a node script serialized from a function. It refuses a call that lacks any isolation flag, has the wrong --system-prompt or the wrong --resume. PATH holds only the fake and a node symlink, so the real claude can't be reached. TMPDIR points into a folder that is removed afterwards. These tests are skipped on win32.

The fake-claude tests cover: a clean run (10 calls, exit 0); an MCP server at turn 1 (one FAIL, stops after 1 call); a tool loaded at turn 2 (stops after 2 calls, which shows every turn is checked); a failed check (exit 1, the run continues); and the guard (runs through a symlink in a folder with spaces, makes no call when imported). The test file imports the script with PATH set to an empty folder, so a broken guard can't reach the real claude.

Fails without the change: in scratch copies I undid each change on its own (M1-M16). Every one failed at least one test: old reply-line, no-draft and menu regexes; flags dropped; first result instead of last; is_error ignored; lists not required; first init only; leaks checked on turn 1 only; continue instead of stopping; a naive entry guard; no guard; HEAD's script; no r.error rethrow. With no guard or with HEAD's script, the import fails with the safe ENOENT path and nothing is billed.

Free replay on the saved live outputs that survive (1b/work/verify-evals-method-rule-coverage/replies): the menu check passes U1, U2 ('1) Done ★'), U5 and U6. U4 (Spanish) fails, as expected under D3. node --check passes.
items.deviations: 1) readTurn checks every init event in a turn's output, not only the first, and lists the leaks of all of them. It fails closed if Claude Code ever emits a second init. 2) turn() rethrows r.error, so a missing claude reports 'spawnSync claude ENOENT' instead of a bare Error. This came up while confirming that the import safety net works; it has its own test. 3) Without --out, the out folder is created only when needed; before, a folder was also created when --out was given. 4) The test design goes beyond the prototype: PATH holds only the fake and a node symlink (the prototype prepended to PATH, which could fall through to the real claude if the fake weren't executable), and TMPDIR is redirected. There are extra tests for leaks on later turns, failed checks, the guard, ENOENT, readTurn and the CASES table. 5) The brief's replay folder (scratchpad/live/universal) is empty now. U3 and U7 exist nowhere I could find, so the question-round checks were verified only on synthetic replies; U1, U2, U4, U5 and U6 came from the 1b replies folder.

review_findings.item: 22a (entry guard asked for in the batch summary); header line 15
review_findings.problem: The entry guard compares this file with process.argv[1]. Under node -e/--eval/-p, argv[1] is the first extra argument, not the entry script. Importing the checks the natural way, node --input-type=module -e 'const U = await import(process.argv[1]); ...' scripts/eval/universal-test.mjs, therefore runs main(). That starts the real, billed 10-turn suite (Sonnet, up to $0.50 per turn). The header says 'Importing this file starts no run', and the implementer's notes_for_next_batches tell batch 2 and 1d the same while asking them to import and replay the checks. The committed test only covers -e without arguments, so it can't catch this.
review_findings.outcome_evidence: Confirmed the misfire first: under node -e, argv[1] is the first extra argument (probe printed execArgv ['-e', ...] and argv[1] = the script path). The guard is now exported as isEntryPoint. It returns import.meta.main when Node sets it (22.18+ and 24.2+, per the Node ESM docs). Otherwise it returns false under -e, --eval, -p, -pe or --print (node accepts -pe but not -ep), and falls back to the real-path compare. The symlink and import test now also runs `--input-type=module -e 'await import(process.argv[1])' <script>` and expects no claude call. A new unit test covers the fallback on any Node. The new test file fails 4 tests on 0a4e098's script; the -e case's assertion message showed all 10 fake turns running. Dropping either branch fails the unit test. One mutation survives: ignoring import.meta.main at the call site, because the fallback covers every entry form tested on Node 24. The header claim 'Importing this file starts no run' is kept, since a test now covers this case.

review_findings.problem: 'recommendation marker' is has(/★/), and the strict 'ok reply line' at :70 requires 'Reply `ok` to accept every ★', which contains ★. Whenever the reply line passes, the ★ check passes too. A question round where no option is starred, which breaks the core's rule of ★ on the recommended option, passes every QUESTIONS and DEEP_ROUND check. This is the 'check can't fail on the break it is named for' problem that finding 22 is about. It isn't on 22a's list of checks to change, so route it to this batch or 1d.
review_findings.outcome_evidence: Confirmed the check could never fail: has(/★/) passed on any text that held the strict reply line. 'recommendation marker' now uses coding-vague 03's pattern: a ★ on an a)-d) option line. New test: an unstarred round fails it (also with a legend line), and the one-line and (a) forms pass. The DEEP_ROUND test now lists it for a full output. Reverting to has(/★/) or () => true fails 2 tests. Free replay: the universal U3 turn 1 and U7 rounds from the planners' corpus.json pass every QUESTIONS check, and fail only this one once their option stars are removed. All 8 recorded question rounds pass it.

review_findings.problem: The comment says 'The menu's first option: numbered or bulleted, one of the starred options ...', and the test is named 'a starred first option ... then Refine'. MENU puts Refine in a lookahead right after 'What next?' and finds the starred option anywhere after it. So it accepts menus whose starred option isn't first, or that list Refine before it. The regex follows the brief; only the description overstates what it pins. The commit message says 'first option' too.
review_findings.outcome_evidence: The MENU comment now says it finds a starred allowed option anywhere after 'What next?', with Refine anywhere after, and doesn't check that the option comes first. The test name is changed to match. The regex is unchanged, because the graders share its prefix.

findings.fix_assessment: Correct (tested). Two caveats. First, the regex rejects a CRLF line end ('### Score\r\n'), so land it after finding 16's normalization, or allow \r before the terminator. Second, the heading text must be followed by a colon or the end of the line. A future heading such as '### Score (0–5)' would therefore fail; that is the price of telling 'Score' apart from 'Score anchors', and the error message should say so. The message should also name a missing heading, not a missing string.
findings.proposed_fix:
scripts/validate.mjs, output-contract block (:150-157): add
```js
const esc = (s) => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
const headingRe = (h) => new RegExp(`(^|\\n)[ \\t]*(?:[-*]|\\d+\\.)?[ \\t]*(?:#{2,4}[ \\t]+${esc(h)}[ \\t]*(?::|\\n|$)|\\*\\*${esc(h)}\\*\\*)`);
```
Then check `g === 'headings' ? headingRe(s).test(t) : t.includes(s)`. For that group, use the error 'missing contract heading "X" (a ##–#### heading or a **bold** list label)'. Land it after finding 16's normalization.

findings.summary: True on this branch, but latent. scripts/version.mjs:67 hands the new frontmatter to String.replace as a replacement string, so $$, $&, $` and $' in the description or a metadata value get expanded. The current frontmatter contains no $, so nothing breaks today.

claims.claim: skill.replace(front[0], newFront) treats the new frontmatter as a replacement pattern, so $$, $&, $` and $' inside it are expanded.
claims.evidence: version.mjs:67: skill.replace(front[0], front[0].replace(…)). Unchanged since 7fb1b1a, which is before 34d9caa (git diff 34d9caa HEAD is empty).

claims.claim: The validator forbids $N and $ARGUMENTS but allows these sequences.
claims.evidence: validate.mjs:106-108 forbids only $ARGUMENTS, $ followed by a digit, ${CLAUDE_, !` and ```!. All four test descriptions passed validate before the bump. Side fact: validate.mjs:75 rejects only < and >, although .claude/CLAUDE.md says the description has no quotes either, so the $' case (which contains a quote) passes.

findings.title: Re-running a release fails before npm and the MCP Registry, so a failed publish can't be finished from CI
findings.summary: release.yml checks nothing before `gh release create` or `mcp-publisher publish`. Both refuse to publish the same tag or version twice, and GitHub re-runs a job from its first step. So once the GitHub release exists, every re-run fails at that step and can't reach npm or the registry. Nothing is lost: npm and the registry can still be published by hand (docs/publishing.md:20, :64).

claims.claim: Only the npm step checks whether its target already has this version.
claims.evidence: release.yml:44-48 is the only guard (npm view). The GitHub release step (:30-38) has none. The registry step (:54-69) waits for npm (:58-66) but never asks the registry. git log --follow shows one commit, 7fb1b1a, so the file is unchanged since 34d9caa.

claims.claim: `gh release create` with assets aborts when the tag already has a release.
claims.evidence: cli/cli create.go v2.89.0:499-506; v2.103.2:503-511 (the gh on ubuntu-latest: Ubuntu2404-Readme.md:112 'GitHub CLI 2.103.2', image 20261026.354.1); v2.103.3 (latest):503-511. All have `return fmt.Errorf("a release with the same tag name already exists: %s", opts.TagName)`. The check is a HEAD request to releases/tags/{tag} (http.go v2.89.0:144-166).

findings.refutation: Fixed after 34d9caa? No: the file has a single commit, 7fb1b1a. Does gh skip or overwrite an existing release? No: every version I read errors out (v2.89.0, v2.103.2 on the runner, v2.103.3 latest). Can a re-run start at a later step? No: GitHub re-runs whole jobs, and release.yml has one job and no workflow_dispatch. Is it a dead end? No. npm by hand (publishing.md:20) and the registry by hand (publishing.md:64) can finish a failed release. Deleting the GitHub release and re-running would also work, but that isn't documented. Nothing irreversible happens, so I rate this minor rather than major. A failure inside the release step itself doesn't block re-runs, because gh deletes its draft (create.go v2.89.0:533-541). The detail that a re-run after full success 'fails at the registry step' is off: it fails earlier, at the GitHub release step.

audit.reasoning: The defect is real at HEAD. release.yml is byte-identical to 34d9caa, and its only commit is 7fb1b1a. Only the npm step checks its target first (.github/pending-workflows/release.yml:45-48). The GitHub release step (:30-38) runs `gh release create` with assets. gh then refuses with 'a release with the same tag name already exists' (create.go:499-506 at v2.89.0, :503-511 at v2.103.2 and at v2.103.3). v2.103.2 is the gh on ubuntu-latest (runner-images Ubuntu2404-Readme.md:112). The registry rejects a duplicate version (registry_service.go:279-280 at v1.8.6, :301-302 at v1.8.7). mcp-publisher turns any non-2xx reply into an error (publish.go:149) and exits 1 (main.go:65). GitHub re-runs whole jobs, never single steps (github/docs re-run-workflows-and-jobs.md:4), and release.yml has one job. So once the GitHub release exists, every re-run stops at that step. One detail in the finding is wrong, as the verifier says: a re-run after a full success fails at the GitHub release step, not at the registry step. Nothing is lost. npm and the registry can be finished by hand (docs/publishing.md:20, :64). Deleting the GitHub release and re-running also works today, because immutable releases are off for this repo (API: enabled false). findings.title: The only CI path to npm (NPM_TOKEN) is scheduled to stop working in January 2027, and the trusted-publishing alternative needs a newer npm than Node 22 bundles
findings.summary: release.yml's only CI path to npm is the NPM_TOKEN secret, on Node 22, which bundles npm 10.9.x. npm's docs, checked today, say three things that publishing.md:19-22 leaves out: direct publishing with granular tokens ends in January 2027; a CI token needs Bypass 2FA, which is off by default; and trusted publishing needs npm 11.5.1 or later plus a package that already exists. Nothing user-facing breaks. Publishing by hand still works.
