owner_questions:
How should CI publish to npm?
(a) Trusted publishing with direct `npm publish`. Fully automatic; this is my recommendation.
(b) `npm stage publish`, approving each version with 2FA on npmjs.com. Safer, but the registry job would skip until you approve, so you'd run the registry publish by hand.
(c) Publish by hand every release and remove npm from the workflow.
Also, may I update plan.md:184? It still says first-publish trusted publishing is unverified, but npm's docs now say the package must exist first.

How should CI publish to npm?
(a) Trusted publishing with direct `npm publish`. It's fully automatic, but npm's own best-practice list says to allow only staging.
(b) Trusted publishing with `npm stage publish` only. You approve each version on npmjs.com with 2FA, then run the MCP Registry publish by hand.
(c) Publish by hand at every release, and remove npm from the workflow.
Also, may plan.md:184 be updated? npm's docs say a package must exist before you can add a trusted publisher, so the first publish can't use trusted publishing.

The reviewer's job split is the right fix. Only a separate job isolates credentials: scoping a secret to one step or setting `persist-credentials: false` doesn't, because steps in one job can read secrets from the Runner Worker's memory.

findings.proposed_fix:
In .github/pending-workflows/release.yml, put `permissions: {}` at the top and split the work into four jobs:
1. `build` (contents: read): checkout with `persist-credentials: false`; setup-node 22; in mcp/, npm ci, npm run build and npm test; then `node scripts/release.mjs --tag "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"`; then `npm pack --pack-destination ../dist` in mcp/; upload dist/ with actions/upload-artifact@v7 and `if-no-files-found: error`.
2. `github-release` (needs build; contents: write): download-artifact into dist/, then `gh release create` with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` and `GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}`. No checkout.
3. `npm` (needs build; contents: read, id-token: write): setup-node 24 with registry-url; download-artifact; `version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"`; keep the `npm view` skip; then `npm publish "dist/prompt-engine-mcp-${version}.tgz" --access public --ignore-scripts`.
4. `registry` (needs npm; contents: read, id-token: write): checkout with `persist-credentials: false`; setup-node 22; `sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6` (v4.1.2); the existing wait loop; download mcp-publisher v1.8.6 and its .sigstore.json and run `cosign verify-blob`; then login github-oidc and publish.

Update docs/publishing.md:24 to describe the per-job permissions, and :62 to describe the job order. Apply findings 25, 28 and 32 at the same time, since they edit the same file. Finding 32's `needs: ci` goes on `build`.

(2) `main` has no branch protection or rulesets. Do you want to protect it and limit who can push v* tags? Only you can change those settings.

findings.area: GitHub workflows (.github/pending-workflows: ci, release, evals, verify-data)
findings.title: The mcp-publisher binary is downloaded and run without any checksum or signature check, contrary to the registry's own instructions
findings.summary: release.yml:67-69 downloads mcp-publisher v1.8.6 and runs it with no hash or signature check. The job holds `contents: write` and `id-token: write`. The registry's own GitHub Actions guide verifies a Sigstore bundle before extracting. The registry's releases aren't immutable, so pinning the tag doesn't pin the bytes. The asset is unchanged today.

claims.claim: The binary is downloaded and run with no checksum or signature check.
claims.evidence: release.yml:67 `curl -fsSL "https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/releases/download/v1.8.6/mcp-publisher_linux_amd64.tar.gz" | tar xz mcp-publisher`; :68-69 run it. Unchanged since 7fb1b1a.

claims.claim: The job can mint OIDC tokens and holds a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN.
claims.evidence: release.yml:9-11 grant contents: write and id-token: write to the whole job. github/docs oidc.md:597-603 list ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL and ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN as variables 'on the runner'. actions/checkout v7 action.yml:52-54 sets persist-credentials to true by default, and README:33 says the token 'enables your scripts to run authenticated git commands'. main is unprotected: GET branches/main/protection returns 404 'Branch not protected', and rulesets is [].

claims.claim: Pinning v1.8.6 doesn't protect the asset, because release assets can be replaced.
claims.evidence: Every registry release from v1.8.0 to v1.8.7 reports "immutable": false. GitHub's immutable-releases doc (:22-23) says only immutable releases lock their tag and have assets that 'cannot be modified or deleted'.

claims.claim: The registry's GitHub Actions guide for this exact flow says to verify the download first.
claims.evidence: docs/modelcontextprotocol-io/github-actions.mdx:14-17 at v1.8.6 (identical at v1.8.7): 'The examples pin `mcp-publisher` to a specific release and verify its Sigstore bundle before extracting it.' The example at :64-83 uses sigstore/cosign-installer pinned by SHA (v4.1.2) and `cosign verify-blob`.

claims.claim: Today the v1.8.6 asset has SHA-256 1fbe93fc...e21340, which matches line 5 of registry_1.8.6_checksums.txt, and a .sigstore.json bundle exists.
claims.evidence: I downloaded the files today into a fresh folder and never ran them. shasum gives 1fbe93fc0783c2394d8012c8d6e50a59e98cb2cc2d216264cc69f405d0e21340; grep -n finds it on line 5. The API digest is the same, and the asset's updated_at (2026-10-27T14:47:24Z) is its upload time. The bundle (10,387 bytes) signs that same digest. Its certificate SAN is .../release.yml@refs/tags/v1.8.6, with issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com.

claims.claim: The Sigstore signature itself is valid.
claims.evidence: cosign isn't installed and I didn't install it. I read the bundle as data only.

Ubuntu2404-Readme.md doesn't mention cosign or sigstore, so cosign isn't preinstalled on the runner.
Fix test in my copy, under bash -e: a matching hash prints 'OK', then the stub publisher's login and publish run. A changed hash prints 'sha256sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match' and exits 1, and nothing is extracted. A synthetic archive stood in for the real one.
findings.refutation: Fixed after 34d9caa? No: release.yml is unchanged since 7fb1b1a. Do the v1.8.6 pin and HTTPS protect the bytes? No. HTTPS protects only the transfer, and the registry's releases aren't immutable, so anyone with write access to that repository can delete and re-upload an asset. Is the step unprivileged? No: the token is job-wide, checkout leaves it usable by later steps, and main is unprotected. Has the asset been tampered with? Not as of today: the file hash, checksums line 5, the API digest and the bundle digest all agree. I couldn't refute the finding. The likelihood is low, because it needs a compromise of the registry's releases. The impact is high: during a release, `contents: write` lets a swapped binary replace this repo's release assets, such as the .mcpb, or push to main. So I keep the severity at major. The manual path at publishing.md:64 has the same gap.

audit.reasoning: The defect is real at HEAD; release.yml is unchanged since 7fb1b1a. release.yml:67 pipes the v1.8.6 asset from curl straight into tar, and :68-69 run it. Nothing checks a hash or a signature. The whole job holds contents: write and id-token: write (:9-11). At the pinned tag, the registry's GitHub Actions guide says the examples 'verify its Sigstore bundle before extracting it' (docs/modelcontextprotocol-io/github-actions.mdx:14-17 at v1.8.6, identical at v1.8.7). That text arrived on 2026-10-24 (registry #1523), five days before release.yml was written (7fb1b1a, 2026-10-29). Every registry release from v1.7.8 to v1.8.7 reports immutable false, so pinning the tag doesn't pin the bytes. Nothing has been swapped so far. The asset I downloaded today hashes to 1fbe93fc...e21340, which matches line 5 of the checksums file, the API digest and the bundle's digest. One nuance: the registry's own quickstart still pipes curl into tar from releases/latest (quickstart.mdx:130 at v1.8.6). So 'contrary to the registry's own instructions' holds only for its CI guide, which is the one that applies here. The impact may be wider than the verifier says. Hosted runners have passwordless sudo (github/docs reference/runners/github-hosted-runners.md:77). The 2025 tj-actions/changed-files attack (CVE-2025-30066) read secrets out of the Runner.Worker process memory from a single step. So a swapped publisher could probably also reach NPM_TOKEN, which the npm step in the same job uses. I didn't test that. Major fits: low likelihood, high impact.
audit.checks_run: Read release.yml:9-11 and :67-69 and the git log. gh api: registry release list (immutable flags), v1.8.6 asset metadata (digest; created_at and updated_at both 2026-10-27T14:47:24Z), attestations for the digest (404), compare v1.8.6...v1.8.7 (163 files, none under cmd/publisher). Also read the commit history and text of github-actions.mdx at v1.8.6 and v1.8.7, quickstart.mdx at v1.8.6, and login.go (the token is kept in ~/.config/mcp-publisher/token.json). Also checked actions/checkout v7 action.yml:52-54 (persist-credentials true) and README:16 and :33, github/docs oidc.md:602-603, runner-images Ubuntu2404-Readme.md (no cosign), and this repo's immutable-releases setting (off). I downloaded the asset, checksums file and .sigstore.json into a fresh folder and never ran them. Hashing with shasum matched line 5. tar tzvf lists LICENSE, README.md and mcp-publisher. I read the bundle as JSON (python3 -I) and its certificate with openssl. The digest matches, the SAN is .../release.yml@refs/tags/v1.8.6, and the issuer is token.actions.githubusercontent.com. I could not check the signature itself because cosign isn't installed. I ran the proposed hash check under bash -e with sha256sum. The right hash prints OK and extracts mcp-publisher into the temp folder. A wrong hash prints 'did NOT match', exits 1 and extracts nothing. I also ran the proposed manual command `shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing registry_1.8.6_checksums.txt` with macOS shasum 6.02: OK, exit 0.
audit.evidence_errors: None that change the result. One nuance: actions/checkout v7 README:16 says v7 keeps credentials 'in a separate file under $RUNNER_TEMP instead of directly in .git/config', while README:33 still says the local git config. Either way later steps can use the token, as the verifier concludes. The verifier's impact analysis also leaves out secrets in runner memory (see reasoning).
audit.fix_corrections: 1. The hash-pin fix works as written; I tested it, and the archive member really is named mcp-publisher. 2. The optional `persist-credentials: false` only goes part way. With passwordless sudo, a swapped binary can still read tokens and secrets from the runner's memory. The real containment is running the registry publish in its own job with only `id-token: write`, which is finding 27's fix. Do 27 and 28 together. 3. The manual check proposed for publishing.md:64 uses the checksums file from the same release. As the verifier says, that catches a broken download, not a swapped one. It's still worth adding.

findings.fix_assessment: Correct. I prefer the hash variant: it pins the exact bytes, needs no new third-party action, and cosign isn't in the ubuntu-24.04 image. A cosign check binds to the tag name refs/tags/v1.8.6, and the tag of a non-immutable release can move. Small improvements: keep the version and the hash next to each other in env, and extract into $RUNNER_TEMP instead of the checkout. mcp-publisher's token lives in ~/.config/mcp-publisher (login.go:30-35), so the binary's location doesn't matter. Fix the manual path in publishing.md:64 too. v1.8.7 is now the latest release (2026-10-30). The registry diff from v1.8.6 to v1.8.7 touches 163 files, none in cmd/publisher, so staying on v1.8.6 looks fine; I didn't run it against the live registry. Checks in my copy: the hash check works under bash -e, and a mismatch stops the step before extraction.
findings.proposed_fix:
In the 'Publish to the MCP Registry' step of .github/pending-workflows/release.yml, add
  env:
    MCP_PUBLISHER_VERSION: v1.8.6
    # SHA-256 of mcp-publisher_linux_amd64.tar.gz in that release (line 5 of its checksums file). Update both together.
    MCP_PUBLISHER_SHA256: 1fbe93fc0783c2394d8012c8d6e50a59e98cb2cc2d216264cc69f405d0e21340
and replace lines 67-69 with
  archive="${RUNNER_TEMP}/mcp-publisher_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
  curl -fsSL -o "${archive}" "https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/releases/download/${MCP_PUBLISHER_VERSION}/mcp-publisher_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
  echo "${MCP_PUBLISHER_SHA256}  ${archive}" | sha256sum -c -
  tar xzf "${archive}" -C "${RUNNER_TEMP}" mcp-publisher
  "${RUNNER_TEMP}/mcp-publisher" login github-oidc
  "${RUNNER_TEMP}/mcp-publisher" publish
In docs/publishing.md:64, after 'download mcp-publisher', add: 'and check it against that release's checksums file: shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing registry_<version>_checksums.txt'. I tested that command on macOS. The checksums file comes from the same release, so it catches corruption, not a full swap; `cosign verify-blob` with the .sigstore.json bundle is stronger. Optional hardening, untested: set `persist-credentials: false` on the release job's checkout (the steps use GH_TOKEN, not git credentials), or move the registry publish into its own job with only `id-token: write`.
owner_questions: Should the publisher be pinned by its SHA-256 (simplest; pins the exact bytes; you update the hash with each version bump), or should the workflow copy the registry guide's cosign block, which adds the sigstore/cosign-installer action? I recommend the hash.

Should the workflow pin mcp-publisher by its SHA-256 (no new action; you update the hash with each version bump), or copy the registry guide's cosign block (adds the sigstore/cosign-installer action)? I recommend the hash.

findings.fix_assessment:

There are two problems:

findings.title: Dispatch inputs are pasted straight into the shell script, and the API key is exposed to the CLI install
findings.summary: evals.yml:32 pastes `${{ inputs.runs }}` and `${{ inputs.max_cost_usd }}` into the script text, in a step whose environment holds ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The `npm install -g` on line 30 also runs with that key set. In an emulation of GitHub's substitution, a crafted value ran its own command and dropped `--max-cost-usd`, and an ordinary "$5" reached the CLI as an empty ceiling. Only users with write access can start this workflow, and today that is only the owner.

claims.claim: The inputs are expanded into the script text before bash runs it, in a step whose environment holds ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
claims.evidence: evals.yml:27-28 set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for the whole step. evals.yml:32: `--runs "${{ inputs.runs }}" --max-cost-usd "${{ inputs.max_cost_usd }}"`. GitHub's script-injections.md:46: the expressions "are evaluated and then substituted with the resulting values, which can make it vulnerable to shell command injection."

claims.claim: A value such as `1" ; <command> ; echo "` runs arbitrary commands.
claims.evidence: In the emulation, the injected command wrote its marker file. The rest of the line, including `--max-cost-usd 5`, went into `echo`, so claude ran without the ceiling flag.

claims.claim: The inputs have no type, so typos pass unchecked.
claims.evidence: evals.yml:8-13 give only a description and a default. Some values change silently: a cost typed as "$10" reaches the CLI as "0", and "$5" as "", because bash expands $1 and $5 inside the double quotes. The plugin-eval docs (line 369) say the flag's default is "No ceiling". How the CLI treats an empty value is not checkable here.

claims.claim: Only users with write access can start the workflow, and GitHub notes they can already read the repository's secrets.
claims.evidence: data/reusables/repositories/permissions-statement-write.md, used by manually-run-a-workflow.md: "Write access to the repository is required to perform these steps." secure-use.md:33: "Any user with write access to your repository has read access to all secrets configured in your repository." Collaborators today: vipul-goel (admin) only. 0 secrets are configured.

claims.claim: The key is in the environment of `npm install -g`, whose postinstall (`node install.cjs`) doesn't need it.
claims.evidence: `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.312 scripts` shows postinstall "node install.cjs". I read install.cjs without running it: it copies the platform's native binary over bin/claude.exe and reads no ANTHROPIC variable. @anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64@2.1.312 has no lifecycle scripts. The same vendor's binary gets the key on the next line, so this part is hygiene rather than a real exposure.

Current file:
- evals.yml:8-13: inputs with only a description and a default.
- evals.yml:27-28: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}` for the whole step.

findings.refutation:
I tried the exploit angle. Starting the workflow needs write access, write users can already read secrets, and only the owner has access. So the injection gives nobody anything new today. That limits the severity, not the defect.

I checked whether the double quotes protect the values. They don't stop a `"` or a `$` (emulated).

I checked for a fix after 34d9caa: nothing under .github changed.

The install-time exposure is real but small, because the binary installed by the same packages receives the key next.

audit.reasoning:
evals.yml:32 pastes `${{ inputs.runs }}` and `${{ inputs.max_cost_usd }}` into the script text. evals.yml:27-28 put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in that step's environment, which includes the `npm install -g` on :30. GitHub names this pattern in script-injections.md:46. In my emulation, a crafted runs value ran its own command and dropped `--max-cost-usd`.

An attacker gains nothing from the injection. Only users with write access can start the workflow (manually-run-a-workflow.md:28), they can already read every secret (secure-use.md:33), and today that is only the owner.

The practical defect is accidental. A cost typed as "$5" reaches the CLI as an empty string, because bash expands $5. I read the pinned 2.1.312 binary's code without running it: `maxCostUsd:e.maxCostUsd?parseFloat(e.maxCostUsd):void 0`. An empty string counts as false, so the run gets no ceiling and the non-negative check is skipped. "$10" becomes "0", a ceiling of 0, so nothing starts and the run exits 2 (plugin-evals.md:402).

The key reaching the install is hygiene only. The package has no dependencies, and install.cjs reads no ANTHROPIC variable.

Nothing changed since 34d9caa. Minor.
audit.checks_run:
- Read evals.yml:1-40.
- Emulated GitHub's text substitution: took the run text with Ruby's YAML parser, replaced the expressions as text, and ran the result with `bash -e` against stub npm and claude commands.
  - The crafted runs value wrote its marker file, and claude got no --max-cost-usd.
  - "$5" reached the CLI as "", "$10" as "0", and "$(echo 9)" as "9".
  - The stub npm saw ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
- Downloaded @anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64@2.1.312 into its own folder, removed the execute bit, and searched the binary's embedded JS with Python. The flag is parsed as `maxCostUsd:e.maxCostUsd?parseFloat(e.maxCostUsd):void 0`. The non-negative check is `if(n.maxCostUsd!==void 0&&(...))`. Runs is parsed as `runs:e.runs?Fu(e.runs):void 0`, and the help text says its default is "case.runs ?? 3". No case.yaml sets runs. The installed 2.1.317 has the same cost-flag logic.
- Read the wrapper package @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.312 without running it: dependencies {}, and install.cjs only reads npm_config_omit.
- Claude Code docs (curl code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md): :369 gives "No ceiling" as the default, :383 says to pin both models, :402 gives exit 2.
- GitHub docs (github/docs 7fa55a0): script-injections.md:46; secure-use.md:33 and :67-69; manually-run-a-workflow.md:26-28; workflow-syntax.md:332-338.
- Ruby's YAML parser on the reviewer's one-line env gave Psych::SyntaxError. The verifier's fixed file, rebuilt from its proposed_fix, parses. With the env approach, crafted values reach the CLI literally, but a blank cost still reaches it as `--max-cost-usd ""`.
- GET requests: collaborators are vipul-goel (admin) only, and the repository has 0 Actions secrets.
audit.evidence_errors: "How the CLI treats an empty value is not checkable here" is wrong. It can be read from the pinned binary without running it. The code parses the cost only when the value is truthy and validates it only when it is defined, so "" means no ceiling. The same holds in the installed 2.1.317. That the option parser passes "" through as the value is my reading of the code; I didn't run it.
audit.fix_corrections:
The verifier's fix works as far as it goes. It parses, and crafted values and "$5" reach the CLI literally; "$5" then fails the CLI's own number check.

But a blank input still reaches the CLI as `--max-cost-usd ""` (tested), and the pinned CLI reads that as no ceiling. A blank runs value falls back to 3 runs per case and arm. A blank can come from `gh workflow run -f max_cost_usd=` or from a field the user cleared. Whether `type: number` or `required: true` stops a blank on GitHub's side is not checkable here.

So add `required: true` to both inputs, and make these the first lines of the run step:
  case "$RUNS" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "::error::runs must be a whole number"; exit 1;; esac
  case "$MAX_COST_USD" in ''|*[!0-9.]*) echo "::error::max_cost_usd must be a number such as 5"; exit 1;; esac
Keep the messages fixed; don't echo the raw input into a `::error::` line.

Tested with the stubs: "5" and "2.5" run. A blank, "$5" and a crafted runs value stop with exit 1, and nothing else runs. File: <scratch>/work/audit-workflows-other/sim30/evals-corrected.yml (Ruby parses it).

findings.fix_assessment:
The reviewer's direction is right, and it matches GitHub's advice to use an intermediate environment variable (secure-use.md:67-69). Tested in a copy: with the inputs passed through env and quoted, the crafted value and "$5" reach the CLI as literal arguments, nothing else runs, and the install step no longer sees the key.

One error: the reviewer's one-line `env: { ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ ... }}, RUNS: ..., MAX_COST_USD: ... }` is not valid YAML. Ruby's parser raises a SyntaxError, because `{` and `}` end plain values inside a flow mapping. Write the env as a block mapping.

Not checked: whether `type: number` makes GitHub reject non-numbers when the workflow is started, and how the CLI treats "", "0" or "$5". Running claude plugin eval is off-limits here.

Outside this finding: the CI section of the plugin-eval docs (line 383) also advises pinning both models, and evals.yml doesn't.
findings.proposed_fix:
In .github/pending-workflows/evals.yml (.github/workflows/ after step 2):

1. Inputs (lines 8-13): add `type: number` to both, with numeric defaults:
      max_cost_usd:
        description: Hard cost ceiling for the run, in USD
        type: number
        default: 5
      runs:
        description: Runs per case and arm
        type: number
        default: 1

2. Replace the "Run the eval suite" step (lines 26-33) with two steps. Write the env as a block mapping:
      - name: Install Claude Code
        run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.312
      - name: Run the eval suite
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          RUNS: ${{ inputs.runs }}
          MAX_COST_USD: ${{ inputs.max_cost_usd }}
        run: |
          claude plugin eval . --trust-plugin --no-publish \
            --runs "$RUNS" --max-cost-usd "$MAX_COST_USD" \
            --allow-tools Write Edit --scaffold -j 3 --json eval-results.json

findings.area: GitHub workflows (.github/pending-workflows: ci, release, evals, verify-data)
findings.title: GitHub switches the monthly check off after 60 quiet days, the same span after which entries count as stale
findings.summary: GitHub's docs say scheduled workflows in a public repository are switched off after 60 days without repository activity, and this repository is public. Entries go stale after the same 60 days. So when the re-verification commit is the last activity, the switch-off comes before the first run that would see stale entries, and the reminder never opens. docs/publishing.md:96-101 doesn't mention this.

claims.claim: In a public repository, GitHub disables scheduled workflows after 60 days with no repository activity.
claims.evidence: github/docs main (7fa55a0, 2026-11-02), events-that-trigger-workflows.md:967 and data/reusables/actions/scheduled-workflows-disabled.md: "In a public repository, scheduled workflows are automatically disabled when no repository activity has occurred in 60 days." `gh api repos/vipul-goel/prompt-engine` shows visibility public.

claims.claim: Entries count as stale after 60 days, so a quiet repository loses the reminder just when it's needed.
claims.evidence: verify-data.yml:27 uses `Date.now() - 60 * 864e5`. Say the entries were verified, and last committed, on 2026-10-29. They are stale from 2026-12-28, the workflow is switched off after 2026-12-28, and the first stale run (2027-01-03) never happens. If the last activity is later, for example a merge on 2026-11-10, the 2027-01-03 run comes first and opens the issue.

claims.claim: Nothing says so, and publishing.md:98 promises an issue once a month.
claims.evidence: docs/publishing.md:98: "opens an issue once a month when an entry ... hasn't been checked for 60 days". A git grep for inactiv, turned off, disabled and "60 days" in docs, README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG and .github finds no note about the switch-off.

claims.claim: What GitHub counts as repository activity, and whether it warns anyone before switching a workflow off.
claims.evidence: The GitHub pages I read neither define activity nor describe a warning. A web search found nothing either. Whether GitHub e-mails the owner is unverified.

audit.reasoning:
GitHub's docs say scheduled workflows in a public repository are switched off after 60 days without repository activity (events-that-trigger-workflows.md:967 and data/reusables/actions/scheduled-workflows-disabled.md). This repository is public. verify-data.yml:27 uses the same 60 days for staleness.

So when the re-verification commit is the last activity, the switch-off almost always comes before the first run that sees stale entries. Over two years of verification dates and four commit times, the issue never opened in 2,876 of 2,924 cases. It opens only when the 60th day falls on the 3rd and the commit came after 06:17 UTC. Any later activity, such as merging the PR, moves the switch-off and lets the issue open.

publishing.md:96-101 promises a monthly issue and says nothing about the switch-off.

A switched-off workflow can't just be run by hand. gh's `workflow run` offers only active workflows, and `gh workflow enable` lists the ones switched off for inactivity.

Confidence is medium. GitHub doesn't define "activity", and one 2026 user report says schedules kept running 70 to 120+ days after the last commit. The missing doc note is a defect either way; changing the schedule or window is the owner's call.

A doc note is the right minimum, but two parts of the reviewer's text are off.

findings.title: Any v* tag publishes without CI's checks and without confirming the commit is on main
findings.summary: On this branch, pushing the tag v<plugin version> runs release.yml from the tagged commit, merged or not. It publishes the GitHub release, npm (once NPM_TOKEN is set) and the MCP Registry, and npm and the registry never accept a version twice. It runs validate.mjs and the Node 22 MCP tests but skips the script tests, `claude plugin validate`, Node 20 and the Inspector gates, and nothing checks that the commit is on main or passed CI, although publishing.md:52 requires a merge first. release.mjs stops tags that don't match the version, and the workflows are parked, so the gap is latent until step 2.

claims.claim: The release job runs validate.mjs (through release.mjs) and the MCP tests on Node 22 only.
claims.evidence: release.yml:18-27: node-version 22, then npm ci, build and test. release.yml:28-29 call release.mjs, and release.mjs:30 runs validate.mjs, which also checks generated files (validate.mjs:215-217).

claims.claim: It skips `claude plugin validate . --strict`, the scripts/test suite, the Node 20 run and the Inspector gates.
claims.evidence: ci.yml has them: :24-25 script tests, :28-31 plugin validate, :39 node [20, 22], :51-53 test:inspector. release.yml has none of them. mcp/package.json:35-37 declares engines node >=20.

claims.claim: Nothing enforces publishing.md:52 ('Merge to main, then tag the merge commit').
claims.evidence: Neither release.yml nor release.mjs checks it. GET rulesets returns []. main returns 404 'Branch not protected'. The repo has no environments.

claims.claim: Any v* tag, including one on an unmerged or unreviewed commit, goes to npm and the registry.
claims.evidence: github/docs events-that-trigger-workflows.md (push): GITHUB_SHA is the 'Tip commit pushed to the ref', and push 'includes workflows that are not merged into the default branch'. But release.mjs:24-28 stops any tag that isn't v<plugin version> at that commit: v9.9.9 and v0.1.0-rc.1 both exit 1 in my copy. So 'any v* tag' is overstated. A tag on the version-bump branch head does publish.

claims.claim: Neither npm nor the registry lets you publish that version number again.
claims.evidence: npm/cli v12.2.1 docs npm-publish.md:59: 'that specific name and version combination can never be used again, even if it is removed with npm unpublish'. The registry rejects duplicates (v1.8.6 registry_service.go:279-280). A publisher can still mark a registry version deprecated or deleted (v1.8.7 handlers/v0/status.go:24, :82-84).

claims.claim: Fix: a compare status of `identical` or `behind` for main...SHA means the commit is on main.
claims.evidence: Tested today: compare/main...4ba0a01 (main) gives identical 0 0; compare/main...3956d22 (the pushed branch) gives ahead 31 0; compare/3956d22...main gives behind 0 31.

claims.claim: Fix: calling ci.yml as a local reusable workflow with `needs: ci` runs CI on the tagged commit.
claims.evidence: github/docs data/reusables/actions/reusable-workflow-calling-syntax.md: with a `./` reference, 'the called workflow is from the same commit as the caller workflow'. reusing-workflow-configurations.md:91: token permissions 'can be only downgraded (not elevated) by the called workflow'.

findings.refutation: Fixed after 34d9caa? No: release.yml and ci.yml are unchanged since 7fb1b1a. 'Any v* tag' is overstated, because release.mjs:24-28 stops tags that don't match the version. The realistic mistake remains: tagging the version-bump branch head. CLAUDE.md step 5 uses Squash and merge, so that head never lands on main. 'Without CI's checks' is partly overstated: validate.mjs, including the generated-file check, and the Node 22 tests do run. Only accounts with write access can push tags, which today means the owner. So this guards against mistakes, not attackers; someone with push access could also tag a commit whose release.yml lacks the check. An on-main check doesn't prove review either, because main has no protection. plan.md records no decision on release gating, and publishing.md:52 already states the policy the check would enforce, so I record this as confirmed (minor), with an owner question on how to gate.

audit.reasoning: The facts hold, but whether this is a defect depends on release policy. Facts I re-checked: release.yml runs on any v* tag push (:5-7). It uses Node 22 only (:20). It runs the MCP tests (:22-27) and release.mjs (:28-29), which runs validate.mjs (release.mjs:30), including the stale generated-file check (validate.mjs:215-217). It skips the script tests (ci.yml:24-25), `claude plugin validate` (ci.yml:28-31), Node 20 (ci.yml:39) and the Inspector gates (ci.yml:51-53). Nothing checks that the commit is on main: there are no rulesets, main is unprotected, and there are no environments. Two parts of the finding are overstated. 'Any v* tag' is wrong: release.mjs:24-28 stops any tag that isn't v<plugin version>. In my copy, v9.9.9, v0.1.0-rc.1 and v0.1 each exited 1 and wrote no dist/. 'Without CI's checks' is partly wrong: validate and the Node 22 tests do run. The script tests and `claude plugin validate` check the validator and the plugin, and the plugin ships from main, not from a release. Also, publishing.md:37-51 has the maintainer run the full list of checks before tagging, which the verifier didn't cite. What's left is a guard against mistakes. vipul-goel is the only collaborator, and CLAUDE.md step 5 and plan.md:188 have Claude ask before pushing any tag. plan.md records no decision on release gating. It did plan for release tooling to boot the packed server on Node 20 and 22 (plan.md:134), which nothing does today. Each remedy has a cost. An on-main check rules out a hotfix release from a branch. Re-running CI adds minutes and more ways for a release to be blocked: a flaky test, or a failed claude-code npm install. And 'on main' proves nothing about review while main is unprotected. Those are the owner's choices.

audit.fix_corrections: If the owner wants gating, the tested diff works: it parses, and I checked the on-main logic live, including the 'behind' case. Improvements: 1. Put the on-main check in its own small job that runs before `ci`, so a wrong tag fails in seconds, not after the full CI. 2. The compare API returns 404 for an annotated tag's object SHA. On git/git v2.47.0, the tag object SHA gives 404 and the tag name gives 'behind'. So if GITHUB_SHA held the tag object, the check would fail closed, never pass by mistake. Whether Actions sets GITHUB_SHA to the commit for annotated tags isn't checkable here; publishing.md:55 uses a lightweight tag. 3. Cheaper alternatives to re-running all of CI: require a successful CI run on GITHUB_SHA (untested), or add just the missing Node 20 test and Inspector gates to the release job. 4. If finding 27 splits release.yml into jobs, put the `needs:` on the first job. The `./.github/workflows/ci.yml` reference only works after step 2 moves the files, as the verifier says.

arbitration.rationale:
The two agents agree on every fact, and I re-checked each one myself. They disagree only on the label. I side with the verifier: confirmed, severity minor. The facts are certain. Where to draw the line between "confirmed" and "needs owner decision" is a judgment call, which is why my confidence is medium.

Why confirmed and not an owner decision:
1. The rule is already written down. publishing.md:52 says "Merge to `main`, then tag the merge commit." The owner-approved plan also wanted the release tooling to check "the packed entry booting on Node 20 and 22" (plan.md:134). The release only ever uses Node 22: release.yml:20 sets it, and pack-mcpb.mjs:75 starts the bundle with whatever Node is running.
2. The step with no guard can't be undone. npm never reuses a name and version, even after an unpublish. The registry rejects a version it already holds.
3. The smallest fix only enforces what publishing.md:52 already says: refuse a tag whose commit isn't on main. It sets no new policy. plan.md records no decision on release gating, and nothing in it conflicts with the fix. What remains for the owner is how far to go: re-run CI, protect main, or add an approval step. The verdict rules let a confirmed finding carry that kind of question.

The auditor's points make a mistake less likely: one collaborator, Claude asks before any tag (plan.md:188), and the local checks in publishing.md:37-51. They lower the severity. They don't close the gap.

What the finding overstates:
- "Any v* tag" is wrong. release.mjs:25-28 stops any tag that isn't v<plugin version>.
- "Without CI's checks" is only partly true. validate.mjs runs (release.mjs:30), including the version-sync check (validate.mjs:182-192) and the stale generated-file check (:215-217). The Node 22 MCP tests run twice, the second time through prepublishOnly (mcp/package.json:48).
- What's actually skipped: the script tests, `claude plugin validate`, Node 20 and the Inspector gates. Only Node 20 and the Inspector gates matter for the npm package. `claude plugin validate` mostly covers the plugin, which ships from main.
- "Goes to npm" only holds once NPM_TOKEN is set (release.yml:49-52), and the repo has no secrets today. A version can still be used up in the registry after a manual npm publish, the first option in publishing.md:20.

The real exposure is small. The workflows are parked, so nothing runs until step 2. Once they run, two plain mistakes get through:
- tagging the head of the version-bump branch. CLAUDE.md:64 says to use Squash and merge, so that commit never lands on main.
- tagging main while its CI is red, for example with Node 20 broken even though engines says >=20.

findings.fix_assessment: Correct, with two adjustments. First, give the calling `ci` job `permissions: contents: read`, and move the write permissions from the workflow level to the release job. The docs say a calling job without permissions passes the default token permissions; ci.yml's own `contents: read` would downgrade them anyway, so this is belt and braces. Second, `uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml` only resolves after step 2 moves the files out of .github/pending-workflows/. The ancestry check is sound: I tested the statuses live, and it fails closed when the API call fails. Putting it in its own job ahead of ci would fail faster, but that's optional. findings.proposed_fix:
Apply this with step 2 or after it. `./.github/workflows/ci.yml` only resolves once the files are in .github/workflows/.
1. ci.yml: add `workflow_call:` under `on:`.
2. release.yml: set the workflow-level `permissions:` to `contents: read`. Add two jobs before `release`, so a wrong tag fails in seconds:
   on-main:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - name: The tagged commit is on main
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
         run: |
           status="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/compare/main...${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq .status)"
           case "${status}" in
             identical|behind) ;;
             *) echo "::error::${GITHUB_REF_NAME} (${GITHUB_SHA}) is not on main (compare status: ${status})"; exit 1;;
           esac
   ci:
     needs: on-main
     uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

owner_questions: Should every release require the tagged commit to be on main? That rules out a hotfix release from a branch. Should the full CI run again inside the release? That adds several minutes, and a flaky test blocks the release until you re-run it. Optionally, a protected 'release' environment with you as the required reviewer would pause each publish for your approval. Since main is unprotected, 'on main' doesn't mean reviewed: do you also want branch protection on main?

Should the release workflow enforce the release rules in publishing.md? (a) Refuse a tag whose commit isn't on main. This is cheap, but rules out releasing a hotfix from a branch. (b) Re-run the full CI (Node 20, the Inspector gates, plugin validate) before publishing. This adds a few minutes, and a flaky test or a failed claude-code install would block the release until you re-run it. (c) Since main is unprotected, do you also want branch protection, so that 'on main' means reviewed? I recommend (a) now; (b), or just a Node 20 step, is optional.

1. Should every release re-run the full CI on the tagged commit first? It adds a few minutes, and the release then depends on the claude-code npm install. A flaky failure stops the run before anything is published, and "Re-run failed jobs" re-runs only the failed jobs and the jobs after them, on the same commit. The cheaper choice is to trust main's CI and only check that the commit is on main, but that would still publish a tag on a main commit whose CI failed.
2. Will you ever want to release a hotfix from a branch? The on-main check forbids it, as publishing.md:52 already does on paper.
3. Optional: do you want branch protection with required checks on main, so that "on main" also means CI passed? Do you want each publish to wait for your approval in a protected "release" environment?

findings.title: 'Don't install it twice' describes the wrong duplicate, misses the real ones and gives no way out
findings.summary: README.md:48 and docs/install.md:3 say that adding the plugin on Claude.ai and in Claude Code gives two copies. Claude Code's docs and the 2.1.317 binary say otherwise: the local copy loads, and the Claude.ai copy is listed as not loaded. The docs do enable real overlaps they never mention. A skill zip uploaded on Claude.ai also syncs into Claude Code and loads next to the plugin. Copilot in VS Code and Cursor read Claude's skill folders as well as `~/.agents/skills/`. And `npx skills add` installs into Claude Code without asking when it's the only agent found, or with `-y`. No doc says how to remove a copy. Confidence is medium because all of this comes from vendor docs and code; I couldn't run a claude.ai sync here.

claims.claim: The README's example (Claude.ai plugin plus Claude Code plugin gives two copies) is wrong.
claims.evidence: code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md, "Name conflicts", item 5: "When an enabled plugin from any other origin matches its name, Claude Code loads that plugin and reports the synced copy as not loaded. To use the claude.ai copy instead, disable your own copy." The Claude Code 2.1.317 binary contains `Synced plugin "…" shadowed by local copy …`, which marks the synced copy "dropped". The rule compares manifest names, and both copies are named "prompt-engine" (.claude-plugin/plugin.json; the marketplace entry is also "prompt-engine").

claims.claim: The Claude.ai copy is then silently unused.
claims.evidence: It is reported, not silent. The 2.1.317 binary shows a /plugin row: `"…" from claude.ai not loaded — "…" on this machine has the same name and takes precedence`. It also gives a hint: "To use the claude.ai copy instead, run `claude plugin enable …`, then disable or remove …".

claims.claim: Claude.ai plugin plus the uploaded skill zip gives two copies on Claude.ai.
claims.evidence: claude.com/docs/skills/overview.md says "A plugin's skills appear on Your skills too, labeled with the plugin's name", but no doc covers a same-name upload. docs/manual-checks.md:72 expects two copies, but that check hasn't been run, and testing it needs a Claude.ai account.

claims.claim: (Extra overlap the finding missed) The uploaded zip also syncs into Claude Code and loads next to the plugin.
claims.evidence: code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md, "Skills synced from claude.ai": synced skills "include the ones you create or turn on in your claude.ai settings". The same page's "Resolve skills that share a name" table says: "A plugin skill and a skill at any of the locations above | Both load, because plugin skills are namespaced". This applies when Claude Code signs in with the same claude.ai account. Untested here.

claims.claim: The plugin plus the .mcpb bundle overlap in Claude Desktop.
claims.evidence: Both are offered for Claude Desktop: README.md:42 says "web, desktop, mobile", and README.md:45 offers the ".mcpb file for Claude Desktop". claude.com/docs/plugins/platform-support.md says plugin skills load in chat, which includes "the Claude desktop app". claude.com/docs/connectors/custom/add-unlisted.md says a .mcpb "runs on your device inside Claude Desktop". mcp/README.md:26 warns about this overlap only for Claude Code. Whether having both causes a visible problem is untested.

claims.claim: Copilot reads both Claude's skill folders and ~/.agents/skills.
claims.evidence: VS Code's docs (code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/agent-skills) list personal "~/.copilot/skills/, ~/.claude/skills/, ~/.agents/skills/" and project ".github/skills/, .claude/skills/, .agents/skills/". They also say: "If another supported location contains a skill with the same name, both skills appear on the Skills page." GitHub's docs list project `.claude/skills` and personal `~/.agents/skills`. Cursor's docs show the same overlap, with no documented rule for same-named skills. I checked vendor docs, not copilot-language-server 1.564.0 itself.

claims.claim: `npx skills add` auto-detects Claude Code.
claims.evidence: skills 1.7.6 (latest; I downloaded it with npm pack and only read it), docs/agents.md:89: "The CLI automatically detects which coding agents you have installed." In dist/cli.mjs, Claude Code counts as installed when `existsSync(claudeHome)` is true, i.e. when ~/.claude exists. runAdd has `else if (installedAgents.length === 1 || options.yes) { targetAgents = ensureUniversalAgents(installedAgents)`, which installs with no prompt. With no agent detected, the prompt preselects "claude-code". `-a` sets the target list exactly.

findings.refutation: I looked for ways the README could still be right. Synced plugins need a claude.ai sign-in and Claude Code 2.1.273 or later, and the docs don't say when the name-conflict rule arrived, so an older client might load both copies. That isn't checkable here, and 2.1.317 drops the synced copy. The advice "don't install twice" is still sound, so the harm is a wrong reason plus missing guidance, not bad advice. plan.md:136 asks for a "don't install twice" note; the fix keeps such a note, so there's no conflict. The finding's word "silently" is wrong. Nothing here changed since 34d9caa.

audit.reasoning:
The note's example is imprecise, and the overlaps where both copies really load are missing.

**The example.** Claude Code's docs (plugins/loading.md, "Name conflicts", item 5) say a same-named local plugin loads and the synced claude.ai copy is reported as not loaded. The code agrees. In the 2.1.317 binary, the synced copy is marked "dropped" with the message `Synced plugin "…" shadowed by local copy`. I also read the 2.1.273 binary from npm. 2.1.273 is the first version that syncs, per the docs, and it has the same rule. So no syncing version loads both copies. README.md:48 is literally true that two copies get installed and listed, but it implies two working copies.

**The missed overlaps:**
- A skill zip uploaded on claude.ai also syncs into Claude Code and loads next to the plugin. skills.md's last same-name row says the synced skill "is then listed and runs only under its full name".
- `npx skills add` writes `.claude/skills/prompt-engine` next to the plugin. The skills.md row for a plugin skill and a local skill says "Both load". skills 1.7.6 installs into Claude Code without asking when `~/.claude` is the only agent it finds, or with -y.
- Cursor and VS Code's local sessions read both `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`.
- The plugin and the .mcpb bundle both run in Claude Desktop chat. README.md:42 and :45 offer both.

**No way out.** No doc says how to remove a copy; manual-checks.md:72 only says "remove one".

This is not an owner decision: plan.md:136 asks for a "don't install twice" note, and the fix keeps one. Severity is minor, because the advice itself is still right. Medium confidence: everything comes from vendor docs and code; no app was run.

Ran strings on ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.317 and on @anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64@2.1.273 (from npm pack, read only). The help text in 2.1.317 lists `plugin enable <plugin>`, `plugin disable [plugin]` and `plugin uninstall <plugin>`. Ran npm pack skills@latest (1.7.6) and read dist/cli.mjs: claude-code detection (:1590-1598), runAdd (:5207-5236), selectAgentsInteractive (:4958), promptForAgents (:4925) and the canonical-folder logic (:2291-2298). Read .claude-plugin/*.json: both names are "prompt-engine". Applied corrected text in scratch: checks unchanged, all links and anchors resolve.

2. Claim 1 ("holds") overstates. Two copies are installed and listed in /plugin; only one loads.
3. For the zip-sync overlap, the cited row ("A plugin skill and a skill at any of the locations above | Both load") doesn't cover synced skills. The right row is the last one ("…the short name of a skill synced from your claude.ai account"). The conclusion is the same.
4. VS Code's page moved to code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills. It documents `~/.claude/skills` for "Local" sessions. Its per-harness table lists only `.github/skills/` and `~/.copilot/skills/` for the Copilot harness ("not every directory it recognizes").

Append this section to docs/install.md:

"## Install it once" — Some options reach more than one app, so a second install can give you two copies:
- **Claude.ai plugin and Claude Code plugin.** A plugin you add on Claude.ai also loads in Claude Code as `prompt-engine@synced` when you sign in there with that Claude.ai account. findings.title: Docs tell users to run `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp`, a package name nobody has published yet
findings.summary: The docs tell users to run `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp`: README.md:45, docs/install.md:103 and seven lines in mcp/README.md. That name is still unpublished on npm (E404 on 2026-11-03), and the repository is public. Whoever publishes it first controls what the documented command runs, and could also block the owner's own npm and MCP Registry publish. The exposure today is small: `main` holds only a stub README, GitHub code search indexes only the default branch, and the repo has 0 stars and 0 forks. It becomes real when this branch merges to `main`.

claims.claim: The npm name is still free.
claims.evidence: `npm view prompt-engine-mcp` returns E404, and `curl https://registry.npmjs.org/prompt-engine-mcp` returns 404. Variants that differ only in punctuation (promptenginemcp, prompt_engine_mcp, prompt.engine.mcp, promptengine-mcp, prompt-enginemcp) all return 404, so npm's similar-name rule won't block the owner. `prompt-engine` exists, but it's an unrelated 2022 library.

claims.claim: The repository is public.
claims.evidence: `gh api repos/vipul-goel/prompt-engine` returns "visibility":"public".

claims.claim: The docs tell users to run `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp`.
claims.evidence: README.md:45, docs/install.md:103, docs/publishing.md:71, and mcp/README.md:23, :33, :43, :48, :120 and :142. The finding named only the first two, plus publishing.md:19.

claims.claim: `-y` skips npx's install prompt.
claims.evidence: npm 11.19.0's npm-exec.md:28 says the prompt "can be suppressed by providing either `--yes` or `--no`". But :29 adds: "When standard input is not a TTY or a CI environment is detected, `--yes` is assumed." MCP clients start stdio servers over pipes, so dropping `-y` wouldn't protect them. It matters only for terminal runs such as `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp --http`.

claims.claim: The "after the first release" caveat is easy to miss.
claims.evidence: In README.md the caveat sits at :48, after the table. docs/install.md:103 puts it in the same sentence, and mcp/README.md:16 puts it at the top of Install. Either way, a caveat doesn't stop someone else claiming the name.

claims.claim: A squatter would control the command and could block the owner's release.
claims.evidence: mcp/server.json "packages" registers npm identifier "prompt-engine-mcp" 0.1.0, and plan.md:38 says the registry needs mcpName to match. If someone else owns the name, the owner can't publish there, and the registry entry fails.

claims.claim: How exposed it is today.
claims.evidence: `main` is "Initial commit" 4ba0a01, and its README is just "# prompt-engine". GitHub's code search docs say "Only the *default branch* is indexed for code search." The repo has stars 0, forks 0, watchers 0.

findings.reproduction:
$ npm view prompt-engine-mcp

$ for n in promptenginemcp prompt_engine_mcp prompt.engine.mcp promptengine-mcp prompt-enginemcp; do curl … registry.npmjs.org/$n; done
404 for each
$ gh api repos/vipul-goel/prompt-engine --jq '{visibility, default_branch}'
{"default_branch":"main","visibility":"public"}
$ gh api repos/vipul-goel/prompt-engine/branches/main --jq .commit.commit.message
Initial commit
$ git grep -n "npx -y prompt-engine-mcp\|\"-y\", \"prompt-engine-mcp\""

$ grep -n "assumed" $(npm root -g)/npm/docs/content/commands/npm-exec.md

$ curl docs.github.com …/about-github-code-search
"Only the *default branch* is indexed for code search."
findings.refutation: The caveats at README.md:48, install.md:103 and mcp/README.md:16 tell users the package isn't out yet. They don't stop a squatter, though, and after a squat the command would simply work, running someone else's code. Today's exposure is limited, because the docs aren't on `main` and code search can't find them, which lowers the urgency but doesn't remove the defect. The lines are unchanged since 34d9caa (mcp/README.md had the same commands then, at :23, :113 and :127).

audit.reasoning:
**The name is still free.** npm returns E404, the registry returns 404, and the punctuation variants also return 404. The docs give `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp` at:
- README.md:45
- docs/install.md:103
- docs/publishing.md:71
- mcp/README.md:23, :33, :43, :48, :120 and :142
All of these were present at 34d9caa.

**`-y` doesn't matter for MCP clients.** npm's libnpmexec skips the install prompt when stdin isn't a TTY (index.js:298, no-tty.js).

**The exposure exists today, not only after merge.** The pushed branch (tip 3956d22) is public. Its docs/publishing.md:19 says the name "was unclaimed", and its .claude/handoff/repo-review-partial.json calls it "a package name nobody has published yet". Discoverability is low: 0 stars, 0 forks, and code search covers only the default branch.

**The release workflow would not catch a squat.** The parked release.yml:45-47 treats any existing version as already published ("already on npm", exit 0), without checking who published it.

The fix needs the owner's npm account (.claude/CLAUDE.md step 5), so this is confirmed with an owner question.
audit.checks_run: Ran `npm view prompt-engine-mcp` and curl against registry.npmjs.org for the name and five variants (all 404; `prompt-engine` is an unrelated 2021 package). `gh api` GET calls on the repo: visibility public, stars 0. Branches: main is "Initial commit" 4ba0a01, and the branch tip is 3956d22. Fetched publishing.md and the review file from the public branch. Ran git grep at HEAD and at 34d9caa. Read .github/pending-workflows/release.yml, mcp/server.json and mcp/package.json. Read npm 11.19.0's npm-exec.md:28-29 and libnpmexec/lib/index.js:288-310. Fetched GitHub's about-github-code-search page. Ran `npm view prompt-engine@0.0.31 _npmUser` to confirm the publisher field exists.
audit.evidence_errors:
1. "It becomes real when this branch merges to main" understates the risk. The public branch already names the package and says it is unclaimed.
2. The code-search quote isn't on the page as quoted. The page says "We currently only support searching for code on the default branch of a repository." The meaning is the same.
audit.fix_corrections:
1. npm never lets a version be reused. Publishing 0.1.0 early from the branch would freeze 0.1.0 at that code, and release.yml:45-47 would then skip publishing the tagged code. Either publish 0.1.0 from the exact commit that will be tagged, with no later mcp/ changes, or claim the name now with a lower version such as 0.0.1.
2. Add a publisher check at release.yml:45-47. For example, `npm view "prompt-engine-mcp@${version}" _npmUser` must name the owner's npm account, or the step fails; then the registry step (:59-69) doesn't run either. Inference, not tested: if a squatter copied the public mcpName, the registry's mcpName check (:57) could pass and point the owner's entry at their code.
3. In publishing.md, drop "before the docs reach main". Say to claim the name now, because the public branch already names it.
4. The fallback at mcp/README.md:33, :43 and :48 is JSON or the Windows `cmd /c` form. Those lines need `"command": "node", "args": ["/path/to/prompt-engine/mcp/dist/cli.js"]` plus a build step first, not a text substitution.

findings.fix_assessment: The reviewer's main remedy is right and closes the risk: claim the name before merge by publishing 0.1.0 by hand, as docs/publishing.md:20 describes. That fits publishing.md:20 ("Do this before you push the tag") and the release workflow's skip-if-published step. It needs the owner, because npm isn't logged in on this Mac and CLAUDE.md step 5 says to ask before publishing. The reviewer's fallback undercounts: replacing the command means eight edits across three files, not two. Dropping `-y` alone would not help. I tested the publishing.md wording in a scratch copy, and the checks didn't change.
findings.proposed_fix:
1. The owner publishes `prompt-engine-mcp` 0.1.0 before the PR to `main` merges. From a clean checkout: `npm login`, then `cd mcp && npm ci && npm publish --access public`. Then confirm with `npm view prompt-engine-mcp`.
2. docs/publishing.md:19: after "was unclaimed when this was written." add: "Claim it before the docs that tell users to run `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp` reach `main`: until then, anyone can publish a package under that name."
3. CLAUDE.md step 5: add a pre-merge check that `npm view prompt-engine-mcp` shows the owner's package.
4. Only if the owner merges first: replace `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp` with `node /path/to/prompt-engine/mcp/dist/cli.js` at README.md:45, docs/install.md:103 and mcp/README.md:23, :33, :43, :48, :120 and :142 until the package exists.
owner_questions: Will you publish `prompt-engine-mcp` to npm yourself before the PR to `main` merges? That needs `npm login` on your Mac, or an NPM_TOKEN secret. Or should the docs switch to the from-clone command until the first release?

Will you claim `prompt-engine-mcp` on npm now (it needs `npm login` on your Mac)? If yes, should it be 0.1.0 from the final PR head right before merge, or a placeholder such as 0.0.1 now? Or should the docs use the from-clone command until the first release?

findings.title: The privacy note implies the MCP server never sees your prompt, but check_prompt and ask_user do, and hosting isn't covered
findings.summary: README.md:101 is literally true: `enhance_prompt` takes only mode and target. But `check_prompt` receives the draft enhanced prompt, and `ask_user` receives the questions and, when a form is shown, the user's answers and notes. Run locally, all of that stays on the machine. On a server someone else hosts, it passes through that server, and neither README says so; mcp/README.md:172 also leaves out `ask_user`. The claims about logging and outbound calls hold.

claims.claim: `enhance_prompt` doesn't receive the prompt.
claims.evidence: mcp/src/server.ts:120-123 has EnhanceInput = { mode?, target? }, and :345 is `async ({ mode, target }) => text(buildBrief(...))`.

claims.claim: `check_prompt` receives the full draft.
claims.evidence: mcp/src/server.ts:179: `prompt: z.string()…describe('The draft enhanced prompt (the full prompt, not the whole reply).')`, used by the handler at :402-403. mcp/src/brief.ts:115 tells the model to "Optionally call check_prompt on your draft full prompt". This was the same at 34d9caa (server.ts:148 there).

claims.claim: `ask_user` carries the questions and the user's answers.
claims.evidence: There's a nuance: answers reach the server only in form mode. mcp/src/server.ts:371-373 reads `inputResponse(ctx.mcpReq.inputResponses, FORM_KEY)` and then `mapFormAnswers(questions, response.content)`, and notes can be up to 1,000 characters (questions.ts:12). In text mode the server only returns questionsText, and the user's reply goes to the model.

claims.claim: The README offers a hosted HTTP mode.

findings.refutation: The sentence is literally true, which is why I rate this minor. What misleads is the "doesn't even" implication, and it matters exactly in the hosted case, where `check_prompt` and form-mode `ask_user` send user content to the host. audit.reasoning:
README.md:101 says "Its main tool doesn't even receive your prompt text." That is literally true: `enhance_prompt` takes only mode and target (mcp/src/server.ts:120-123, handler at :345). But the other tools do receive user content:
- `check_prompt` takes the full draft (server.ts:179, handler at :402), and mcp/src/brief.ts:115 invites the model to call it.
- `ask_user` receives the questions. In form mode, the user's answers and notes (up to 1,000 characters, mcp/src/questions.ts:12) come back to the server (server.ts:371-373).

Run locally, this is harmless. On a hosted copy (mcp/README.md:117-166; docs/publishing.md:15 and :85-87), those inputs reach the host, and neither README says so. mcp/README.md:172 also leaves out ask_user.

The logging and no-outbound-call claims hold. mcp/src/log.ts:15-44 keeps request text out of log lines. Every CLI log line either goes through describeError (cli.ts:104, :141, :181) or is the usage message (:74). worker.ts:37-38 logs only the ALLOWED_HOSTS warnings, and wrangler.jsonc:8 turns observability off. The SDK's own console calls are registration warnings. There are no outbound calls in mcp/src.

findings.title: Test-status claims don't match the recorded evidence: missing trigger set, in-sample score, wrong re-run row, install source
findings.summary: Confirmed on this branch. No commit contains the 24-request trigger set that CHANGELOG.md:31 and README.md:82 present. By compatibility.md's own numbers, its held-out sentence (:56) gives no evidence for the shipped description. The Claude Code row (:15) was tested from the feature branch, and the documented unpinned command fails today. The re-run row's cost and without-skill figures (:40) can't be re-checked on this Mac.

claims.claim: (a) CHANGELOG and README present a 24-request trigger set that isn't in the repository.
claims.evidence: CHANGELOG.md:31 'trigger tests for the skill description (24 requests…)' sits under '### Added' (:11). README.md:82 says '24 requests, half of them near-misses'. git ls-files finds only 3 trigger eval cases. Across every commit, 'should_trigger' appears only in .claude/handoff/repo-review-partial.json. compatibility.md:51,53 name at most 6 requests plus the 'prompt-engine:' class. .claude/CLAUDE.md:62 tells sessions to re-run the trigger tests from 'the eval set … described in docs/compatibility.md'. That can't be done.

claims.claim: (b) compatibility.md:56 is garbled and suggests the shipped description was validated on held-out requests.
claims.evidence: The sentence says the first description 'never saw' 8 requests 'during tuning', but the first description was never tuned. By :53 (21/24) and :56 (all 8 held-out passed), its 3 misses were among the 16 tuning requests, so the whole 21-to-24 gain is in-sample. skill-creator run_loop.py on this Mac holds out int(12*0.4)=4 per class (:37-38, :254) and picks best by test score only (:218). Python's max keeps the first tie (my check printed 1). So an original at 8/8 would itself be the loop's best_description. The shipped description (55a5b2b, unchanged since) differs from the original.

claims.claim: (b) The shipped description was hand-written (candB.json) after all 24 results were seen, and the loop's final description differs from it.
claims.evidence: None of the tuning files (desc-tune, eval-set.json, candB.json) are on this Mac. The claim is consistent with the selection-rule point above.

claims.claim: (c) The re-run row should read 6 cases, 6/6, without-skill 1/3 (mean 0.67), $0.68.
claims.evidence: evals/results/ doesn't exist on this Mac. The 998e0c8 message says 'the 5 affected cases now pass', which supports the row's 5. If the total was $0.685, the row's $0.69 is normal rounding and the reviewer's $0.68 is not. In 2.1.317, `claude plugin eval --help` says --ablation defaults to 'with-without', so the row's '—' means the run used --ablation none or the data was dropped. No record shows which.

claims.claim: (d) The interactive test installed from the feature branch, and the documented command can't work yet.

audit.reasoning:
Confirmed. Parts (a) and (b) hold on HEAD. Part (c) can't be checked on this Mac. Part (d) has the right facts, but the row's wording isn't false.

(a) Holds. CHANGELOG.md:31 lists "trigger tests for the skill description (24 requests…)" under "### Added" (:11), next to things that are in the repo (17 eval cases, the two-turn test). No commit has the set: across all 33 commits, `should_trigger` appears only in .claude/handoff/repo-review-partial.json. git ls-files finds only the 3 trigger eval cases. evals/results/ doesn't exist, and no ignored file holds the set. compatibility.md:51 and :53 name 6 requests plus the "prompt-engine:" class, so the instruction at .claude/CLAUDE.md:62 can't be followed.
- Partial refutation: plan.md:139 says to run run_loop "from a scratch directory" and never asks for the set to be committed. So the missing set fits the plan. The defects are the "Added" wording and CLAUDE.md:62.
- README.md:82 reports a real one-off result (the reviewer's checked_ok saw 24/24). It only needs a "one-off" note.

(b) Holds. :56 gives the 8/8 to "the first description", which was never tuned, so the sentence says nothing about the shipped description. The current description also passed 24/24, so on either reading the held-out set can't tell the two apart. The verifier read the run_loop.py on this Mac correctly:
- :37-38 hold out int(12*0.4)=4 per class.
- :218 picks the best iteration by test score alone.
- Python's max keeps the first of a tie (my check printed 1).
So in the stock loop, an original scoring 8/8 would be best_description. The shipped description (55a5b2b, unchanged since) differs from the original. compatibility.md:52 says the loop was "adapted", so this fits the reviewer's "picked by hand" claim but doesn't prove it.

(c) Can't be checked here. The row's 5 matches the 998e0c8 message ("the 5 affected cases now pass") and the 5 cases that commit touched: 3 histories, the secret-redaction grader, and research through SKILL.md. But the SKILL.md:64 change also affects question-round cases such as coding-vague, so a sixth re-run is plausible. Nothing here settles the cost or the missing without-skill results.

(d) The facts hold:
- main's only commit is 4ba0a01, holding README.md. The contents API returns 404 for .claude-plugin/marketplace.json on main. The only other branch is the feature branch, so any GitHub install came from it.
- I re-ran both commands. Unpinned: "✘ Failed to add marketplace: Marketplace file not found…", exit 1. With #claude/gallant-thompson-eblqe0: "✔ Successfully added marketplace".
- But :15 says only "installed from this repository's marketplace on GitHub", which is true of the branch. What it leaves out: README.md:41's unpinned commands were never run, and 998e0c8 changed SKILL.md:64, :93 and :99 after the test (see finding 43).

Not already fixed: `git diff 34d9caa HEAD` is empty for compatibility.md and README.md. The CHANGELOG line only moved from :26 to :31.

Severity: "major" is arguable. These are accuracy problems in the test-status docs, which matter under the honesty rule, but no result was invented.

findings.title: The prior-art claim isn't what the cited release notes say, and time-sensitive pages have no checked-on date
findings.summary: README.md:91 credits Anthropic's release notes with retiring the 'Console prompt improver and generator'. The cited page never says 'improver'. It retires the legacy Workbench and the experimental generate, improve and templatize prompt APIs. The next sentence about other 'enhance prompt' buttons has no source, and install.md has no checked-on date. README.md:42 and install.md:59 give only the old toggle name; Anthropic now says it is called 'Create and edit files' in the updated Settings layout.

claims.claim: The cited release notes never mention a prompt improver.
claims.evidence: Release notes downloaded today as .md and HTML: 0 matches for 'improver'. The only related entries are relnotes.md:247-248 under '### July 17, 2026' and relnotes.md:197 under '### August 18, 2026' ('Workbench is now playground').

claims.claim: The notes announce the retirement of the legacy Workbench and of the experimental prompt-tools API endpoints.
claims.evidence: July 17, 2026: 'The legacy Workbench ... is being sunset with access ending on August 17, 2026' and 'The experimental prompt tools APIs for generating, improving, and templatizing prompts (/v1/experimental/generate_prompt, /v1/experimental/improve_prompt, and /v1/experimental/templatize_prompt) are being retired along with the Workbench on August 17, 2026.'

claims.claim: Implied by README.md:91: the Console UI's prompt improver and generator were retired.
claims.evidence: Checking needs a Console login. Indirect signs only: Anthropic's old docs pages .../prompt-engineering/prompt-improver and /prompt-generator now redirect to 'Prompting best practices'. Help Center 8606378 (modified 2026-10-19) says 'Workbench is now retired' but names neither tool. A web search found no Anthropic statement naming them. plan.md:40 records only 'Console prompt generate/improve endpoints'.

claims.claim: 'Most remaining enhance-prompt buttons ... rewrite silently' has no source.
claims.evidence: README.md:91 has no link. git grep finds no source in docs/sources.md or .claude/handoff/. Whether the claim is true wasn't checked: it generalises over many products.

claims.claim: The prior-art descriptions have no as-of date.
claims.evidence: README.md:89-97 has no date. Side check: all four descriptions still match their READMEs today. prompt-master README:86 says 'max 3 questions' and :91 'one clean copyable block'. claude-code-prompt-improver README:15 says 'asks 1-6 grounded questions only when the prompt is genuinely vague'. prompt-architect README:3 says '31 frameworks' and :101 has 'Quality Scoring System'. mattpocock/skills grilling SKILL.md:8 works in 'rounds' and :15 gives 'your recommended answer'.

claims.claim: docs/install.md has no checked-on date, unlike compatibility.md, sources.md and publishing.md.
claims.evidence: grep -E '20[0-9]{2}|checked|last updated|as of' docs/install.md finds nothing. compatibility.md:3 has 'Last updated: 2026-10-29'; sources.md:3 and publishing.md:3 have 'checked on 2026-10-29'. install.md:55 has a version only: 'tested here with Claude Code 2.1.312'.

claims.claim: The toggle is now called 'Create and edit files' in the updated Settings layout, and README and install.md give only the old name.
claims.evidence: Help Center 12512180 and 12111783 (both modified 2026-10-30): 'Code execution and file creation (called Create and edit files in the updated Settings layout)'. README.md:42 and install.md:59 use only the old name, as do compatibility.md:18 and plan.md:35.

claims.claim: Extra, not in the finding: install.md:59's owner and plan wording is out of date.
claims.evidence: install.md:59 says 'on Team and Enterprise plans an Owner enables it'. Help Center 12111783 says the feature 'is enabled by default for Team plan organizations' and 'for new Enterprise plan organizations', and owners can disable it. The skills article now says 'Skills are available for users on Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans'; install.md:59's plan sentence doesn't mention Ultra. I didn't check whether other Anthropic pages still disagree on plans.

findings.refutation: I asked whether the README is a fair paraphrase. The retired APIs were the API side of the Console's generate and improve tools, and the old docs pages now redirect, so the Console features are probably gone. But no Anthropic page I found says so, and the README attributes the claim to release notes that don't make it. sources.md:31 and plan.md:40 already word it accurately, so only the README drifted. The files are unchanged since 34d9caa, so nothing was fixed. The old toggle name is still on Anthropic's pages (and on mobile), so the docs are incomplete for the new layout rather than wrong. The toggle is on by default for most accounts, which lowers the impact. Severity stays minor.

audit.reasoning:
README.md, docs/install.md, docs/sources.md and docs/compatibility.md are unchanged since 34d9caa (`git diff --stat 34d9caa HEAD` on them is empty), so nothing was fixed.

Core defect holds. README.md:91 says the 'Console prompt improver and generator were retired in August 2026, according to Anthropic's release notes'. I fetched the notes today (overview.md, 136,891 bytes, and the HTML): 0 matches for 'improver'. The only related entries are July 17, 2026 (overview.md:247-248: the legacy Workbench is sunset and the experimental generate/improve/templatize prompt APIs are retired on Aug 17) and Aug 18 (overview.md:197: 'Workbench is now playground'). So the README credits the notes with a claim they don't make.

I tried to refute it by finding any Anthropic statement that the Console UI tools were retired. I found none:
- Help Center 8606378 (modified 2026-10-19) says 'Workbench is now retired' and never mentions generating or improving prompts.
- The docs pages prompt-improver, prompt-generator and prompting-tools (en, ja, pt-BR) now redirect to Prompting best practices.
- The API pages prompt-tools-generate and prompt-tools-improve redirect to the docs home.
- One page points the other way: Help Center 8114533 (modified 2026-03-16) still says 'You can use the prompt improver in the Claude Console'.

Anthropic's own pages conflict, and the README presents the retirement of the UI tools as a sourced fact. That breaks the repo's honesty rule.

The secondary claims hold too:
- The 'enhance prompt buttons ... rewrite silently' sentence has no source (git grep finds it only at README.md:91).
- install.md has no date (grep for a year, 'checked' or 'as of' finds nothing), while compatibility.md:3, sources.md:3 and publishing.md:3 are dated. This part is weak: install.md:3 already points readers to compatibility.md, which is dated.
- Help Center 12512180 and 12111783 (both modified 2026-10-30) say 'Code execution and file creation (called Create and edit files in the updated Settings layout)'. README.md:42, install.md:59, compatibility.md:18 and plan.md:35 give only the old name. That makes them incomplete, not wrong.

The four prior-art descriptions still match their sources:
- prompt-master README:86 'max 3 questions' and :91 'one clean copyable block'
- claude-code-prompt-improver README:15 'asks 1-6 grounded questions'
- prompt-architect README:3 '31 frameworks'
- mattpocock grilling SKILL.md:8 'rounds' and :15 'your recommended answer'

Severity: minor.

findings.summary: README.md:43's folder, ~/.agents/skills/, is right for every agent it names. Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode and Goose list it in their own docs, and Cline reads it in its shipped code. The defects are in install.md and sources.md. install.md:90-93 leaves ~/.agents/skills/ out for Copilot, Cline, OpenCode, Goose and Mistral Vibe and still calls Cursor unverified. OpenCode and Goose are marked verified with no source in sources.md. The installer's different folders, the reviewer's evidence, show only where `npx skills add` writes, so they don't make the README wrong.

findings.title: 'Mutation tests confirm each check' and 'tested automatically' overstate the test coverage
findings.summary: README.md:84 says mutation tests "confirm each check catches what it should", and docs/architecture.md:40 says the same. The tests assert 10 of validate.mjs's 53 err() sites, and none covers a size budget. universal/README.md:54 says the universal prompt is "tested automatically", but the test is a billed script run by hand that no workflow runs. Its only recorded result (compatibility.md:47) predates d63abbf's change to the universal prompt. The review's count of 47 checks is wrong (the real count is 53), but the conclusion holds.

claims.claim: README.md:84 says 'mutation tests that confirm each check catches what it should'
claims.evidence: README.md:84, quoted as stated.

claims.claim: docs/architecture.md:40 says 'each validator rule catches what it should'
claims.evidence: architecture.md:40, quoted as stated.

claims.claim: The validator has 47 error checks
claims.evidence: There are 53 err() call sites: 47 with template literals and 6 with plain strings. The reviewer's count matches the template-literal subset only. Loops expand some sites further.

claims.claim: The mutation suite has 11 tests
claims.evidence: 11 'rejects' tests in scripts/test/validate.test.mjs:71-102.

claims.claim: No test covers the size budgets that CONTRIBUTING highlights
claims.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:12 mentions 7,500 characters and :44 mentions 8,000. grep for skillBodyMaxChars, skillKeySections, universalCoreMaxChars or budget in scripts/test exits 1. validate.mjs:131-139 never fires in any test.

claims.claim: Nor the name and allowed-tools rules, media-target fields, eval-case structure or MCP manifest version sync
claims.evidence: validate.mjs:69-71, 81, 199-201 and 209-211 never fire in a test. Lines 182-192 fire only as side effects of the version-mismatch test, which asserts only metadata.version.

claims.claim: universal/README calls the test automatic, but it is a billed script run by hand that no workflow runs
claims.evidence: universal/README.md:54: "tested automatically with Claude". universal-test.mjs:5: "Real, billed model calls". grep of .github/ finds no universal-test. ci.yml:13's job is named "Skill, plugin and universal prompt" but only runs validate.

claims.claim: Its recorded outputs predate the latest change to the universal prompt
claims.evidence: 7fb1b1a recorded 36/36 at 15:05:12Z. d63abbf changed the universal prompt at 16:03:53Z. Nothing since records a re-run. The reviewer's 14:45 file time can't be checked here.
